confirmed.title: updateOrderSchema and updateOrderStatusSchema require body `id` that the frontend never sends → PUT /orders/:id and PATCH /orders/:id/status 400 on every call
confirmed.evidence: order.schema.ts:56-58 `updateOrderSchema = createOrderSchema.partial().extend({ id: z.string().uuid() })` and :61-65 `updateOrderStatusSchema = z.object({ id: z.string().uuid(), status, reason })`. Routes wire these via validateBody (order.routes.ts:39-45). The controller reads id from req.params only (order.controller.ts:703, 499). Frontend OrderForm.tsx:918-942 builds orderData WITHOUT id and calls `updateOrder(id, orderData)`; frontend type UpdateOrderStatusRequest = { status } only (order.types.ts:228-230).
confirmed.failureScenario: User edits any order in the UI and clicks Save → validateBody parses body, `id` missing → 400 'Invalid request data' every time; order editing (and any status PATCH from the typed client) is completely broken.
confirmed.fixSketch: Remove `id` from both body schemas (it belongs to params, already validated by idParamSchema); alternatively make it optional. Also drop unused `reason`/`status` extras or wire them through.

verdict.reasoning: updateOrderSchema (order.schema.ts:56-58) is createOrderSchema.partial().extend({ id: z.string().uuid() }) — extend runs after partial, so body `id` is REQUIRED; updateOrderStatusSchema (:61-65) likewise requires `id`. order.routes.ts:39 wires validateBody(updateOrderSchema) on PUT /:id and :40-45 wires validateBody(updateOrderStatusSchema) on PATCH /:id/status. validation.middleware.ts:25-45 does schema.parse(req.body) and returns 400 'Invalid request data' on any ZodError. The controller (order.controller.ts:703, 499) reads id from req.params only, so the body-id requirement protects nothing. OrderForm.tsx:918-942 builds orderData with no `id` key and calls updateOrder(id, orderData) → api.put(`/orders/${id}`, body-without-id) (order.service.ts:71-74); UpdateOrderRequest (order.types.ts:216-226) has no id field. Therefore every UI order edit fails Zod with field "id" Required → 400 before the handler runs. The status half is identically broken in the typed client (UpdateOrderStatusRequest = { status } only, order.types.ts:228-230) but grep shows no frontend caller of updateOrderStatus or /orders/:id/status, so that portion is latent rather than live.
verdict.failureScenario: Open any existing order in the UI (OrderForm in edit mode), change any field, click Save. Frontend issues PUT /orders/{uuid} with body { customerId, orderDate, expectedDeliveryDate, priority, totalQuantity, paymentTerms?, shippingAddress?, remarks?, items? } — no `id`. validateBody(updateOrderSchema) parses, Zod reports { field: "id", message: "Required" }, middleware returns 400 { error: 'Validation Error', message: 'Invalid request data' }. OrderForm's catch shows 'Invalid request data'; the update never reaches the controller. This happens on 100% of edits. Equivalent 400 awaits any future caller of the typed updateOrderStatus client (body = { status } only), though no page currently invokes it.

confirmed.title: updateOrder replaces order items via sequential global-prisma deletes/creates with no transaction; totals written in a separate later update
confirmed.evidence: order.controller.ts:786-801: `prisma.order_item_breakup.deleteMany(...)`, then `prisma.order_items.deleteMany(...)`, then a for-loop of `prisma.order_items.create(...)`, then per-work-order breakup deletes/creates (803-841), and only at :847 the order header (totalQuantity/totalAmount) is updated — all on the global client, no $transaction.
confirmed.failureScenario: Item replacement where the 2nd create fails (e.g., duplicate (colorId,sizeId) breakup → P2002, or bad styleId → P2003): breakups and items are already deleted, order is left with 0/partial items, header totals still show the old values, and work_orders.orderItemId has been set NULL by the delete — silent corruption with no rollback.
confirmed.fixSketch: Wrap the whole item-replacement + work-order sync + header-total update in one prisma.$transaction(tx => ...) and use tx.* throughout.

verdict.reasoning: Read backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:702-882 (updateOrder). Every claimed element is present: (1) prisma.order_item_breakup.deleteMany (:786) and prisma.order_items.deleteMany (:789) run on the GLOBAL prisma client; (2) new items are created one-by-one in a for-loop of prisma.order_items.create (:794-801); (3) pending work-order sync does work_order_breakup.deleteMany + work_orders.update + per-row creates (:803-841), also global client; (4) the order header totals (totalQuantity/totalAmount computed at :782-783) are only written by the final prisma.orders.update at :847. There is no prisma.$transaction anywhere in the function and no compensating rollback/catch — errors propagate to the error middleware after earlier writes have already committed. Schema confirms both concrete failure triggers: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:1080 has @@unique([orderItemId, colorId, sizeId]) on order_item_breakup, so a payload where one item's breakup array contains two rows with the same non-null colorId + sizeId makes the nested create throw P2002; order_items.styleId is a required FK to styles, so a bad styleId throws P2003. And schema.prisma:3031/3078 shows work_orders.orderItemId is an optional relation with NO explicit onDelete, so Prisma's default for optional relations (SetNull) applies — the order_items.deleteMany at :789 silently nulls orderItemId on all work orders referencing the old items; if the subsequent create/sync fails, that link is never restored. The pre-check at :731-746 only blocks orders with approved BOMs/active MRP; it does nothing to make the replacement atomic. Even the success path has a visible-inconsistency window (order with zero items, then items but stale header totals) for concurrent readers.
verdict.failureScenario: PUT /api/orders/:id with items = [{ styleId: valid, unitPrice: 100, breakup: [{colorId: 'C1', sizeId: 'S1', quantity: 5}, {colorId: 'C1', sizeId: 'S1', quantity: 3}] }]. Sequence: deleteMany(order_item_breakup) commits, deleteMany(order_items) commits (SetNull-ing work_orders.orderItemId on any pending WOs), then order_items.create with nested breakup create throws P2002 on @@unique([orderItemId, colorId, sizeId]). Request returns an error, but the order is now permanently left with 0 items, header totalQuantity/totalAmount still showing the old values (the :847 update never ran), and work orders detached from their order items — silent corruption with no rollback. Same outcome via P2003 with a stale/deleted styleId, or on any transient DB error mid-loop with multi-item payloads (partial items). Note: duplicate breakup rows with NULL colorId do NOT trigger P2002 (Postgres NULLs don't collide in unique indexes), but the non-null duplicate case and FK case are real and user-reachable since no Zod/controller check deduplicates breakup rows.

confirmed.title: Order status route bypasses the state machine: service.updateStatus validates transitions, but the wired controller does a raw update allowing any transition
confirmed.evidence: order.service.ts:446-482 `updateStatus` calls `validateTransition('order', existing.status, status, userRole)` — but order.routes.ts:40-45 wires PATCH /:id/status to controller `updateOrderStatus` (order.controller.ts:498-523) which does `prisma.orders.update({ data: { status } })` with no transition check. Similarly `deleteOrder` (order.controller.ts:888-908) cancels without any status guard.
confirmed.failureScenario: PATCH /orders/:id/status with status=PENDING on a DISPATCHED order (or CANCELLED→COMPLETED) succeeds; DELETE /orders/:id cancels a DISPATCHED/COMPLETED order, releasing lace allocations and cancelling work orders for goods already shipped.
confirmed.fixSketch: Make the controller delegate to orderService.updateStatus (which runs validateTransition) and add a status guard to deleteOrder/cancelOrder; delete the dead duplicate path.

verdict.reasoning: order.routes.ts:40-45 wires PATCH /:id/status to the controller's updateOrderStatus with only validateBody(updateOrderStatusSchema); that schema (order.schema.ts:61-65) validates status is one of the enum values ['PENDING','IN_PRODUCTION','COMPLETED','DISPATCHED','CANCELLED'] but contains no transition logic. The controller (order.controller.ts:498-539) reads previousStatus but uses it ONLY to decide whether to auto-clone CAD rows on entry to IN_PRODUCTION — it then executes a raw prisma.orders.update({ where:{id}, data:{status} }) with no call to validateTransition. The guarded path exists at order.service.ts:446-482 (updateStatus calls validateTransition('order', existing.status, status, userRole) and throws ValidationError on invalid transitions), but grep shows orderService.updateStatus is invoked nowhere in backend/src — it is dead code; the state machine is fully bypassed. Similarly, deleteOrder (order.controller.ts:888-909) checks only that the order exists, then calls orderService.cancelOrder (order.service.ts:488+), which has no status guard at all: it unconditionally sets status=CANCELLED, cancels PENDING/IN_PRODUCTION work orders, deactivates BOMs, and releases non-terminal lace allocations back to stock — regardless of the order being DISPATCHED or COMPLETED. Only the separate POST /:id/cancel route (cancelOrderWithOptions) has even a partial guard (rejects only if already CANCELLED). Minor caveat found: updateOrderStatusSchema also requires id (uuid) in the request BODY, so the repro payload must include {id, status}; a bare {status} gets a 400 — a small extra contract quirk that does not block the bypass. Partial mitigation on delete: lace allocations already CONSUMED/RETURNED/TRANSFERRED are skipped (order.service.ts:544), so fully-consumed lace is not double-released, but reserved/in-use allocations for shipped goods are.
verdict.failureScenario: Repro 1 (backward transition): for a DISPATCHED order, PATCH /api/orders/:id/status with body {"id":"<same uuid>","status":"PENDING"} (auth token required) — validateBody passes (PENDING is in the enum), controller runs prisma.orders.update directly, order regresses to PENDING with no error. CANCELLED→COMPLETED succeeds identically. Bonus effect: transitioning any order back into IN_PRODUCTION re-runs the COSTING→RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD clone block (order.controller.ts:548+). Repro 2 (cancel shipped order): DELETE /api/orders/:id on a DISPATCHED/COMPLETED order — deleteOrder has no status check and orderService.cancelOrder none either, so the shipped order becomes CANCELLED, its remaining work orders are cancelled, BOMs deactivated, and RESERVED/IN_USE lace allocations are released back to stock for goods already dispatched (inflating lace stock). Only allocations already in CONSUMED/RETURNED/TRANSFERRED state are spared.

confirmed.title: RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD clone guard checks the wrong row → duplicate CAD clones when a style appears in multiple orders
confirmed.evidence: order.controller.ts:557-577: `findFirst({ where: { purpose: 'RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION', styleFabric: {...styleId} } })` returns ANY raw-mat CAD for the style, then skips only if `existingRawMat.clonedFromOrderId === id`. With no state machine (orders-3), status can be toggled off/on IN_PRODUCTION repeatedly.
confirmed.failureScenario: Order A (style S) confirmed → clones CADs. Order B (style S) confirmed → clones again. Order A toggled back to PENDING and re-confirmed → findFirst may return B's row, guard fails (clonedFromOrderId !== A), A clones a THIRD set → duplicate RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD rows inflate downstream material calculations. Loop also runs off-transaction with per-item catch-swallow (:669-681).
confirmed.fixSketch: Query `findFirst({ where: { purpose: 'RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION', clonedFromOrderId: id, styleFabric: {...} } })` — i.e. guard on THIS order's clones — and wrap the clone loop in a transaction.

verdict.reasoning: order.controller.ts:557-566 queries findFirst for ANY RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD matching the style (no clonedFromOrderId filter, no orderBy → arbitrary row), and line 569 skips only if that one arbitrary row has clonedFromOrderId === id. updateOrderStatus has no transition validation (updateOrderStatusSchema at order.schema.ts:61-65 is just an enum), so IN_PRODUCTION can be left and re-entered, re-firing the trigger (guard at line 548 only checks previousStatus !== 'IN_PRODUCTION'). The schema-level unique constraint that could have blocked duplicates — @@unique([costingStyleId, componentName, styleFabricId, cutableWidth, purpose, approvalStatus]) at schema.prisma:4343 — is inert here because the clone create (lines 620-656) leaves costingStyleId and componentName NULL, and Postgres treats NULLs as distinct in unique indexes. The clone loop also runs after the orders.update commit on the global prisma client with no $transaction, and the per-item catch at lines 669-681 swallows errors (status update stands, partial clone sets persist). Minor refinement: with a single order the guard accidentally holds (all rows belong to that order, so findFirst must return a matching row); the failure requires the style to appear in >=2 confirmed orders plus one re-confirm — a routine scenario since styles recur across orders.
verdict.failureScenario: Style S has approved COSTING CADs. (1) Order A containing S: PATCH /api/orders/A/status {status:'IN_PRODUCTION'} → no existing raw-mat CAD → clones set #1 with clonedFromOrderId=A. (2) Order B containing S: same PATCH → findFirst returns A's row, A !== B → clones set #2 for B. (3) Order A: PATCH status PENDING (allowed — no state machine), then PATCH IN_PRODUCTION again → trigger re-fires; findFirst without orderBy can return one of B's rows → guard (clonedFromOrderId === A) fails → a THIRD full set (including cloned sizeBreakdowns) is created with clonedFromOrderId=A. Order A now has two complete RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD sets; any downstream material-requirement/BOM sum over raw-mat CADs for the order double-counts fabric requirements → over-procurement. The NULL costingStyleId/componentName make the @@unique constraint a no-op, and errors mid-loop are swallowed off-transaction, additionally allowing partial sets.

confirmed.title: Editing order items cascade-deletes order_item_costing snapshots (variance baseline) and never recreates them
confirmed.evidence: updateOrder deletes all order_items and recreates them with new randomUUID ids (order.controller.ts:789-801). order_item_costing has `orderItemId @unique` with `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:4416, 4443), so the cost-sheet snapshot created at order time (order.controller.ts:294-312, including costingSnapshot JSON, estimatedCostPerPiece, originalCostSheetVersion) is destroyed; the update path contains no snapshot re-creation.
confirmed.failureScenario: User edits an order to fix a size quantity → all items replaced → every order_item_costing row (the frozen pricing/variance baseline) is silently deleted; later variance tracking and costing comparison return null; selectedCadId choices on items are also lost.
confirmed.fixSketch: Update items in place (upsert by styleId) instead of delete-and-recreate, or carry order_item_costing (and selectedCadId) over to the replacement items inside the same transaction.

verdict.reasoning: PUT /api/orders/:id routes to controller updateOrder (order.routes.ts:39). When items are provided, updateOrder deletes all order_items (order.controller.ts:789-791) and recreates them with new randomUUID ids (763, 794-801). schema.prisma:4416/4443 gives order_item_costing a unique orderItemId FK with onDelete: Cascade, so the DB cascade-deletes every costing snapshot row. The entire remainder of the handler (through res.json at 878) contains no order_item_costing recreation; grep shows the only creation sites are createOrder (order.controller.ts:294) and a manual recalc upsert (orderCosting.service.ts:198) which cannot restore the original baseline — it would snapshot the CURRENT cost-sheet version, not the order-time frozen one (originalCostSheetVersion, snapshotCreatedAt, costingSnapshot). The pre-replace guard (731-746) only checks approved BOMs and material requirements, not costing. Downstream, workOrder.service.ts:1082-1118 (CMT actuals) finds no costing row and skips variance with only a warn; orderProductionStatus.service.ts:392/699 degrade similarly. selectedCadId/cadMeters on the costing row are also lost and the recreated items carry no CAD selection. order.service.ts:765's explicit costing delete is the hard-delete path, not update — it does not rescue this flow.
verdict.failureScenario: Create an order for a style with an approved cost sheet — createOrder writes an order_item_costing snapshot (frozen pricing/variance baseline). Later, edit the order via PUT /api/orders/:id changing one size quantity in the items array (no approved BOM yet, so the guard passes). All order_items are deleted and recreated with new ids; the DB cascade silently deletes every order_item_costing row. Nothing recreates them. Subsequently, recording CMT actuals logs "No order_item_costing record for order item ..." and cost variance stays null forever; the order-time cost baseline (costingSnapshot, originalCostSheetVersion, estimatedCostPerPiece) and any selectedCadId are unrecoverable.

confirmed.title: createQuotationSchema strips placeOfSupplyId/includeTaxEstimate/taxRate that the service reads and the frontend sends → quotation GST estimation silently never runs
confirmed.evidence: createQuotationSchema (quotation.schema.ts:43-58) has no placeOfSupplyId/includeTaxEstimate/taxRate fields; route POST / uses validateBody(createQuotationSchema) (quotation.routes.ts:67-72) which replaces req.body with the parsed (stripped) object; quotation.service.ts:220-247 branches on `data.includeTaxEstimate` to compute estimatedCGST/SGST/IGST/totalWithTax; frontend CreateQuotationRequest includes all three fields (frontend/src/types/quotation.types.ts:139-141). No route exposes service estimateGST() as a fallback.
confirmed.failureScenario: User creates a quotation with 'include tax estimate' checked → fields silently stripped → quotation saved with estimatedCGST/SGST/IGST = 0 and totalWithTax null; customer-facing quote omits tax with no error anywhere.
confirmed.fixSketch: Add `placeOfSupplyId: z.string().uuid().optional(), includeTaxEstimate: z.boolean().optional(), taxRate: z.number().optional()` to createQuotationSchema (and updateQuotationSchema), and/or register a route for estimateGST.

verdict.reasoning: Traced end-to-end: validateBody (validation.middleware.ts:28) replaces req.body with schema.parse output; createQuotationSchema (backend/src/schemas/quotation.schema.ts:43-58) is a default-mode z.object lacking includeTaxEstimate/placeOfSupplyId/taxRate, so Zod strips them. Controller (quotation.controller.ts:20) passes the stripped body to quotationService.create, which branches on data.includeTaxEstimate at quotation.service.ts:220 — that branch and the entire GST-estimation path (lines 214-335, including gstService.calculateGST, per-item calculateLineItemGST, and the estimatedCGST/SGST/IGST/totalWithTax/taxRate writes at 328-335) can never execute via POST /api/quotations. service.estimateGST() (line 640) is exposed by no route (grep of backend/src). One correction to the finding: the frontend TYPE CreateQuotationRequest declares the three fields (frontend/src/types/quotation.types.ts:139-141), but QuotationForm.tsx handleSubmit (lines 160-174) never sends them and no 'include tax estimate' checkbox exists in any component — so no shipped UI flow triggers the silent loss today; the fields are a lying contract and the server-side feature is dead code.
verdict.failureScenario: Any API client following the published CreateQuotationRequest type — e.g. POST /api/quotations with {customerId, validUntil, items:[...], includeTaxEstimate: true, placeOfSupplyId: "<state-uuid>", taxRate: 12} — gets 201 Created, but validateBody strips all three tax fields before the service runs, so the quotation is saved with estimatedCGST/SGST/IGST/totalWithTax/taxRate all null and no per-item GST, with no error or warning anywhere. Via the current UI this cannot happen because QuotationForm.tsx never sends those fields (no tax-estimate checkbox exists); instead the entire quotation GST-estimation feature (service lines 214-335 plus the un-routed estimateGST()) is unreachable dead code, and the frontend type invites a future developer to wire a checkbox that will silently do nothing.

confirmed.title: updateQuotation deletes all quotation_items on the global client before the header update — a failed update leaves the quotation permanently itemless
confirmed.evidence: quotation.service.ts:471-473 `await this.prisma.quotation_items.deleteMany({ where: { quotationId: id } })` runs standalone; the recreate happens only via nested create inside `this.model.update(...)` at :492-496. No $transaction spans the two.
confirmed.failureScenario: Items deleteMany succeeds, then model.update throws (DB connection blip, constraint on a nested item like a since-deleted styleId FK) → quotation keeps its old totalAmount but has ZERO line items; document prints empty; no error recovery path.
confirmed.fixSketch: Wrap deleteMany + update in `this.prisma.$transaction`, or use nested `quotation_items: { deleteMany: {}, create: [...] }` inside the single update call (atomic).

verdict.reasoning: quotation.service.ts:471-473 runs `this.prisma.quotation_items.deleteMany({ where: { quotationId: id } })` as a standalone top-level call on the global Prisma client (base.service.ts line 62: `protected readonly prisma = prisma` from ../config/database; no $transaction exists in the base or in updateQuotation). Prisma commits each top-level call in its own implicit transaction, so the delete is durable before `this.model.update` at :492-496 even starts. The replacement items exist only as a nested `create` inside that second, independent update call. The nested create sets `styleId: item.styleId` (:478) with no existence check, so a stale styleId yields a P2003 FK violation after the delete committed; the catch at :500-503 only logs and rethrows — no compensation. The recalculated totalAmount (:468) is part of the failed update payload, so the header keeps its OLD total while owning zero items. Minor mitigation vs the claim: the :459 guard limits exposure to DRAFT/SENT quotations, and a subsequent successful re-edit would repopulate items, so 'permanently' overstates it slightly — but no automatic recovery exists and nothing flags the inconsistent state.
verdict.failureScenario: PUT /quotations/:id on a DRAFT or SENT quotation with an items array containing one styleId that was deleted (or any DB error mid-call: connection blip, timeout). Step 1: deleteMany commits, all quotation_items rows for the quotation are gone. Step 2: model.update throws P2003 on the nested item create (or fails on the connection error) and rolls back only itself. Result: 500 returned to the client; the quotation now has zero line items but retains its previous non-zero totalAmount; the printed/emailed quotation document renders a total with no lines. Recovery only happens if a user later re-submits a fully valid edit.

confirmed.title: GRN item Zod schema strips receivedAsReadyFabric/actualRatePerUnit/updateFutureSourcing — source-mismatch override silently never fires
confirmed.evidence: grnItemSchema (grn.schema.ts:39-53) has no receivedAsReadyFabric, actualRatePerUnit, or updateFutureSourcing fields and is NOT .passthrough() (only the top-level createGRNSchema is). validateBody (validation.middleware.ts:28) replaces req.body with the stripped parse. grn.service.ts:177-179 persists item.receivedAsReadyFabric/actualRatePerUnit/updateFutureSourcing, and approveGRN branches on them at grn.service.ts:987 (overrideItems filter). Frontend sends the fields (frontend/src/pages/GRNForm.tsx).
confirmed.failureScenario: User receives a GREIGE PO 'as ready fabric' with an actual rate and ticks 'update future sourcing'. Zod strips all three flags from every item → GRN stores receivedAsReadyFabric=false → approval books the receipt into greige_stock at the greige PO rate instead of fabric_stock at the actual rate; downstream processing POs are not cancelled and cost-sheet sourcing is never updated. No error anywhere.
confirmed.fixSketch: Add the three override fields (and thanCount if intended) to grnItemSchema so they survive validateBody stripping.

verdict.reasoning: The full chain checks out in code. (1) Route: backend/src/routes/grn.routes.ts:84 applies validateBody(createGRNSchema) to POST /. (2) Middleware: backend/src/middleware/validation.middleware.ts:28 does req.body = schema.parse(req.body), so the controller only ever sees the parsed output. (3) Schema: backend/src/schemas/grn.schema.ts:39-53 — grnItemSchema is a plain z.object with NO receivedAsReadyFabric, actualRatePerUnit, or updateFutureSourcing fields and no .passthrough(); Zod's default object mode strips unknown keys. The .passthrough() at createGRNSchema (line 87) applies only to the TOP-LEVEL object — nested array element schemas still strip their own unknown keys, so the three per-item flags are removed from every item. (4) Controller: grn.controller.ts:119-120 takes req.body as CreateGRNDTO (a hand-written DTO, not z.infer, so TypeScript never flags the mismatch) and passes it to the service. (5) Service: grn.service.ts:177-179 writes receivedAsReadyFabric: item.receivedAsReadyFabric || false, actualRatePerUnit: item.actualRatePerUnit || null, updateFutureSourcing: item.updateFutureSourcing || false — after stripping, all three are undefined, so every GRN item is persisted with false/null/false. (6) Approval: grn.service.ts:987-988 filters overrideItems by item.receivedAsReadyFabric — always empty, so the override branch (actual-rate booking at :1050-1052, updateFutureSourcing handling at :1117) is dead code in the live request path. (7) Frontend really sends the fields: GRNForm.tsx:436-439 sets receivedAsReadyFabric/actualRatePerUnit/updateFutureSourcing on GREIGE items when the checkbox is ticked, and the UI exposes the toggle at :772-810. No compensating path exists — there is no later PATCH that re-supplies the flags.
verdict.failureScenario: User creates a GRN against a GREIGE PO, ticks "received as ready fabric" on an item, enters an actual rate different from the PO rate, and selects "update future sourcing" (permanent). Frontend POSTs items containing receivedAsReadyFabric:true, actualRatePerUnit:<number>, updateFutureSourcing:true. grnItemSchema strips all three keys; the GRN row is stored with receivedAsReadyFabric=false, actualRatePerUnit=null, updateFutureSourcing=false. On approval, overrideItems (grn.service.ts:987) is empty, so the item is processed as a normal greige receipt: stock is booked into greige_stock at the greige PO rate instead of fabric_stock at the actual rate, downstream processing-PO cancellation never runs, and cost-sheet/future sourcing is never updated. HTTP 200/201 throughout — no error surfaces anywhere; the user's checkbox is silently ignored.

confirmed.title: POST/PUT /api/procurement validated by TWO disagreeing schemas — endpoint cannot succeed with either documented shape
confirmed.evidence: Route: validateBody(createProcurementSchema) (fabric-procurement.routes.ts:36) requires {supplierId, items[]} (fabricProcurement.schema.ts:46-54). Controller then re-parses with a LOCAL CreateProcurementSchema (controller lines 39-65, .parse at 197) requiring a flat {procurementType, quantityPurchased, width, ratePerUnit, totalCost}. For PUT, route updateProcurementSchema status enum is ['PLANNED','PO_CREATED','ORDERED','PARTIAL_RECEIVED','RECEIVED','CANCELLED'] while controller UpdateProcurementSchema enum is ['ORDERED','CONFIRMED','IN_TRANSIT','RECEIVED','PROCESSING','COMPLETED','CANCELLED']; controller schema also strips route-documented fields (invoiceNumber, supplierId, items) via ...validatedData spread at line 258.
confirmed.failureScenario: A client sending the flat controller shape gets 400 from the route ('items required'); a client sending the route's header+items shape gets a ZodError from the controller ('procurementType required'). Updating status to 'IN_TRANSIT' → 400 at route; to 'PARTIAL_RECEIVED' → controller rejects. Setting invoiceNumber on update is silently dropped.
confirmed.fixSketch: Delete the controller-local schemas and consume the typed body validated by the single route schema; align the status enum with the Prisma enum.

verdict.reasoning: Route POST / uses validateBody(createProcurementSchema) (fabric-procurement.routes.ts:36) requiring {supplierId, items[] min 1} (fabricProcurement.schema.ts:46-54, .passthrough()); the controller then re-parses req.body at fabric-procurement.controller.ts:197 with a local CreateProcurementSchema (lines 39-65) requiring flat procurementType/quantityPurchased/width/ratePerUnit/totalCost — the shape that actually matches the flat fabric_procurement Prisma model (schema.prisma:4504-4530, no items relation). Neither documented shape passes both validators; the sole passable shape is an undocumented union (route schema is passthrough), and even then the controller's default-strip schema discards items[] so line items are silently never persisted. PUT: route status enum is [PLANNED, PO_CREATED, ORDERED, PARTIAL_RECEIVED, RECEIVED, CANCELLED] (schema lines 14-21) vs controller enum [ORDERED, CONFIRMED, IN_TRANSIT, RECEIVED, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, CANCELLED] (controller line 68) — intersection is only {ORDERED, RECEIVED, CANCELLED}, and the DB status is a plain String defaulting to 'ORDERED' with deleteProcurement (line 426) expecting 'CONFIRMED', a value PUT can never set. invoiceNumber/invoiceDate are allowed by the route update schema (lines 70-71) and exist as Prisma columns (schema.prisma:4529-4530) but are stripped by the non-passthrough controller UpdateProcurementSchema before the ...validatedData spread at line 258 — 200 response, field never written. Controller ZodErrors surface as 400 via error.middleware.ts:141-143, so both failure paths return 400s with contradictory messages. Mitigating fact found during verification: grep of frontend/src shows zero callers of POST/PUT /api/procurement (no createProcurement/updateProcurement/procurementType usage); the UI drives procurement through the separate purchase-orders + GRN flow, so only external API/script consumers hit this dead contract.
verdict.failureScenario: 1) POST /api/procurement with the controller's flat shape {procurementType:'GREIGE', supplierId, greigeId, quantityPurchased:100, width:60, ratePerUnit:50, totalCost:5000} → 400 from route validateBody: 'At least one item is required'. 2) POST with the route's documented shape {supplierId, items:[{greigeId, quantity:100}]} → passes route, then CreateProcurementSchema.parse at controller line 197 throws ZodError (procurementType/quantityPurchased/width/ratePerUnit/totalCost required) → 400. Endpoint is unusable with either documented contract; only sending BOTH shapes merged succeeds, and then items[] is silently dropped. 3) PUT /:id {status:'IN_TRANSIT'} → 400 at route (not in route enum); {status:'PARTIAL_RECEIVED'} → passes route, 400 at controller (not in controller enum). 4) PUT /:id {invoiceNumber:'INV-123'} → 200 'Procurement updated successfully' but invoiceNumber is stripped by the controller schema and never written to the existing invoiceNumber column.

confirmed.title: receiveChallan credits general-material stock via createStockIn on the GLOBAL client inside the receive transaction
confirmed.evidence: Inside prisma.$transaction (challan.service.ts:565), line 695 calls stockMovementService.createStockIn({...}) with NO tx argument. createStockIn (stockMovement.service.ts:204-205) does not accept a tx and opens its OWN prisma.$transaction on the global client. Contrast issueChallan line 410-424, which passes the outer tx to createStockOut precisely to avoid this (comment cites F4).
confirmed.failureScenario: During challan receive, material stock-in commits on a second connection; if the subsequent challans.update (line 815) or a later item's processing fails, the outer tx rolls back but the stock_movements + stock_levels credit survives → phantom stock with no RECEIVED challan behind it. Also risks pool exhaustion/deadlock (nested tx waiting on outer tx's locks).
confirmed.fixSketch: Give createStockIn an optional outerTx parameter (same pattern as createStockOut) and pass the receive transaction's tx.

verdict.reasoning: receiveChallan (challan.service.ts:565) runs in prisma.$transaction, and at line 695 calls stockMovementService.createStockIn with no tx. createStockIn (stockMovement.service.ts:204) has no tx parameter at all — it unconditionally opens its OWN prisma.$transaction on the global client and commits stock_movements, stock_transactions, stock_levels (increaseStockInTx), and specialized-stock rows (routeToSpecializedStock) independently of the outer challan transaction. The try/catch at challan.service.ts:706-710 re-throws, so it only protects one direction (inner failure aborts outer); it cannot undo an already-committed inner tx when a LATER outer-tx step fails. The asymmetry is proven by the codebase itself: createStockOut (stockMovement.service.ts:405) was retrofitted with an outerTx? parameter and issueChallan passes tx at challan.service.ts:423-424 with a comment citing F4 — the identical fix was never applied to createStockIn/receiveChallan.
verdict.failureScenario: INWARD challan (no fabricProcessingId) with two general-material items: item 1's createStockIn commits on its own connection (stock_movements + stock_levels + specialized stock credited); item 2's createStockIn throws (missing stock_level, routing failure, DB error) → re-thrown at line 709 → outer tx rolls back challan_items.receivedQty and the challans.update (line 815), leaving the challan IN_TRANSIT — but item 1's stock credit survives: phantom stock with no RECEIVED challan. Retrying the receive credits item 1 AGAIN (double stock). Same one-way failure with a single item if any later in-tx write fails (material_requirements update line 716, service-requirement update lines 723-737, or the final challans.update). Secondary: each createStockIn holds a second pool connection while the outer interactive tx holds its own, risking pool exhaustion under concurrent receives.

confirmed.title: receiveChallan has no status guard and re-credits the FULL receivedQty on every call — double stock credit
confirmed.evidence: receiveChallan (challan.service.ts:564-833) never checks challan status (no guard that it is ISSUED/IN_TRANSIT and not already RECEIVED). Item receivedQty is set by assignment (line 577), but the INWARD credit loop increments stock by the full receivedQty per call: fabric_stock quantityAvailable:{increment:receivedQty} (line 638), lace_stock (line 662), plus syncStockLevelQuantity(+receivedQty) (649/682) and createStockIn for materials (695).
confirmed.failureScenario: Partial receive of 50/100 → stock +50, status PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. User completes the receipt entering total 100 → item receivedQty overwritten to 100 but stock incremented by another 100 → 150 credited for 100 received. Calling receive again on a RECEIVED challan doubles it again. stock_levels and lot tables both drift upward.
confirmed.fixSketch: Guard on status (reject if RECEIVED/CANCELLED) and credit only the DELTA (newReceivedQty − previous receivedQty) per item.

verdict.reasoning: receiveChallan (backend/src/services/challan.service.ts:564-833) fetches the challan selecting only { challanType, fabricProcessingId, orderId } — status is never read, and neither the route (challan.routes.ts:37, only validateParams) nor the controller (challan.controller.ts:91-103, pass-through) guards against re-receiving. Item receivedQty is written by ASSIGNMENT (line 577), but every stock credit uses the full value as a DELTA: fabric_stock quantityAvailable { increment: receivedQty } (638), lace_stock (662), syncStockLevelQuantity(+receivedQty) (649/682), stockMovementService.createStockIn (695), and the fabric-processing path creates a NEW fabric_stock row via fabricStockService.createStyleStock per call (786). Worse than the finding states: the credit loop iterates over allItems (line 619) — every item on the challan with a non-null receivedQty — not just input.items, so any subsequent receive call re-credits ALL previously-received items at their full stored quantity, even items untouched by the current request. Side effects also repeat: material_requirements flipped to FULFILLED_STOCK (716), duplicate lace_stock_transaction audit rows (668), duplicate style stock rows. The $transaction only provides atomicity, not idempotency.
verdict.failureScenario: Repro 1 (single item, two-step receive): challan item qty 100; call PUT /challans/:id/receive with receivedQty 50 → stock +50, status PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. User completes receipt entering cumulative 100 → item overwritten to 100 but stock incremented by another 100 → 150 credited for 100 goods (entering the delta 50 instead still double-credits: 100 credited, item shows 50). Repro 2 (multi-item): call 1 receives item A (50) → +50; call 2 receives only item B (30) → +30 for B AND another +50 for A because the credit loop runs over allItems. Repro 3: re-submitting receive on a RECEIVED challan doubles every credit again and, on the processing path, creates duplicate fabric_stock rows. stock_levels, fabric_stock/lace_stock, and lot tables all drift upward.

confirmed.title: createGRN PROCESSING branch runs AFTER the GRN commit on the global client, and throws user-facing errors after the receipt is already booked
confirmed.evidence: GRN + purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity increments commit in the tx at lines 113-224. Then the PROCESSING block (lines 227-340) runs on global prisma: it THROWS 'already been received' (line 239) or 'Cannot receive. Job status is …' (line 241) — re-thrown at 330-337 — after the GRN exists; fabric_master update (263), createChallan (275, failure swallowed at 298-300), and job_work_orders update (303) are three separate non-atomic writes.
confirmed.failureScenario: Second GRN against a PROCESSING PO whose job was already received: GRN row created and PO item receivedQuantity incremented, then the API returns the 'already been received' error → user retries → a third GRN and another increment; PO flips to RECEIVED with phantom receipts. Separately, a crash between the job update and challan creation leaves a RECEIVED job with no inward challan (only logged).
confirmed.fixSketch: Validate the job-work-order state BEFORE the GRN transaction, and move the job/challan/fabric writes into the same tx (or a compensating saga); do not swallow the inward-challan failure.

verdict.reasoning: backend/src/services/grn.service.ts: the $transaction (lines 113-224) creates the GRN, grn_items/details, and increments purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity, then commits. The PROCESSING branch (227-340) runs afterwards on the global singleton client (imported line 22; used at 229, 263, 303) plus createChallan (275) which is an external service — none of it shares a tx with the GRN. The catch at 329-337 explicitly re-throws the two user-facing errors thrown at 239 ('already been received') and 241 ('Cannot receive. Job status is …'), and grn.controller.ts:148 does no compensation, so the API returns an error while the committed GRN and PO increments persist; the throw also skips updateReceivingStatus (line 343), so PO status is never recomputed on that path. The sub-writes are three separate non-atomic operations in order fabric_master.update (263) → createChallan (275, failure swallowed at 298-300 leaving inwardChallanId null) → job_work_orders.update (303, sets status RECEIVED). Guards I looked for and did not find: no tx around the PROCESSING block, no GRN cleanup on error, no unique/idempotency constraint preventing a second GRN for the same job.
verdict.failureScenario: Repro (no external module needed): 1) Create GRN #1 for a PROCESSING PO with processingData, receiving a partial qty — job_work_orders gets receivedDate + status RECEIVED; updateReceivingStatus leaves the PO PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, which is in receivableStatuses (lines 61-65). 2) Create GRN #2 (double-submit or user retry): status check at 67 passes, tolerance check at 84 passes (cumulative < ordered×1.10), the tx commits GRN #2 and increments receivedQuantity again, then line 238 sees receivedDate → throws 'already been received' at 239, re-thrown at 336 → API returns an error, but the phantom GRN row and the increment persist. 3) User retries → GRN #3, another increment, until the 10% tolerance cap finally blocks — leaving multiple phantom GRNs and receivedQuantity ≈ 2-3× actual. Same mechanism with more headroom when the job was received via the Printing/Dyeing module while the PO is still SENT/ACKNOWLEDGED. Separately: a createChallan failure is swallowed (298-300) → job marked RECEIVED with inwardChallanId null; a crash between line 263 and 303 leaves fabric_master updated but the job stuck AT_MILL with a booked GRN.

confirmed.title: updateReceivedQuantity credits the FULL accepted qty to EVERY requirement_po_link of a PO item instead of allocating it
confirmed.evidence: mrp.service.ts:2418-2447 — for each link of purchaseOrderItemId: newReceived = Number(link.receivedQuantity) + receivedQuantity (the whole GRN accepted qty), and marks the requirement RECEIVED when newReceived >= allocatedQuantity. Yet PO generation explicitly allocates one PO item across MULTIPLE requirements proportionally (requirement_po_links.allocatedQuantity, mrp.service.ts:2296-2311).
confirmed.failureScenario: One consolidated PO item of 100m covers requirement A (allocated 60) and B (allocated 40). GRN approves 40m → BOTH links get receivedQuantity=40; B (40>=40) flips to RECEIVED even though its physical share may be zero, and total link receivedQuantity (80) is double the real receipt (40). MRP stops chasing B's material → production shortage that MRP believes is fulfilled.
confirmed.fixSketch: Distribute the accepted qty across links proportionally to allocatedQuantity (or fill sequentially up to each link's remaining allocation), not the full amount to each link.

verdict.reasoning: mrp.service.ts:2418-2447: updateReceivedQuantity(purchaseOrderItemId, receivedQuantity) loads ALL requirement_po_links for the PO item and, for EACH link, computes newReceived = Number(link.receivedQuantity) + receivedQuantity (line 2424) — crediting the full item-level receipt to every link with no proration against link.allocatedQuantity and no remaining-quantity tracking. The caller (grn.service.ts:816,881, inside GRN approval tx) passes acceptedQty = the whole GRN item's acceptedQuantity for that PO item. Meanwhile PO generation (mrp.service.ts:2296-2311) deliberately creates MULTIPLE links per consolidated PO item with proportional allocatedQuantity = (reqShortfall/totalShortfall) * item.quantity, and linkRequirementToPO (2339-2372) can attach further links to the same item. Line 2425 then flips a requirement to RECEIVED when newReceived >= allocatedQuantity (2433-2437), so any requirement whose allocation is <= the item's cumulative receipts is marked RECEIVED regardless of its actual physical share. Nothing downstream corrects this: the only recent fix here (F4 #12 comment) addressed atomicity, not allocation, and the inflated link.receivedQuantity is exposed as-is via the API (mapToResponse poLinks, line 2623). The classic F5 shape — the guard (newReceived >= allocatedQuantity) checks a figure that no longer means "received against THIS allocation".
verdict.failureScenario: generatePOFromRequirements consolidates requirements A (shortfall 60m) and B (shortfall 40m) into one PO item of 100m, creating two links with allocatedQuantity 60 and 40. A GRN approving 40m calls updateReceivedQuantity(poItemId, 40): both links get receivedQuantity = 40; link B satisfies 40 >= 40, so requirement B flips to RECEIVED even though only 40 of 100m arrived (B's proportional share is 16m). Total link receivedQuantity = 80 vs 40 actually received. A second 40m GRN pushes both links to 80: A (80 >= 60) also flips RECEIVED at 80m physically received of 100m ordered. MRP stops chasing requirements it believes fulfilled, causing an untracked production-material shortage; API/reports show double-counted phantom receipts. Only single-link PO items (the non-consolidated case) escape the bug.

confirmed.title: purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity is a hand-maintained counter that permanently includes QC-REJECTED quantity — PO closes as RECEIVED with rejected goods never re-procured
confirmed.evidence: createGRN increments receivedQuantity by GROSS item.receivedQuantity at GRN creation, pre-QC (grn.service.ts:212-219). approveGRN never subtracts rejectedQuantity (rejections only get an ADJUSTMENT_OUT stock_movements audit row, lines 887-907). rejectGRN decrements only whole-GRN rejection (1793-1801). updateReceivingStatus derives PO status from this gross counter (purchaseOrder.service.ts:878-893). Meanwhile MRP link receivedQuantity is updated with ACCEPTED qty only (grn.service.ts:881) — the two rollups use different figures.
confirmed.failureScenario: PO orders 100; GRN receives 100 with 20 rejected at QC. receivedQuantity stays 100 → PO status RECEIVED, pendingQuantity shows 0 (purchaseOrder.service.ts:1242), so the 20 rejected units awaiting supplier return are never reordered; MRP shows the requirement 80/100 while the PO says fully received.
confirmed.fixSketch: Derive received qty from accepted grn_items of ACCEPTED GRNs (or decrement rejectedQuantity at approval), and use one definition of 'received' for both PO status and MRP links.

verdict.reasoning: grn.service.ts:212-219 increments purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity by GROSS item.receivedQuantity inside the createGRN transaction, and line 343 immediately calls updateReceivingStatus — which (purchaseOrder.service.ts:878-893) sets the PO to RECEIVED when gross receivedQuantity >= orderedQuantity, at GRN creation, before QC. approveGRN never subtracts rejectedQuantity: accepted qty goes to stock and to MRP via mrpService.updateReceivedQuantity(poItemId, acceptedQty, tx) (line 881), while rejected qty gets only an ADJUSTMENT_OUT stock_movements audit row (lines 886-907). A repo-wide grep confirms the ONLY decrement of purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity in the backend is rejectGRN (lines 1793-1801), which applies solely to whole-GRN rejection while status is still PENDING_QC — partial QC rejection during approval leaves the gross counter untouched forever. pendingQuantity is derived as ordered - receivedQuantity (purchaseOrder.service.ts:1242, grn.service.ts:519), so it reads 0. The finding is actually WORSE than claimed: createGRN (lines 61-68) rejects any PO not in SENT/ACKNOWLEDGED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, so once the PO flips to RECEIVED a replacement GRN for the rejected units cannot even be created; and the over-receipt guard (lines 82-92) computes maxAllowed from the gross counter, capping any replacement at the 10% tolerance. The dual-rollup inconsistency is also confirmed: the parallel po-status-manager.service.ts path (used by unified-po.controller.ts) increments receivedQuantity by acceptedQuantity (lines 66-73) — the opposite convention — so the column's meaning depends on which code path handled the receipt. No supplier-return/debit-note flow exists anywhere that restores pending quantity after partial rejection.
verdict.failureScenario: PO orders 100 units. GRN created for 100 (accepted 80, rejected 20 recorded on the GRN item). At creation, receivedQuantity increments to 100 (gross) and updateReceivingStatus sets PO status = RECEIVED. QC approval then stocks only 80 and tells MRP 80, but never decrements the PO counter by the 20 rejected — pendingQuantity shows 0 and the PO reads fully received. When the supplier ships 20 replacement units, createGRN throws "Cannot receive goods for PO in RECEIVED status" (grn.service.ts:67-68), so the replacement physically cannot be booked against the PO; the 20-unit shortfall (MRP shows 80/100) is permanently unreconcilable with the PO ledger and never re-procured through it.

confirmed.title: allocateStock marks requirements FULFILLED_STOCK without verifying stock exists, and reserves against quantityAvailable ignoring existing reservations
confirmed.evidence: mrp.service.ts:1805-1813 computes newAllocated/newShortfall/FULFILLED_STOCK purely from the REQUESTED data.quantity. The FIFO loops (1844-1889) reserve best-effort — `remaining` can end > 0 and is never checked, no error thrown. toReserve = min(remaining, lot.quantityAvailable) with quantityReserved only incremented, never netted against quantityAvailable, so an already-fully-reserved lot is reserved again.
confirmed.failureScenario: Requirement needs 500m, physical free stock is 200m. allocateStock(500) → requirement flips to FULFILLED_STOCK, shortfall 0, MRP stops procuring; only 200m actually reserved. Second requirement allocates against the same lots (available still >0) → double-reserve. At cutting time 300m is missing with no PO in flight.
confirmed.fixSketch: Compute reservable = available − reserved per lot, throw (rolling back) if remaining > 0 after the FIFO pass, and set allocatedFromStock to the actually-reserved amount.

verdict.reasoning: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts allocateStock (1796-1919): lines 1805-1813 compute newAllocated/newShortfall/FULFILLED_STOCK purely from the requested data.quantity before any stock lookup; the only guards anywhere upstream are z.number().positive() (mrp.schema.ts:86-89) and quantity<=0 in mrp.controller.ts:187 — no stock-sufficiency check exists. The three FIFO loops (fabric 1844-1858, greige 1859-1873, lace 1874-1889) are best-effort: `remaining` can end > 0 and is silently discarded (no throw, no status correction), and for material types other than FABRIC/GREIGE/LACE no physical reservation happens at all while the status still flips to FULFILLED_STOCK. The stock_reservations audit row (1898-1911) records reservedQuantity = data.quantity regardless of actual reservation. The double-reserve claim is confirmed by comparing with the canonical reservation implementations: greige-stock.service.ts:408-418 throws on insufficiency and decrements quantityAvailable while incrementing quantityReserved, and laceStock.service.ts:462-470 does the same — i.e., quantityAvailable is net-free and MUST be decremented on reserve. allocateStock only increments quantityReserved (1855/1870/1885) and never decrements quantityAvailable, so a fully-reserved lot still advertises its full quantityAvailable and the FIFO filter (quantityAvailable > 0, never netted against quantityReserved) selects it again for the next requirement. One correction to the finding's framing: the whole block IS now wrapped in prisma.$transaction (added per the F4 bug-hunt comment at 1815-1818), so there is no partial-write/atomicity issue — but the transaction faithfully commits the wrong numbers; all F5 defects remain.
verdict.failureScenario: Requirement R1 needs 500m of fabric F; physical free stock is one lot with quantityAvailable=200, quantityReserved=0. POST /api/mrp/requirements/R1/allocate-stock {quantity:500} passes validation (only positivity checked) → R1 is updated to allocatedFromStock=500, shortfall=0, status=FULFILLED_STOCK; the FIFO loop reserves only 200 (remaining=300 discarded); the lot ends available=200/reserved=200; stock_reservations records 500 reserved. MRP dashboards and PO generation exclude R1 (they filter shortfall>0 / status PO_REQUIRED, e.g. mrp.service.ts:1757-1777), so no PO is ever raised for the missing 300m. A second requirement R2 for fabric F then allocates 200m: the same lot still shows quantityAvailable=200 (never decremented) so it is picked again → quantityReserved=400 against 200 physical meters (double-reserve). At cutting time 300m is missing with no procurement in flight and an audit trail claiming 700m was reserved.

confirmed.title: work_orders.completedQuantity is stored-not-derived and effectively never updates
confirmed.evidence: addProductionTracking only sets completedQuantity when a SINGLE tracking entry satisfies `data.productionStage === ProductionStage.PACKING && data.quantityCompleted >= workOrder.totalQuantity` (lines 604-616). production_tracking rows are the line items but are never summed. work_order_breakup.completedQuantity is written once as 0 (line 131) and never updated by any code path (grep confirms no other writer). Meanwhile updateWorkOrderSchema (workOrder.schema.ts:52) lets any PUT /work-orders/:id set completedQuantity to an arbitrary number with no derivation check. calculateCMTCost (line 1035) then computes totalCost = perPieceCost * workOrder.completedQuantity from this stale/hand-set value.
confirmed.failureScenario: Pack a 1000-pc WO in two PACKING tracking entries of 500 each: neither entry is >= 1000, so the WO never flips to COMPLETED and completedQuantity stays 0; CMT actual-cost update (updateActualCMTCosts) computes totals from completedQuantity=0. Conversely a client PUT with completedQuantity=99999 is accepted verbatim.
confirmed.fixSketch: Derive completedQuantity from SUM of finishing/packing line items (finishing_output_skus / production_tracking for PACKING) at read time or recompute inside the same transaction as each output write; remove completedQuantity from the update schema.
confirmed.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

verdict.reasoning: workOrder.service.ts:604-617 is the ONLY writer of work_orders.completedQuantity (grep confirms; all other references are zero-initializers at lines 120/131/881/894 and stockProductionOrder.service.ts:292/303). It fires only when a SINGLE tracking entry has productionStage===PACKING && quantityCompleted >= totalQuantity, then sets completedQuantity=totalQuantity wholesale — production_tracking rows (the true line items) are never summed anywhere in the codebase. The frontend (ProductionTrackingInlineForm.tsx:117-148) sends per-batch quantities (validates each entry <= totalQuantity, toast says 'N pieces completed'), so multi-batch packing never triggers the branch. work_order_breakup.completedQuantity is created as 0 (line 131) and has no updater. Meanwhile updateWorkOrderSchema (workOrder.schema.ts:52) accepts any nonnegative int for completedQuantity, the controller copies it into updateData, and updateWorkOrder (service line 480-484) spreads ...data into prisma.update with no cap or derivation check — 99999 on a 100-pc WO persists. calculateCMTCost:1035 computes totalCost = perPieceCost * completedQuantity from this value, and workOrder.controller.ts:141-166 auto-runs updateActualCMTCosts whenever a PUT sets status=COMPLETED (the manual workaround users must use since auto-completion never fires), writing CMT actuals into order_item_costing from completedQuantity=0, with the try/catch at line 163 swallowing any error. Dashboards (getProductionDashboard _sum at 633-636, productionStatus.service.ts:277, orderProductionStatus.service.ts:332) all aggregate the stored stale column.
verdict.failureScenario: 1000-pc WO packed in two PACKING tracking entries of 500 each: neither entry satisfies 500 >= 1000, so completedQuantity stays 0 and status never flips to COMPLETED. User then manually PUTs status=COMPLETED (without setting completedQuantity) — controller triggers calculateCMTCost with completedQuantity=0, so totalCost=0 and updateActualCMTCosts writes wrong actual CMT into order_item_costing, silently (errors swallowed at controller line 163). Conversely, PUT /work-orders/:id with completedQuantity=99999 on a 100-pc WO is accepted verbatim (schema only enforces nonnegative) and inflates CMT totalCost and every dashboard sum.

confirmed.title: completeCuttingBatch fabricReturns: three-way field-name drift (schema returnQuantity vs controller returnedQuantity vs frontend returnedQuantity) breaks fabric returns
confirmed.evidence: completeCuttingBatchSchema (production.schema.ts:186-192) REQUIRES `returnQuantity: z.number().positive()` per item; the controller reads `ret.returnedQuantity` (cutting.controller.ts:612: `if (ret.fabricStockId && ret.returnedQuantity > 0)`); the frontend sends `returnedQuantity` (frontend/src/pages/CuttingDetail.tsx:196, frontend/src/types/cutting.types.ts:237). validateBody strictly parses (validation.middleware.ts:28), so the required-but-missing returnQuantity fails.
confirmed.failureScenario: User completes a cutting batch and enters any fabric return (the dialog pre-fills returns with the full balance, CuttingDetail.tsx:178) → POST /cutting/batches/:id/complete returns 400 'Invalid request data'; batch cannot be completed with returns, and the return challan / stock restore never happens. Even if the schema were fixed to match the frontend, the controller/schema mismatch would silently drop returns.
confirmed.fixSketch: Align on one field name (returnedQuantity) in schema, controller, and frontend type; add a test that completes a batch with a return.
confirmed.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

verdict.reasoning: Three-way field-name drift verified in code. (1) Route cutting.routes.ts:106-109 applies validateBody(completeCuttingBatchSchema) to POST /batches/:id/complete. (2) Schema production.schema.ts:186-191 requires `returnQuantity: z.number().positive()` per fabricReturns item; .passthrough() admits extra keys but does not waive the required field. (3) Frontend CuttingDetail.tsx:192-197 sends `{ fabricStockId, returnedQuantity }` (only items with qty > 0), matching the type in cutting.types.ts:235-238 — so every item in a non-empty array is missing the required `returnQuantity`. validation.middleware.ts:28 does schema.parse(req.body) and returns 400 'Invalid request data' on ZodError. (4) Independently, the controller (cutting.controller.ts:612-613) reads `ret.returnedQuantity`, so a schema-compliant client sending `returnQuantity` would pass validation but `undefined > 0` is false → returnMap empty → createFabricReturnChallan (line 631) never called, cutting_batch_fabrics.fabricReturned written as 0, actualConsumption overstated (line 647). The .passthrough() on the item object is the only reason the controller COULD work if just the schema key were renamed — it currently cannot, because validation rejects first.
verdict.failureScenario: Cutting batch IN_PROGRESS with fabric issued via internal challan and any un-consumed balance. User clicks Complete: handleOpenCompleteDialog (CuttingDetail.tsx:169-180) pre-fills return qtys with the full balance, so fabricReturns is non-empty, each item {fabricStockId, returnedQuantity}. Zod requires returnQuantity → 400 'Invalid request data' (detail: fabricReturns.0.returnQuantity required); batch cannot be completed with returns. Only workaround is manually zeroing every return qty (fabricReturns: [] passes — no .min on the array), which completes the batch but silently skips the return challan and fabric-stock restore and inflates actualConsumption by the unreturned balance.

confirmed.title: record-output and issue-to-stitching schemas require skuId that neither controller nor frontend uses → 400s / silent skips
confirmed.evidence: recordCuttingOutputSchema requires `skuId: z.string().uuid()` per SKU (line 99) but the controller iterates `if (sku.id)` (cutting.controller.ts:511) and silently SKIPS items without `id`; the frontend type sends `id?` and no skuId (cutting.types.ts:215). issueToStitchingSchema likewise requires skuId (line 162) but cutting-issue.controller.ts:68-113 reads only colorId/sizeId/quantity, and the frontend builds `{colorId, sizeId, quantity}` (CuttingDetail.tsx:386-391).
confirmed.failureScenario: POST /cutting/batches/:id/record-output and /issue-to-stitching with the frontend's actual payload → Zod 400 (missing skuId), endpoints unusable. A client that appeases Zod by sending only skuId gets a 200 from record-output while ZERO cutting_batch_skus rows are updated (sku.id undefined → loop skips silently).

confirmed.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

verdict.reasoning: All four legs of the finding check out in code. (1) production.schema.ts:99 and :162 require skuId (z.string().uuid(), not optional) in each skuOutputs item for recordCuttingOutputSchema and issueToStitchingSchema. (2) cutting.routes.ts:100-103 and :138-142 wire both endpoints through validateBody, and validation.middleware.ts:25-45 does a strict schema.parse that 400s on any ZodError. confirmed.title: createCuttingBatch auto-issues the ENTIRE fabric lot because it reads sku.cutQuantity which is never set at creation
confirmed.evidence: `const totalPieces = skuOutputs.reduce((sum, s) => sum + (Number(s.cutQuantity) || 0), 0)` (line 277) — but at batch creation the SKUs carry toCut/plannedQty (created with cutQty: 0, line 207) and the frontend CreateCuttingBatchRequest has no cutQuantity. So totalPieces=0 and line 294 falls through to `fabricNeeded = Number(stock.quantityAvailable)` → `issueQty = min(fullLot, fullLot)` — the whole lot is issued via challan for every batch.
confirmed.failureScenario: Create a batch needing ~200m from a 1,000m lot → the auto-challan issues all 1,000m (fabric_stock.quantityAvailable → 0). Recovery depends on completion-time returns, which are broken by production-2 → the 800m surplus is stranded/lost from available stock and other work orders see zero stock.
confirmed.fixSketch: Compute fabricNeeded from toCut/plannedQty * cadAvg (the fields actually present at creation), and never default to issuing the full lot.

verdict.reasoning: The code confirms every link of the claimed chain. (1) backend/src/controllers/cutting.controller.ts:277-280 computes `totalPieces` by summing `s.cutQuantity` over skuOutputs — but at batch creation skuOutputs carry only planning fields: the create call at line 198-210 stores `toCut: sku.toCut || sku.plannedQty` and hard-codes `cutQty: 0`. Proof the field is wrong: 30 lines earlier (lines 243-246) the SAME skuOutputs array is summed for production_tracking using `Number(s.toCut) || Number(s.plannedQty)` — the same figure computed two ways in one function (classic F5 compute-twice). (2) Neither frontend caller ever sends `cutQuantity`: frontend/src/types/cutting.types.ts:195-199 defines CreateCuttingBatchRequest.skuOutputs as `{colorId, sizeId, plannedQty}` only, and both builders (CuttingForm.tsx:341-347, CuttingChart.tsx:183-189) map exactly those three fields. A repo-wide grep shows `cutQuantity` appears nowhere else except as an optional field in the Zod skuOutputSchema (production.schema.ts:39) — so validation passes and totalPieces is always 0. (3) At line 294, `cadAvg && totalPieces > 0` is false (cadAverageUsed is required >0 by both the Zod schema and the line-162 guard, so cadAvg is truthy — the ternary fails solely on totalPieces===0), so `fabricNeeded = Number(stock.quantityAvailable)` and `issueQty = min(fullLot, fullLot)` = the entire lot; the same fallback fires per additional lot in `fabricStocks`. (4) The challan is real: issueChallan (backend/src/services/challan.service.ts:279-306) for INTERNAL challans decrements fabric_stock.quantityAvailable by the item quantity in a transaction, sets status EXHAUSTED at 0, and syncs stock_levels down by the same amount. Recovery paths exist but are manual: deleteCuttingBatch restores fabricIssued/fabricConsumed (lines 410-442), and completeCuttingBatch accepts an explicit `fabricReturns` array (lines 608-637) — surplus comes back only if the user types the return quantities at completion; nothing automatic reconciles issued-vs-needed. One nuance vs the finding text: the intended `totalPieces * cadAvg` branch is dead code, so this is not a partial miscalculation — it is a systematic full-lot issue on 100% of batches created through the UI.
verdict.failureScenario: Repro: a fabric lot (fabric_stock row) has quantityAvailable = 1000m. In the Cutting form, create a batch for a work order needing 200 pcs with CAD average 1.0 m/pc (expected need ~200m), selecting that lot. The frontend POSTs skuOutputs = [{colorId, sizeId, plannedQty: 200}]. In createCuttingBatch: totalPieces = sum(cutQuantity) = 0 (field absent) → line 294 falls to fabricNeeded = 1000 → issueQty = min(1000, 1000) = 1000 → an INTERNAL challan for 1000m is created and issued → issueChallan sets fabric_stock.quantityAvailable = 0, status = EXHAUSTED, and decrements stock_levels by 1000. Immediately, every other work order/batch sees zero available stock for that lot even though 800m is physically uncut. If additional lots were selected via fabricStocks, each is also issued in full. The 800m surplus only returns if the operator manually enters fabricReturns at batch completion (or the batch is deleted); until then — or forever, if returns are skipped or broken per production-2 — available stock is understated by the surplus on every batch.

confirmed.evidence: Sequence: cutting_batches.create (180) → cutting_batch_fabrics.createMany (218) → work_orders.update (232) → production_tracking.create in try/catch (242-261, logs and continues) → createChallan+issueChallan in try/catch that logs 'Don't fail batch creation if challan fails' (263-330). verdict.reasoning: Verified in backend/src/controllers/cutting.controller.ts. createCuttingBatch (lines 180-330) executes five writes on the global prisma client with no wrapping $transaction: cutting_batches.create (180), cutting_batch_fabrics.createMany (218), work_orders.update to IN_PRODUCTION (232), production_tracking.create inside a try/catch that logs and continues (242-261), and createChallan+issueChallan inside a second try/catch whose comment literally says "Don't fail batch creation if challan fails — log and continue" (327-330). issueChallan (backend/src/services/challan.service.ts:197) is the ONLY place fabric_stock is deducted for the batch: it runs in its OWN prisma.$transaction and throws on "Insufficient fabric stock" (lines 283-288). Two realistic throw sources: (1) createChallan's generateChallanNumber does read-max-then-insert with challanNumber @unique (schema.prisma:8347) — concurrent challan creation anywhere in the system collides and the whole createChallan tx throws; (2) the controller caps issueQty against quantityAvailable read OUTSIDE the tx (lines 284-295), so a concurrent deduction between the pre-read and issueChallan's re-read triggers the insufficient-stock throw. Either way the error is swallowed and the batch stands. Downstream: completeCuttingBatch (556-710) computes totalFabricIssued solely from ISSUED/RECEIVED INTERNAL challans (586-598); with no challan it gets 0, sets fabricIssued/actualConsumption to null, and falls back to lay-based fabricConsumed at line 666 for averaging only — NO code path in completion (or recordCuttingOutput) ever deducts fabric_stock. So the physically-cut fabric is never removed from the ledger. Worse, deleteCuttingBatch (412-450) restores `fabricIssued || fabricConsumed` back into fabric_stock via increment — if the challan had silently failed (nothing was ever deducted) but fabricConsumed was recorded, deletion CREATES phantom stock. The crash-window claim also holds: batch.create and work_orders.update are separate top-level writes, so a crash between them leaves a live batch on a PENDING work order. Aggravating detail: line 277-280 sums `s.cutQuantity`, a field skuOutputs do not carry (they carry toCut/plannedQty per lines 200-210), so totalPieces is 0 and issueQty defaults to the ENTIRE available lot — the auto-issue path is fragile exactly where the swallow hides its failures.
verdict.failureScenario: Repro A (challan-number race): User A creates a cutting batch while any other user issues any challan concurrently. Both generateChallanNumber calls read the same max and compute e.g. CHN-0042; the second insert violates the challanNumber @unique constraint (schema.prisma:8347), createChallan's tx rolls back, the catch at cutting.controller.ts:327 logs a warning and returns 201. Result: batch exists, work order is IN_PRODUCTION, but zero meters were deducted from fabric_stock. The batch proceeds through start → recordCuttingOutput (fabricConsumed recorded) → completeCuttingBatch, where the challan groupBy finds nothing, totalFabricIssued=0, fabricIssued/actualConsumption are stored null, and fabric_stock.quantityAvailable still shows the consumed meters as available — silently overstated, exactly the stock_levels-drift template. Repro B (concurrent lot depletion): two batches created near-simultaneously against the same fabric_stock lot; both pre-read the same quantityAvailable (line 289), and because totalPieces=0 (line 277 reads nonexistent cutQuantity) both try to issue the whole lot; the first issueChallan tx deducts everything, the second throws Insufficient fabric stock inside its tx, is swallowed, and batch 2 is cuttable with no stock backing. verdict.reasoning: Traced end-to-end. (4) Meanwhile, in the SAME function, fabric_stock.quantityAvailable is `{ increment: quantityGood }` (line 434-437) and updateProductionTracking (lines 522-567) uses increment/decrement of quantityGood per call — delta semantics. These two semantics cannot both be right: if the user enters this-delivery quantity (the natural reading — the form is titled "Record receipt of material from smocking vendor" and shows no remaining-balance figure), the send-out record's cumulative fields are overwritten, totalAccountedFor (line 392-394) never reaches quantitySent so status is stuck at PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, the service requirement is never set COMPLETED (line 425-429), the RECEIVED-gated production_tracking record is never created (line 450-459), and actualCost (line 398) reflects only the last delivery. If instead the user re-enters the cumulative total, the record is right but fabric_stock and piece counts double-increment. There is no reconciliation/guard either way. Bonus defect confirming F1/F5 flavor: line 392 computes totalAccountedFor = quantityReceived + quantityDamaged even though quantityGood = quantityReceived - quantityDamaged (line 375) means quantityReceived already includes damaged — damaged is double-counted, so a single receipt of 90 (10 damaged) against 100 sent is marked fully RECEIVED.
verdict.failureScenario: Send 100m fabric to smocking (sourceType FABRIC_STOCK). Dashboard still shows a "Receive" button (status PARTIALLY_RECEIVED). Vendor returns the last 50m; user clicks Receive, enters 50 → update ASSIGNS quantityReceived=50 (first receipt erased), totalAccountedFor=50 < 100 so status stays PARTIALLY_RECEIVED forever, actualCost=50*rate (half the true liability), service requirement never COMPLETED — while fabric_stock correctly gained 100 total. confirmed.evidence: updateCostSheetActuals does `data: { [actualField]: actualCost }` (plain assignment, costSheet.service.ts:265-270). Its only caller, grn.controller.ts approveGRN (lines 216-287), computes styleActuals from THIS GRN's items only (`for (const grnItem of grnWithItems.grn_items)` at 218, unitPrice*receivedQty summed at 222-242) and passes that per-GRN figure as actualCost. The whole block is wrapped in `catch { logError(...) }` (grn.controller.ts:289-292) — fire-and-forget, off-transaction (F4).
confirmed.failureScenario: Style receives fabric via GRN-1 (₹80,000) then GRN-2 (₹30,000). verdict.reasoning: All claims verified in code. (1) costSheet.service.ts:265-270: updateCostSheetActuals writes `data: { [actualField]: actualCost }` — plain assignment, no { increment }, no re-derivation from GRN line items. (2) Grep confirms the ONLY invocations are grn.controller.ts:250/263/276 inside approveGRN (purchaseOrder.controller.ts:17 and workOrder.controller.ts:12 merely import it, never call it). (3) approveGRN fetches only the GRN being approved (prisma.goods_receiving_notes.findUnique({ where: { id } }), line 182) and sums unitPrice*receivedQty over that single GRN's grn_items (lines 218-245), so each approval passes a per-GRN figure that replaces, not accumulates, the prior actual. (4) calculateVariance (lines 75-88, 181-187) computes fabricVariance from the stored fabricActual and sets varianceStatus WITHIN_BUDGET when |variance%| <= buffer — it never re-derives actuals, so the corrupted value flows straight into the approval gate. (5) F4 aspects confirmed: entire block wrapped in try/catch that logError-and-continues (lines 180, 289-292), runs after grnService.approveGRN has committed (line 173), and the per-style/per-category update loop is non-transactional. One correction to the claimed repro: with the ₹80k-then-₹30k figures, Math.abs(variancePercent) > buffer (line 85) would set REQUIRES_APPROVAL (wrong number, wrong direction — flagged as favorable), not WITHIN_BUDGET; the WITHIN_BUDGET-despite-overspend outcome occurs when the LAST GRN alone lands near budget.
verdict.failureScenario: Style S has a PROCUREMENT_PRODUCTION cost sheet with fabricBudget ₹30,000 (5% buffer). Fabric PO is delivered in two partial shipments. GRN-1 approved: fabric items worth ₹25,000 → fabricActual = 25,000. GRN-2 approved: items worth ₹29,000 → updateCostSheetActuals overwrites fabricActual = 29,000 (real cumulative spend ₹54,000, 80% over budget). calculateVariance then computes -3.3% variance → varianceStatus = WITHIN_BUDGET, silently approving an 80% overspend. Conversely, with the original ₹80k/₹30k example the sheet shows a phantom -70% 'favorable' variance flagged REQUIRES_APPROVAL — wrong in the other direction. Any style received across 2+ GRNs (routine partial deliveries) gets a wrong actual; and because the block is catch-and-continue off-transaction, any error (e.g. no PROCUREMENT_PRODUCTION sheet throws at costSheet.service.ts:245) is swallowed and the actuals silently never update at all.
