confirmed.title: Decimal >= Decimal compares as STRINGS — 'fully received' check is lexicographic
confirmed.evidence: `item.receivedQuantity >= item.orderedQuantity` (lines 1805-1807 in updateLaceProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeLaceGRN and 1862 in updateProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeGRN). Both columns are Prisma Decimal (schema.prisma purchase_order_items:1235-1236). decimal.js Decimal.prototype.valueOf returns a STRING, so JS relational comparison of two Decimal objects is string comparison: '95' >= '100' is true, '100' >= '20' is false.
confirmed.failureScenario: Greige PO orders 100m, GRN receives 95m → '95' >= '100' → lexicographically TRUE → PO treated as fully received → linked Processing PO auto-flipped PENDING_GREIGE → READY_FOR_PROCESSING before the greige exists. Conversely ordered 20m, received 100m → '100' >= '20' false → processing PO never released.
confirmed.fixSketch: Compare numerically: Number(item.receivedQuantity) >= Number(item.orderedQuantity), or item.receivedQuantity.gte(item.orderedQuantity).

verdict.reasoning: Verified in code and at runtime. (1) Schema: backend/prisma/schema.prisma purchase_order_items lines 1235-1236 declare orderedQuantity and receivedQuantity as Decimal @db.Decimal(10,3), so Prisma returns them as Prisma.Decimal (decimal.js) objects. (2) The comparisons at backend/src/services/costSheetPOGeneration.service.ts:1805-1807 (updateLaceProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeLaceGRN) and :1862 (updateProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeGRN) use raw JS `item.receivedQuantity >= item.orderedQuantity` with no .gte()/Number() conversion. (3) decimal.js (backend/node_modules/decimal.js/decimal.js:2461) defines `P.valueOf = P.toJSON` returning a STRING; per ES abstract relational comparison, when ToPrimitive yields strings for both operands the comparison is lexicographic. (4) Runtime-proven against the project's own @prisma/client: `new Prisma.Decimal('95') >= new Prisma.Decimal('100')` evaluates TRUE and `new Prisma.Decimal('100') >= new Prisma.Decimal('20')` evaluates FALSE. (5) The live call path exists: grn.service.ts:935 invokes updateProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeGRN(grn.poId) as a post-commit cascade after GRN approval, and that method re-fetches the PO with prisma.purchase_orders.findUnique (costSheetPOGeneration.service.ts:1850-1855), so the compared fields are genuine Decimal objects, not numbers. The `every(...)` at line 1862 is the sole gate before flipping linked Processing POs from PENDING_GREIGE to READY_FOR_PROCESSING (lines 1870-1884); no other guard exists. Partial receipt is an explicitly supported state (the code logs 'Greige PO not fully received yet'), and receivedQuantity is incremented per-GRN via mrpService.updateReceivedQuantity, so mismatched-digit-length values like 95 vs 100 arise in normal operation. One mitigating note: the lace variant (line 1789) has no callers in backend/src — only the GREIGE variant at grn.service.ts:935 is live — so the lace-specific instance is currently latent dead code with the same defect.
verdict.failureScenario: Greige PO orders 100m of greige fabric; first GRN receives 95m and is approved. Post-commit, updateProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeGRN runs: '95' >= '100' compares lexicographically ('9' > '1') → TRUE → PO deemed fully received → the linked Processing PO is flipped PENDING_GREIGE → READY_FOR_PROCESSING and annotated '[Auto-updated] Greige received - Ready for processing' even though 5m of greige does not exist yet. Conversely, a PO ordering 20m that receives 100m (over-delivery, or ordered 8 / received 10): '100' >= '20' is FALSE → deemed not fully received → the Processing PO stays stuck in PENDING_GREIGE forever with no error, silently blocking the processing workflow. Reproduced deterministically against the project's Prisma client. Comparisons where both quantities render to same-length strings (100 vs 100, 50 vs 100) happen to give correct results, which is why the bug is intermittent and data-dependent.

confirmed.title: Greige-lace PO shortfall computed against FINISHED lace stock, not greige-lace stock
confirmed.evidence: In calculateRequirements, stockInfo comes from `this.getStockInfoForLace(laceItem.laceId)` (line 371, finished lace_stock). For GREIGE_PROCESSED, the greige item uses `shortfall: Math.max(0, greigeRequiredQty - stockInfo.available)` (lines 438 and 450) — i.e., greige requirement offset by FINISHED-lace availability of a different master (laceId, not greigeLaceId). The fabric flow does this correctly via getStockInfoForGreige(fabricItem.greigeId) (line 185).
confirmed.failureScenario: 20m of finished lace in stock, 0m greige lace, requirement 100m greige → shortfall computed 80m → greige-lace PO under-ordered by 20m; production starves. Or greige lace in stock is ignored entirely → over-ordering.
confirmed.fixSketch: Add a getStockInfoForGreigeLace(greigeLaceId) (lace_stock rows for the greige master or its own stock table) and compute greige-lace shortfall/availableStock from it.

verdict.reasoning: In backend/src/services/costSheetPOGeneration.service.ts, calculateRequirements fetches stockInfo once per lace item via getStockInfoForLace(laceItem.laceId) (line 371), which sums lace_stock rows where laceId = the FINISHED lace master. In the GREIGE_PROCESSED branch, the greige-lace requirement greigeRequiredQty = requiredQty / (1 - shrinkage/100) (line 428) is offset by that finished-lace availability: shortfall: Math.max(0, greigeRequiredQty - stockInfo.available) at line 438 (greige-lace PO line, materialId = laceItem.greigeLaceId) and again at line 450 (LACE_PROCESSING line). The spread `...item` also copies availableStock: stockInfo.available (finished lace) onto the greige line, so the displayed stock is for the wrong master. No getStockInfoForGreigeLace exists; schema.prisma:1945 confirms greigeLace is a lace_master, so greige-lace stock sits in lace_stock keyed by greigeLaceId — calling the existing getStockInfoForLace(laceItem.greigeLaceId) would have been correct and is never done. The fabric flow proves the intended pattern: GREIGE_PROCESSED fabric calls getStockInfoForGreige(fabricItem.greigeId) (line 185) and nets shortfall against greige stock (line 196), and its processing item uses shortfall = full requiredQty (lines 214-215), unlike the lace processing line. Shortfall feeds directly into PO quantity via calculateOrderQuantities (orderQty = shortfall + allowance, line 601). Even under a charitable "net finished stock against greige buy" reading, the math is dimensionally wrong (finished meters subtracted from shrinkage-inflated greige meters instead of netting before the divide), so no interpretation makes the code correct.
verdict.failureScenario: Under-order: cost sheet lace requirement 100m finished at 10% shrinkage; 20m of that finished lace in lace_stock, 0m greige lace. greigeRequiredQty = 111.1m; shortfall computed 111.1 - 20 = 91.1m, so the greige-lace PO (and the matching greige-processing service PO at line 450) are ~20m short of the 111.1m needed — production starves. Over-order: 100m of the greige lace already AVAILABLE in lace_stock under greigeLaceId, 0m finished lace; stockInfo.available = 0 (queried for laceId, not greigeLaceId), shortfall = full 111.1m → PO re-purchases greige lace already on hand. Both flow straight into orderQty in calculateOrderQuantities.

confirmed.title: Preferred-supplier lace price never used: query selects 'pricePerMeter' but code reads '.price'
confirmed.evidence: The lace_suppliers select fetches `pricePerMeter` (lines 154-163), but getReadyLaceCost checks `if (preferredSupplier?.price) { cost = Number(preferredSupplier.price); ... rateSource='SUPPLIER_PRICE' }` (lines 368-372). `.price` is always undefined, so the branch is dead and it silently falls through to lace_master.pricePerMeter.
confirmed.failureScenario: Preferred supplier quotes ₹18/m, stale lace-master rate is ₹12/m → READY_LACE option costed at ₹12/m with rateSource LACE_MASTER → comparison recommends READY_LACE on a price nobody will honor → cost sheet and downstream PO budget wrong by 50%.
confirmed.fixSketch: Read preferredSupplier.pricePerMeter (the selected field name).

verdict.reasoning: Traced the full path in backend/src/services/laceCostingCalculation.service.ts. (1) The lace_master query (lines 154-163) selects lace_suppliers with `where: { isPreferred: true, isActive: true }, take: 1` and its select list is exactly `{ id, supplierId, pricePerMeter, supplier: { id, name } }` — no field named `price`. (2) The Prisma model `lace_suppliers` (backend/prisma/schema.prisma lines 5610-5626) confirms the column is `pricePerMeter Decimal?`; there is no `price` field on the model at all, so even an unrestricted select could never return `.price`. (3) getReadyLaceCost (lines 358-402) branches on `if (preferredSupplier?.price)` (line 368) — this is always undefined, making the entire SUPPLIER_PRICE branch (cost, supplierId, supplierName, rateSource='SUPPLIER_PRICE') dead code. It unconditionally falls to `else if (lace.pricePerMeter)` (line 373), returning rateSource 'LACE_MASTER' with supplierName null, so the details string always renders "(Lace Master rate)" and never the supplier attribution. Secondary latent bug in the same fallback: line 376 reads `lace.updatedAt`, which is also not in the select, so lastUpdated is always null too. No serializer/camelCase transformation applies here — this is a raw Prisma result consumed in-process, so nothing rescues the `.price` read. The `lace: any` parameter type is why TypeScript never flagged it. This is classic F3/F5: query contract and consumer drifted, and the guard checks a field that cannot exist.
verdict.failureScenario: Repro: create a lace_master with pricePerMeter=12; add a lace_suppliers row for it with isPreferred=true, isActive=true, pricePerMeter=18. Call calculateLaceCost for that laceId. getReadyLaceCost receives the supplier row but `preferredSupplier.price` is undefined, so it returns readyLaceCost=12, rateSource='LACE_MASTER', supplierId/supplierName=null. The comparison table prices the 'Ready Lace' strategy at ₹12/m instead of the ₹18/m the preferred supplier actually charges; if greige+dyeing costs, say, ₹15/m effective, the recommendation picks READY_LACE on a 33% understated cost, and the cost sheet / downstream PO budget inherits the wrong figure. The only mitigation is coincidental: if lace_master.pricePerMeter happens to equal the supplier quote, the number is right but rateSource/supplier attribution are still wrong.

confirmed.title: 'Weighted' average cost is an UNWEIGHTED _avg of per-lot WACs
confirmed.evidence: calculateWeightedAverage aggregates `_avg: { weightedAvgCost: true }` and uses it as existing average (lines 80-94); getCurrentWeightedAverage does the same (lines 276-286). A simple mean of per-lot WACs ignores lot quantities. The repo's decimal.js weightedAverage helper in backend/src/utils/currency.ts (called out by the guardrails doc) is not used.
confirmed.failureScenario: Lot A: 1000m @ ₹10, Lot B: 10m @ ₹100 → true WAC ₹10.89, _avg returns ₹55. Next receipt blends new cost against ₹55 → fabric_stock.weightedAvgCost corrupted; STOCK_REUSE costing option (checkStockAvailability reads weightedAvgCost) and stock valuation report all inherit the wrong figure.
confirmed.fixSketch: Compute existing value as SUM(quantityAvailable * weightedAvgCost) / SUM(quantityAvailable) (per-lot quantities), routing the math through utils/currency.ts weightedAverage.

verdict.reasoning: The code defect is exactly as claimed: WeightedAverageCostService.calculateWeightedAverage (backend/src/services/WeightedAverageCostService.ts:80-97) aggregates fabric_stock with `_avg: { weightedAvgCost: true }` — an UNWEIGHTED per-row mean that ignores quantityAvailable — and passes it to calculateNewAverageCost as the existing average; getCurrentWeightedAverage (lines 276-286) returns the raw unweighted _avg directly. Neither uses the decimal.js weightedAverage helper in backend/src/utils/currency.ts; rounding is raw-float Math.round(x*100)/100. Ironically, getStockValuation in the SAME file (lines 316-334) computes the quantity-weighted figure correctly — an F5 compute-twice divergence. HOWEVER, adversarial tracing shows the claimed corruption chain is currently unreachable: grep over backend/src and backend/scripts finds the only non-test importer of this service is fabric-stock.controller.ts (lines 890, 902), which calls only getStockValuation (the correct method). receiveStock, consumeStock, calculateWeightedAverage, and getCurrentWeightedAverage have ZERO production callers (unit tests cover only the pure static functions, not the _avg aggregate methods). All live writes to fabric_stock.weightedAvgCost bypass this service: manual create sets it to purchaseCost (fabric-stock.controller.ts:167,197), dyeing/printing set it to totalCostPerMeter (dyeing.controller.ts:1094, printing.controller.ts:1143), stock-routing.helper.ts:125 sets it to cost, and the manual-edit endpoint sets it directly. So checkStockAvailability (fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:231-289) does read weightedAvgCost for STOCK_REUSE costing as claimed, but the value it reads was never produced by the buggy blend. Note: the identical unweighted-mean anti-pattern IS live elsewhere — lace.controller.ts:1143 averages laceStock WACs by row count — which deserves its own finding.
verdict.failureScenario: Latent, not currently triggerable. If any caller is wired to receiveStock (its evident purpose — e.g., a future GRN/procurement receipt path), the repro is exact: fabric has 2+ existing AVAILABLE/RESERVED lots with differing stored WACs (Lot A 1000m with weightedAvgCost 10, Lot B 10m with weightedAvgCost 100). _avg returns (10+100)/2 = 55 instead of the true 10.89; the next receipt of 500m @ ₹12 blends against 55 → new lot stored at (1010*55 + 500*12)/1510 = ₹40.76/m instead of ₹11.26/m, and checkStockAvailability/STOCK_REUSE costing and valuation reports inherit it. Today, however, no route or script invokes receiveStock/calculateWeightedAverage/getCurrentWeightedAverage, so no production data can be corrupted by this file as shipped — the wrong number is computed nowhere at runtime.

confirmed.title: Order-item costing omits laceTotal from the subtotal that style costing includes
confirmed.evidence: recalculate: `subtotal = fabricTotal + trimsTotal + embroideryTotal + accessoriesTotal + cmtTotal + processingTotal + overheadsTotal` (lines 174-175) — no lace term. The style cost sheet's own subtotal includes laceTotal (styleCostingLaceItems.service.ts:419 `subtotal = ... + laceTotalNum`). Duplicated value-loss/markup pipeline diverges between the two.
confirmed.failureScenario: Style with ₹40/pc of lace: cost sheet totalProductCost includes lace, but order-item recalculation (triggered on CAD width selection) produces totalCostPerPiece ₹40+markup lower → margin/selling-price decisions on the order made from an understated cost.
confirmed.fixSketch: Include laceTotal (from baseCosting.laceTotal or style_costing_lace_items sum) in the order costing subtotal; ideally extract the subtotal→valueLoss→markup pipeline into one shared function (also used by styleCosting.controller:104-134, costing.service.ts:508-534, styleCostingLaceItems.service.ts:409-423).

verdict.reasoning: orderCosting.service.ts recalculate() builds its per-piece subtotal (lines 174-175) from fabricTotal + trimsTotal + embroideryTotal + accessoriesTotal + cmtTotal + processingTotal + overheadsTotal, copying each component from baseCosting (style_costing) at lines 151-171 — but never reads baseCosting.laceTotal, which exists as a dedicated Decimal column (schema.prisma:1691) and is maintained by styleCostingLaceItems.service.ts:389-436, whose own recompute is subtotal = fabric + trims + cmt + embroidery + accessories + laceTotalNum → totalProductCost/totalCostPerPiece. Lace is stored separately from trims (own table style_costing_lace_items, own column), so it cannot be captured via the copied trimsTotal; the no-baseCosting fallback (calculateTrimsCost, lines 367-379) counts only usageCategory === 'GARMENT_TRIM' BOM rows and also misses lace. The order_item_costing upsert (lines 198-235) has no lace field at all. The trigger is live: orderProductionStatus.controller.ts:76 calls selectCadAndRecalculate on CAD selection and line 129 calls recalculate directly. The omission is amplified by value loss (2%) and markup (15%) at lines 178-184 and inflates profitMargin at line 193; getCostingComparison (lines 428-502) then presents the gap as a legitimate CAD-driven cost difference, masking the bug.
verdict.failureScenario: Style has ₹40/pc of lace in style_costing_lace_items; style cost sheet totalProductCost includes it (₹40 × 1.02 × 1.15 ≈ ₹46.92 after value loss + markup). User selects a CAD width on the order item → orderProductionStatus.controller.ts:76 → selectCadAndRecalculate → recalculate() writes order_item_costing.totalCostPerPiece ≈ ₹46.92 lower than the true cost and a correspondingly overstated profitMargin. Selling-price/margin decisions on the order are made from the understated figure, and the costing-comparison endpoint reports the shortfall as a plausible CAD saving rather than an error.

confirmed.title: GSTR-1 silently excludes all OVERDUE invoices — under-reported GST liability and GSTR-1/GSTR-3B mismatch
confirmed.evidence: generateGSTR1 fetches invoices with `status: { not: InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE }` (comment claims 'Include PENDING, PARTIALLY_PAID, PAID'). GST liability arises on invoice issuance, not payment. Meanwhile generateGSTR3B (line 270) fetches invoices with NO status filter, and invoice.service.updateOverdueInvoices() (invoice.service.ts:747, exposed as POST /invoices/update-overdue for cron) bulk-flips every past-due PENDING/PARTIALLY_PAID invoice to OVERDUE.
confirmed.failureScenario: Invoice issued June 1, due June 15, unpaid. Cron marks it OVERDUE. GSTR-1 generated for June omits it entirely (b2b, b2cs, hsnSummary, totals) while GSTR-3B for the same period includes it → filed GSTR-1 under-reports outward tax and disagrees with GSTR-3B — the exact divergence that triggers GST department notices. Every invoice unpaid at filing time is silently dropped.
confirmed.fixSketch: Remove the status filter from the GSTR-1 invoice query (report on invoiceDate period regardless of payment status); add a shared 'reportable invoices' query used by both GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B so the two returns can never diverge.

verdict.reasoning: Every element of the finding checks out in the code. (1) backend/src/services/gstReport.service.ts:102 — generateGSTR1 queries `prisma.invoices.findMany({ where: { invoiceDate: {...}, status: { not: InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE } } })`, and every downstream section (b2b line 138, b2cs line 160, hsnSummary line 195, totals line 242) is built solely from that filtered list, so an OVERDUE invoice vanishes from all four sections. (2) The Prisma enum (schema.prisma:8657) is exactly {PENDING, PARTIALLY_PAID, PAID, OVERDUE} — OVERDUE is not a cancellation state; it is simply "issued and past due-date, unpaid", i.e. a fully valid taxable supply. There is no CANCELLED status the filter could have been intended for, so the exclusion has no legitimate interpretation. (3) Invoices reach OVERDUE through three paths: invoice.service.ts:747 updateOverdueInvoices() bulk-flips all past-due PENDING/PARTIALLY_PAID invoices (exposed as POST /api/invoices/update-overdue, invoice.routes.ts:42, intended for a daily cron); calculateStatus() (invoice.service.ts:212-221) returns OVERDUE whenever a payment recalculation happens past dueDate; and create() itself (invoice.service.ts:277) sets status='OVERDUE' at birth if the invoice is created after its dueDate — such an invoice never appears in GSTR-1 at all. (4) generateGSTR3B (gstReport.service.ts:270) fetches the same period with NO status filter, so its outward-supply taxable/cgst/sgst/igst figures include the invoices GSTR-1 dropped — a guaranteed GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B divergence for the same period. The report is also non-deterministic: the same period's GSTR-1 changes depending on when it is generated (before/after the overdue flip, and again after later payment flips the invoice to PAID). This is F5 (guard-the-wrong-thing: a payment-collection status used as a tax-liability filter) with a compliance-critical blast radius. No mitigating code exists — no snapshot, no alternate GSTR-1 path, no warning.
verdict.failureScenario: Concrete repro: create an invoice dated 2026-06-01 with dueDate 2026-06-15 for a GSTIN customer, record no payment. On any day after June 15 the daily cron hits POST /api/invoices/update-overdue (or any payment recalculation runs), flipping status to OVERDUE. On 2026-07-11 (GSTR-1 filing day) call GET /api/gst-reports/gstr1?fromDate=2026-06-01&toDate=2026-06-30 — the invoice is absent from b2b, b2cs, hsnSummary, and totals (taxable value, CGST/SGST/IGST all under-reported). Call GET /api/gst-reports/gstr3b for the same period — the invoice IS included in outwardSupplies.taxable. The two statutory returns disagree by exactly the tax on every past-due unpaid invoice; since B2B credit terms routinely exceed the ~11-day gap between period end and filing, a large fraction of each month's invoices is silently dropped. Edge case: an invoice created after its own dueDate (invoice.service.ts:277) is OVERDUE from creation and is excluded from GSTR-1 permanently unless later paid.

confirmed.title: TDS create: Zod schema, service input, and Prisma model are three different contracts — POST /api/tds can never succeed
confirmed.evidence: createTDSSchema fields (vendorId, section, panNumber, tanNumber, challanNumber, challanDate) do NOT exist on tds_entries (schema.prisma:9498), while the model's REQUIRED columns deductorName, deducteeName, tdsSection, financialYear, quarter are absent from the schema, so validateBody (tds.routes.ts:17) strips them even if sent. tds.service.ts:33 then spreads the validated body straight into prisma.tds_entries.create({ ...data }). Also deductionDate is optional in Zod but `new Date(data.deductionDate)` runs unconditionally (service line 36) → Invalid Date.
confirmed.failureScenario: Any POST /api/tds: body passes Zod, then Prisma throws Unknown argument `section`/`vendorId` (or missing required deductorName/financialYear/quarter) → 500 on every request. The TDS-entry feature is dead via the API; the interface TDSCreateInput in the service documents the fields the schema refuses to deliver.
confirmed.fixSketch: Rewrite createTDSSchema/updateTDSSchema to mirror tds_entries columns (deductorName, deducteeName, tdsSection, tdsRate, grossAmount, tdsAmount, netAmount, certificateNo, deductionDate required, financialYear, quarter, remarks); add a refine that tdsAmount ≈ grossAmount*tdsRate/100 and netAmount = grossAmount − tdsAmount.

verdict.reasoning: Three-way contract mismatch verified by reading all layers. (1) Zod createTDSSchema (backend/src/schemas/tds.schema.ts:24-39) defines vendorId/section/panNumber/tanNumber/challanNumber/challanDate and requires `section`; it omits deductorName/deducteeName/tdsSection/financialYear/quarter. (2) validateBody (validation.middleware.ts:28) does req.body = schema.parse(req.body) with a default-mode z.object, so unknown keys are stripped and `section` is enforced. (3) The frontend (frontend/src/types/tds.types.ts CreateTDSRequest, services/tds.service.ts createTDS) sends the Prisma-shaped fields (deductorName, tdsSection, financialYear, quarter...) and never sends `section` — so every real POST from the UI 400s at validation. (4) A hand-crafted Zod-conformant body is stripped to Zod's shape and spread by tds.service.ts:33-39 into prisma.tds_entries.create; the Prisma model tds_entries (schema.prisma:9498-9522) has no section/vendorId/pan/tan/challan columns and requires deductorName/deducteeName/tdsSection/financialYear/quarter → PrismaClientValidationError → 500. No path succeeds. Corroborating drift in the same module: updateTDSStatusSchema lacks certificateNo which the controller reads (tds.controller.ts:39) so it is silently stripped; Zod TDSStatusEnum (PENDING/DEDUCTED/DEPOSITED/FILED/CANCELLED) disagrees with the Prisma/frontend statuses (PENDING/CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED/VERIFIED) used by tds.service.ts getSummary and TDSList UI, so the UI's status transitions also 400. The claimed unconditional new Date(data.deductionDate) on an optional field (service line 36) is real but moot since create fails earlier. Minor correction to the claim: for actual frontend traffic the failure is a 400 at Zod (missing `section`), not a Prisma 500 — the 500 only occurs for Zod-conformant hand-crafted requests. Either way POST /api/tds can never succeed.
verdict.failureScenario: User opens the TDS page and submits the create form. Frontend createTDS() POSTs CreateTDSRequest {deductorName, deducteeName, tdsSection, tdsRate, grossAmount, tdsAmount, netAmount, deductionDate, financialYear, quarter} to /api/tds. validateBody(createTDSSchema) rejects it with 400 {details:[{field:'section',message:'Section is required'}]}. If a caller instead crafts a body satisfying Zod (adds section:'194C'), validation strips everything to the Zod shape and tds.service.create spreads it into prisma.tds_entries.create, which throws PrismaClientValidationError (Unknown argument `section`/`vendorId`; missing required deductorName, deducteeName, tdsSection, financialYear, quarter) → 500. No request shape can pass both Zod and Prisma, so TDS entry creation is impossible via the API; status updates from the UI (CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED/VERIFIED) also 400 against Zod's PENDING/DEDUCTED/DEPOSITED/FILED/CANCELLED enum.

confirmed.title: TDSStatusEnum (Zod) vs TDSStatus (Prisma) enum drift + updateStatus schema strips certificateNo the controller reads
confirmed.evidence: Zod: TDSStatusEnum = ['PENDING','DEDUCTED','DEPOSITED','FILED','CANCELLED']. Prisma (schema.prisma:9492): enum TDSStatus { PENDING, CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED, VERIFIED }. Only PENDING overlaps. Additionally tds.controller.ts:39 destructures `{ status, certificateNo }` from req.body but updateTDSStatusSchema (line 66) only allows status/challanNumber/challanDate/remarks — certificateNo is silently stripped. tds.service.getSummary (tds.service.ts:117-119) counts statuses 'CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED'/'VERIFIED' that the API can never set.
confirmed.failureScenario: PUT /api/tds/:id/status with status='DEDUCTED' (a Zod-approved value) → Prisma enum rejection → 500. The two statuses that actually exist (CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED, VERIFIED) are rejected by Zod with a 400. certificateNo sent with a status update is silently dropped (never persisted). TDS summary certificate counts are permanently 0.
confirmed.fixSketch: Make TDSStatusEnum mirror the Prisma TDSStatus enum exactly (the enum-drift ratchet's positive fix) and add certificateNo to updateTDSStatusSchema.

verdict.reasoning: Read all four files in the chain. (1) tds.schema.ts:14 TDSStatusEnum = ['PENDING','DEDUCTED','DEPOSITED','FILED','CANCELLED'] vs schema.prisma:9492 enum TDSStatus { PENDING, CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED, VERIFIED } — only PENDING overlaps. (2) tds.routes.ts:24-29 wires validateBody(updateTDSStatusSchema) on PUT /:id/status; validation.middleware.ts:28 replaces req.body with schema.parse() output (non-strict Zod strips unknown keys), so certificateNo — which tds.controller.ts:39 destructures and tds.service.ts:93-96 would persist — is always undefined and never written. Inverse drift too: challanNumber/challanDate/remarks pass Zod but the controller ignores them (and challanNumber/challanDate aren't even tds_entries columns; the model has certificateNo). (3) tds.service.ts:118-119 counts CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED/VERIFIED, statuses the API can never set (Zod 400s them), so summary certificate/verified counts are permanently 0; the tdsQuerySchema status filter (line 82) has the same wrong enum so listing can't filter by real statuses either. Bonus: createTDSSchema (vendorId/section/panNumber) matches neither the model nor the service's TDSCreateInput — required model fields deductorName/deducteeName/financialYear/quarter are stripped, so POST /api/tds always fails at Prisma. No guard anywhere in the chain mitigates any of this; the TDS write path appears never exercised end-to-end.
verdict.failureScenario: PUT /api/tds/:id/status with {"status":"DEDUCTED","certificateNo":"CERT-001"}: Zod accepts DEDUCTED and strips certificateNo; prisma.tds_entries.update({data:{status:'DEDUCTED'}}) throws PrismaClientValidationError (invalid TDSStatus) → 500. Sending the real statuses {"status":"CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED"} or {"status":"VERIFIED"} → Zod 400 "Invalid request data". The only value that round-trips is PENDING (the column default), so no meaningful status transition is possible via the API, certificateNo can never be persisted through this endpoint, and GET /api/tds/summary certificateReceived/verified counts stay 0 forever.

confirmed.title: createInvoiceSchema/updateInvoiceSchema require z.string().datetime() but InvoiceForm sends YYYY-MM-DD — invoice create/update from the UI 400s
confirmed.evidence: dueDate: z.string().datetime(...).transform(...) (lines 23-26; invoiceDate line 17, and updateInvoiceSchema lines 81-91). Frontend InvoiceForm.tsx builds dueDate/invoiceDate from <Input type="date"> state initialized `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` (lines 42-43) and submits them raw (lines 198-218). z.string().datetime() rejects date-only strings. Only fromDate/toDate of invoice.schema.ts are grandfathered in scripts/hooks/datetime-schema-baseline.json — dueDate/invoiceDate are not.
confirmed.failureScenario: User fills the Create Invoice form and submits → validateBody returns 400 'Invalid request data' (details: dueDate 'Invalid date format') on every attempt; edit-invoice PUT fails identically. This is precisely the datetime-schema bug class the smart-check hook exists to block.
confirmed.fixSketch: Replace z.string().datetime().transform(...) with z.coerce.date() for invoiceDate/dueDate in both schemas (and fromDate/toDate in invoiceQuerySchema while there).

verdict.reasoning: Traced the full chain. (1) backend/src/schemas/invoice.schema.ts: createInvoiceSchema.dueDate = z.string().datetime('Invalid date format').transform(...) (lines 23-26, required); invoiceDate same pattern but optional (17-21); updateInvoiceSchema repeats both (81-91). Zod's .datetime() requires a full ISO-8601 timestamp and rejects date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD'. (2) frontend/src/pages/InvoiceForm.tsx: invoiceDate state initialized new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0] (line 42), dueDate from a required <Input type="date"> (line 324); handleSubmit sends both raw in create (lines 198-207) and update (213-218); edit mode re-truncates loaded dates with .split('T')[0] (100-101), so both fields are ALWAYS present as date-only strings. (3) frontend/src/services/invoice.service.ts posts data unmodified; the axios request interceptor in frontend/src/lib/api.ts (43-81) only sets auth/Content-Type — no date conversion (transforms are commented out). (4) backend/src/routes/invoice.routes.ts wires validateBody(createInvoiceSchema) on POST / (line 52) and validateBody(updateInvoiceSchema) on PUT /:id (line 79); validation.middleware.ts validateBody (25-45) does schema.parse(req.body) and returns 400 'Invalid request data' on ZodError before the controller runs. (5) scripts/hooks/datetime-schema-baseline.json grandfathers only invoice.schema.ts fromDate/toDate (query schema), not dueDate/invoiceDate — this is an un-baselined instance of the exact datetime bug class the smart-check hook targets. No refuting guard exists anywhere in the chain.
verdict.failureScenario: Admin/Accounts user opens Create Invoice, selects customer and order (items auto-populate), sets Due Date via the date picker, submits. POST /api/invoices carries dueDate:"2026-08-20" and invoiceDate:"2026-07-21" (date-only). validateBody(createInvoiceSchema) fails z.string().datetime() on both fields and returns 400 {error:'Validation Error', message:'Invalid request data', details:[{dueDate:'Invalid date format'},...]}; the user sees 'Failed to create invoice' on every attempt. Editing an existing invoice hits the identical failure on PUT /api/invoices/:id (updateInvoiceSchema, same pattern, both dates always sent). The form has no code path that produces a valid ISO datetime, so invoice create/update from the UI is deterministically broken 100% of the time.

confirmed.title: Chart of Accounts update always returns 409 — controller reads accountCode that updateChartOfAccountSchema deliberately strips
confirmed.evidence: updateChartOfAccountSchema (chartOfAccounts.schema.ts:51, 'Note: accountCode is not updatable') omits accountCode; the route applies validateBody(updateChartOfAccountSchema) (chartOfAccounts.routes.ts:42). Controller updateAccount destructures accountCode from req.body (line 231) — always undefined post-validation — then `if (accountCode !== existingAccount.accountCode)` is always true, and `findFirst({ where: { accountCode: undefined, isActive: true } })` (lines 249-251): Prisma ignores undefined filters, so it matches the FIRST active account → ConflictError('Account code already exists') on every call.
confirmed.failureScenario: PUT /api/chart-of-accounts/:id with any valid body (e.g. rename an account) → 409 'Account code already exists' 100% of the time (any active account exists, including the one being edited). Editing the chart of accounts is impossible via the API.
confirmed.fixSketch: Drop accountCode from the controller's destructure and from the update data, and delete the code-uniqueness check (or gate it behind `accountCode !== undefined`).

verdict.reasoning: validateBody (backend/src/middleware/validation.middleware.ts:28) replaces req.body with schema.parse output, and updateChartOfAccountSchema (backend/src/schemas/chartOfAccounts.schema.ts:51-63) is a default-strip z.object that omits accountCode ('Note: accountCode is not updatable'). The route (backend/src/routes/chartOfAccounts.routes.ts:39-44) applies this schema, so in updateAccount (backend/src/controllers/chartOfAccounts.controller.ts:231) accountCode is always undefined. Line 248's guard `accountCode !== existingAccount.accountCode` compares undefined to a stored string → always true. Lines 249-251 then run findFirst({ where: { accountCode: undefined, isActive: true } }); Prisma ignores undefined filters, making it findFirst({ where: { isActive: true } }), which matches the first active account whenever any exists → ConflictError 409 (line 254) on every call. No passthrough, no alternate unvalidated route, no short-circuit exists. Secondary drift in same handler: schema accepts isActive but controller never reads it.
verdict.failureScenario: PUT /api/chart-of-accounts/:id on any non-system account with a valid body, e.g. { "accountName": "Renamed" } → validateBody strips everything but the allowed fields (accountCode was never allowed) → controller sees accountCode === undefined → guard at line 248 is true → findFirst({ isActive: true }) returns some active account (any real chart of accounts has at least one, including the row being edited) → 409 'Account code already exists'. Editing name/type/group/parent/description of any account fails 100% of the time; the only non-failing state is an empty/all-inactive chart_of_accounts table, in which case there is nothing to edit.

confirmed.title: Approved credit notes never touch invoice balanceAmount — over-collection possible and receivables overstated
confirmed.evidence: approve() only flips status DRAFT→APPROVED (lines 331-334); nothing in creditNote.service writes invoices.paidAmount/balanceAmount (grep confirms the only balance writers are invoice.service create/update/recordPayment). recordPayment validates strictly against invoice.balanceAmount (invoice.service.ts:633-635), and dashboard receivables sum balanceAmount (dashboard.controller.ts:420,506) — both blind to credit notes. The stored balance aggregate is maintained for payments but not for the other document that reduces the receivable.
confirmed.failureScenario: Invoice ₹10,000; approved credit note ₹2,000 for returned goods. balanceAmount still reads ₹10,000, so a ₹10,000 customer payment passes validation and is recorded → ₹2,000 over-collected with no flag; dashboard receivables and invoice status ('PENDING' on a fully-settled invoice) are wrong for every credited invoice.
confirmed.fixSketch: On credit-note approval (and reversal on cancel of an approved note), atomically decrement invoices.balanceAmount and recompute status in the same transaction — or better, derive effective balance as totalAmount − sum(payments) − sum(approved credit notes) everywhere it is checked.

verdict.reasoning: Traced the full document lifecycle in the actual code. (1) creditNote.service.ts approve() (lines 317-348) does exactly one write: `prisma.credit_notes.update({ data: { status: 'APPROVED' } })` — no transaction, no touch of the `invoices` table, no adjustment of paidAmount/balanceAmount. The controller (creditNote.controller.ts:81-87) is a pure pass-through, so nothing upstream compensates. (2) Repo-wide grep confirms the only writers of invoices.paidAmount/balanceAmount are in invoice.service.ts: create (sets balance=total, lines 371/411-426), update (recomputes balance only when totalAmount changes, line 571), and recordPayment (atomic increment/decrement, lines 678-679). invoice.service.ts references credit notes only once — to BLOCK deletion of an invoice with active credit notes (lines 604-611) — never to reduce the balance. (3) recordPayment validates strictly against the stored balanceAmount (lines 633-636) and even has a negative-balance abort at line 685, but both guards check a balance that credit notes never reduced, so a full-face-value payment on a credited invoice passes every check. (4) Dashboard receivables (dashboard.controller.ts:418-420, 504-506) and invoice summary (invoice.service.ts:718-735) sum the stored balanceAmount — all blind to approved credit notes. Notably, creditNote.create() DOES enforce that cumulative credit notes ≤ invoice total (lines 126-147), proving credit notes are meant to offset the invoice — the offset is simply never applied to the stored aggregate. This is exactly the F1 pattern: balanceAmount is maintained for one balance-reducing document type (payments) but not the other (credit notes).
verdict.failureScenario: Create invoice for ₹10,000 → balanceAmount = 10,000, status PENDING. Create credit note CN-00x for ₹2,000 against it (passes the ≤ invoice-total check) and approve it — approve() writes only status='APPROVED'. Invoice still shows balanceAmount = 10,000. Customer pays the correct net ₹8,000 → invoice sits at PARTIALLY_PAID with a phantom ₹2,000 balance forever (shows in overdue/receivables, may trigger dunning). Alternatively AR records the full ₹10,000 — recordPayment's guard (amount ≤ 10,000 stored balance) passes, atomic decrement lands at 0, status flips PAID → ₹2,000 over-collected from the customer with no flag anywhere. Dashboard totalReceivables/outstandingInvoices are overstated by the sum of every approved credit note in the system.

confirmed.title: updateInvoice mutates header money fields without recomputing GST columns, line items, or totals — header/items/GST-report divergence
confirmed.evidence: updateInvoice spreads the validated body (subtotal, taxAmount, totalAmount independently optional) straight into prisma update (lines 567-581). cgstAmount/sgstAmount/igstAmount and invoice_items are never recomputed; balance/status only recomputed when totalAmount is passed. The UI edit path (InvoiceForm.tsx:213-218) sends subtotal WITHOUT taxAmount/totalAmount. Also balanceAmount is computed from a pre-read paidAmount (line 570-571) outside any transaction/atomic op — the very read-compute-write pattern recordPayment (lines 642-695) was just fixed to avoid.
confirmed.failureScenario: (a) User edits an invoice and changes line amounts → PUT sends only subtotal → totalAmount, taxAmount, cgst/sgst/igst and invoice_items all keep old values → totalAmount ≠ subtotal + taxAmount and GSTR-1 (which reads header subtotal + cgst/sgst/igst) reports a taxable value with mismatched tax. (b) A payment recorded concurrently with an update that passes totalAmount → balanceAmount computed from the stale paidAmount clobbers the payment's decrement.
confirmed.fixSketch: Recompute taxAmount/totalAmount/cgst/sgst/igst server-side from subtotal (or from items) on any amount change instead of accepting them independently; wrap the update in a transaction and derive balanceAmount from the row read inside it.

verdict.reasoning: Every element of the finding checks out in the code. (1) updateInvoice (invoice.service.ts:561-589) builds `updateData = { ...data }` and writes it directly; there is no recomputation of taxAmount, totalAmount, cgstAmount/sgstAmount/igstAmount, and invoice_items are never touched — contrast createInvoice, which computes per-item GST and header cgst/sgst/igst inside a $transaction (lines ~297-383). (2) updateInvoiceSchema (invoice.schema.ts:80-112) makes subtotal, taxAmount, and totalAmount independently optional with no cross-field invariant (no refine that totalAmount = subtotal + taxAmount), and the controller (invoice.controller.ts:75) passes the body straight through. (3) The UI edit path is exactly as claimed: InvoiceForm.tsx:212-218 in edit mode sends only invoiceDate, dueDate, subtotal, remarks — even though the form lets the user edit line items and displays "GST will be calculated automatically... on save". So the shipped UI deterministically produces a header where subtotal is new but taxAmount/totalAmount/GST columns and invoice_items are stale. (4) GSTR-1/3B (gstReport.service.ts:138-249) sum header subtotal alongside header cgst/sgst/igst and totalAmount, and the HSN summary uses the stale invoice_items — so the report emits a taxable value whose tax columns no longer correspond to it. (5) The balance race is real: line 564 reads the invoice via getInvoiceById (plain read, no tx), line 570-571 computes balanceAmount = data.totalAmount - stale paidAmount, line 577 writes it as a plain assignment — while recordPayment (lines 642-695) was explicitly rewritten (per its own comment, "bug-hunt T1/F4") to use $transaction + atomic increment/decrement to avoid precisely this pattern. A payment committing between the read at 564 and the write at 577 has its balanceAmount decrement overwritten by the stale-based value, and status is recomputed from the stale paidAmount (line 574). No optimistic lock, version field, or transaction guards this.
verdict.failureScenario: (a) Deterministic, no race needed: invoice created with items — subtotal 10,000, taxAmount 500 (5% GST split into cgst 250 + sgst 250 in header and invoice_items), totalAmount 10,500. User opens the invoice in edit mode, changes a line quantity so items now sum to 20,000, saves. PUT body = { invoiceDate, dueDate, subtotal: 20000, remarks } (InvoiceForm.tsx:213-218). updateInvoice writes subtotal=20000; taxAmount stays 500, totalAmount stays 10,500, cgst/sgst stay 250/250, invoice_items rows still show the old amounts. Now totalAmount (10,500) ≠ subtotal + taxAmount (20,500), balanceAmount still reflects 10,500, and GSTR-1 reports taxable value 20,000 with tax 500 (2.5% effective) — header, items, and statutory report all diverge. (b) Race: invoice totalAmount 10,000, paidAmount 0. Admin A calls updateInvoice with totalAmount 12,000 — line 564 reads paidAmount=0. Before line 577 commits, a payment of 5,000 lands via recordPayment (atomic: paid=5,000, balance=5,000). A's update then writes balanceAmount = 12,000 - 0 = 12,000 and status from paidAmount=0 → PENDING. Result: paidAmount=5,000 but balanceAmount=12,000 (should be 7,000) — the payment's balance effect is clobbered and the invoice is dunned as fully unpaid.

confirmed.title: FG stock deduction on delivery-note creation is off-transaction, race-prone read-modify-write, and silently skipped
confirmed.evidence: Lines 311-361: prisma.delivery_notes.create is followed by a per-item loop that does findFirst({ where: { styleId, colorId: item.colorId || undefined, sizeId, quantity: { gte: item.quantity } } }) then update({ data: { quantity: fgStock.quantity - item.quantity } }). No $transaction, no { decrement }. If NO single finished_goods_stock row has >= item.quantity, the deduction is skipped entirely (comment at line 359: 'If no FG stock found, still allow dispatch'). If item.colorId is undefined, the colorId filter drops out and ANY color's stock row is deducted.
confirmed.failureScenario: (a) Two concurrent delivery notes for the same SKU both read quantity=100, both write 100-60=40 → one 60-pc deduction lost, FG stock overstated forever. (b) SKU spread across two rows of 50 each, dispatch 60 → gte:60 matches nothing → note created, zero deduction → stock overstated by 60 silently. (c) colorId omitted → wrong color's stock decremented. (d) Crash mid-loop → note exists with partial deductions.
confirmed.fixSketch: Wrap note creation + deductions in one prisma.$transaction; use quantity: { decrement } with an updateMany guard (quantity >= qty) per exact SKU, allocate across multiple rows, and fail (or explicitly flag) instead of silently skipping.

verdict.reasoning: backend/src/controllers/dispatch.controller.ts: grep confirms zero $transaction usage in the file. createDeliveryNote (line 261) creates the delivery note via global prisma (line 311), then loops items (338-361) doing findFirst({ styleId, colorId: item.colorId || undefined, sizeId, quantity: { gte: item.quantity } }) followed by update({ data: { quantity: fgStock.quantity - item.quantity } }) — an absolute-assignment read-modify-write on the global client, not { decrement }, with no tx, no lock, no retry. Line 359's comment explicitly permits skipping the deduction when no row matches. Line 345's `|| undefined` makes Prisma drop the colorId filter entirely, so any color's row for the style+size can be deducted. The FG loop has no try/catch (unlike the production_tracking block at 365-384), so a mid-loop failure 500s the client while the note persists with partial deductions. Additionally, deleteDeliveryNote (390-408) deletes PENDING notes without restoring the deducted FG stock, compounding the ledger drift.
verdict.failureScenario: (a) Two concurrent delivery notes for the same style/color/size: both findFirst read quantity=100; note A writes 100-60=40, note B writes 100-30=70 — B's write overwrites A's, 60 pcs of deduction lost, FG stock permanently overstated. (b) SKU stock held as two location rows of 50 each; dispatch 60 → gte:60 matches no single row → fgStock null → note created with ZERO deduction, silently (comment at line 359 sanctions this). (c) Frontend omits colorId (guard at line 340 doesn't require it) → colorId filter drops out → the first matching row of ANY color is decremented, corrupting a different SKU's stock. (d) DB error on the 3rd of 5 items → 500 returned, but the note and 2 partial deductions already persisted; a client retry double-deducts those 2 items. Also: deleting a PENDING note never restores the deducted stock.

confirmed.title: Deleting a delivery note never restores the FG stock deducted at creation
confirmed.evidence: deleteDeliveryNote (lines 390-411) only checks status === 'PENDING' and calls prisma.delivery_notes.delete (items cascade via onDelete: Cascade, schema.prisma:627). FG stock was decremented in createDeliveryNote, but there is no compensating increment anywhere on delete.
confirmed.failureScenario: User creates a delivery note for 200 pcs (FG stock -200), realizes it is wrong, deletes it while still PENDING (allowed). The 200 pcs vanish from finished_goods_stock permanently even though nothing shipped — hand-maintained balance drifts exactly like stock_levels did in the template bug.
confirmed.fixSketch: In deleteDeliveryNote, inside one transaction, re-increment finished_goods_stock per item before deleting; or derive FG on-hand from receipts minus dispatched delivery-note items instead of storing it.

verdict.reasoning: Traced both sides of the asymmetry in backend/src/controllers/dispatch.controller.ts. createDeliveryNote (lines 261-388): after creating the delivery_notes row with status 'PENDING' (line 318), it loops the items (lines 337-361) and for each finds a finished_goods_stock row with quantity >= item.quantity and writes `quantity: fgStock.quantity - item.quantity` (line 354) — a hand-maintained decrement at CREATION time, before anything ships. deleteDeliveryNote (lines 390-411): checks only `existing.status !== 'PENDING'` (line 402) — i.e., deletion is permitted exactly and only in the state where stock has already been deducted but nothing has been dispatched — then calls prisma.delivery_notes.delete (line 406). Items are removed via `onDelete: Cascade` on delivery_note_items.delivery_notes (schema.prisma line 627). There is no compensating finished_goods_stock increment anywhere in the delete path, and a repo-wide search shows the only files touching finished_goods_stock are dashboard.controller.ts (read), finishing.controller.ts (creates stock), dispatch.controller.ts (this decrement), saleOrder.service.ts (allocateStock/getAvailableStock — reads), and a cleanup script. No service, trigger, or workflow restores the quantity. Downstream, saleOrder.service.getAvailableStock (line 326) and allocateStock (line 247) make allocation decisions from this now-understated table, and createDeliveryNote's own `quantity: { gte: item.quantity }` filter (line 347) will silently skip deduction on the re-created note if the drifted stock row can no longer cover it — compounding the drift. Bonus confirmation of the F1 pattern: the decrement itself is also fire-and-forget (skipped entirely if no matching row, line 359 comment) and off-transaction, but the delete-without-restore alone is a concrete, reachable failure.
verdict.failureScenario: 1) FG stock exists: finished_goods_stock row for style S / color C / size Z has quantity 500. 2) User POSTs /dispatch/delivery-notes with an item {styleId:S, colorId:C, sizeId:Z, quantity:200} → note created with status PENDING, FG row updated 500 → 300 (line 354). 3) User realizes the note is wrong and calls DELETE /dispatch/delivery-notes/:id. The PENDING guard passes (line 402), the note and its items are deleted (line 406 + cascade). 4) No code path increments finished_goods_stock back: the table permanently shows 300 although 500 pcs are physically on hand and nothing shipped. Every create/delete cycle leaks the item quantity; sale-order allocation (allocateStock) and available-stock views then under-report, and a subsequent legitimate dispatch for 400 pcs finds no row with quantity >= 400 and silently skips deduction (line 342-359), so the ledger can drift in both directions.

confirmed.title: Over-dispatch guard checks only order-level totals (per-SKU map built but never used per-SKU) and races check-then-insert
confirmed.evidence: Lines 288-305: dispatchedMap is built keyed by styleId-colorId-sizeId, but the guard only compares totalAlreadyDispatched + totalNewDispatch > totalOrdered (sums across ALL SKUs). No per-SKU comparison against order_items. The whole check is a plain read before the create with no transaction/lock.
confirmed.failureScenario: Order: 100 pcs size M + 100 pcs size L. Dispatch 200 pcs of size M → total (200) <= 200 → passes; customer receives double M and zero L. Separately, two users creating notes concurrently both read the same 'already dispatched' figure and both pass, exceeding the order cap.
confirmed.fixSketch: Compare the dispatchedMap per SKU key against per-order_item quantities, and run validation + create inside one serializable transaction (or enforce with a DB constraint / SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the order).

verdict.reasoning: In createDeliveryNote (backend/src/controllers/dispatch.controller.ts:261-388), dispatchedMap is built per styleId-colorId-sizeId (lines 288-292) but its only consumer is Array.from(dispatchedMap.values()).reduce(...) at line 296 — a flat sum. The sole guard (line 299) compares totalAlreadyDispatched + totalNewDispatch > totalOrdered, where totalOrdered sums ALL order_items (line 295). No per-SKU comparison, and no check that dispatched items even belong to the order. The read (lines 271-285) and delivery_notes.create (line 311) use the global prisma client with no $transaction, lock, or DB constraint, so the check-then-insert races. Additionally, `if (order)` at line 276 silently skips validation when the order lookup fails. No downstream re-validation exists (FG stock deduction at 337-361 even tolerates missing stock by design).
verdict.failureScenario: Order: 100 pcs size M + 100 pcs size L (totalOrdered=200). POST delivery note with one item {sizeId: M, quantity: 200}: guard evaluates 0+200 > 200 → false → passes; note created with 200 M, customer gets double M and zero L, and L can never be dispatched without exceeding the cap. Concurrency: two users simultaneously create 200-pc notes; both read totalAlreadyDispatched=0, both pass 0+200<=200, both commit → 400 dispatched against a 200-pc order.

confirmed.title: SHIPPED production_tracking rows record the FULL delivery-note quantity once PER work order, inside an error-swallowing catch
confirmed.evidence: Lines 364-384: for every work_order of the order, production_tracking.create is called with quantityCompleted = items.reduce(... total of the whole delivery note ...). An order with N work orders gets N rows each carrying the full dispatched qty (N× inflation). The whole block is try/catch { logger.error(...) } — fire-and-forget, so failures silently lose tracking while the note still succeeds.
confirmed.failureScenario: Order with 3 work orders, delivery note of 500 pcs → three SHIPPED tracking rows of 500 each → any report summing production_tracking shows 1500 shipped for a 500-pc dispatch. Conversely, if the create throws, shipped tracking is silently absent.
confirmed.fixSketch: Attribute dispatched quantity to the correct work order (via order_items/WO linkage) or record one order-level event; include the write in the same transaction as the note instead of a swallowed catch.

verdict.reasoning: backend/src/controllers/dispatch.controller.ts:363-385 (createDeliveryNote) does exactly what the finding claims: after the delivery_notes.create, it runs prisma.work_orders.findMany({ where: { orderId } }) and, for EACH work order, calls prisma.production_tracking.create with quantityCompleted = items.reduce(sum of ALL delivery-note item quantities) (line 376) — the full note total, not the per-work-order share. Multiple work orders per order is a designed state (the query itself is findMany; production-run-split.service.ts and stockProductionOrder.service.ts create multiple WOs per order), so N work orders → N SHIPPED rows each carrying the full note quantity. The entire block is wrapped in try/catch { logger.error(...) } (lines 365, 382-384) with no rethrow and no shared transaction — the 201 response at line 387 is sent regardless, so a failed tracking create is silently lost. It also bypasses productionStatusService.createTracking's stage-transition validation by writing to prisma directly. Two refinements on the claimed BLAST RADIUS, from reading the consumers: (1) no current backend consumer SUMS production_tracking — productionStatus.service.ts:282-292 and orderProductionStatus.service.ts:341-349 both take only the LATEST row per WO (orderBy updateDate desc, take: 1) and report piecesInStage = latestTracking.quantityCompleted, so the literal "report shows 1500 for a 500-pc dispatch" summation does not occur in today's code; (2) the stored rows are still wrong per-row: a 100-pc work order gets a SHIPPED row of 500, which IS displayed as-is in per-WO tracking timelines (workOrder detail includes production_tracking; frontend ProductionTracking lists show quantityCompleted per row) and in the status services' 'shipped' figure — and with multiple partial delivery notes, the latest-row-only consumers show only the LAST note's quantity instead of the cumulative dispatched total. So the ledger corruption is real and permanent; the N-times-summed inflation is latent, waiting for any consumer that aggregates production_tracking.
verdict.failureScenario: Order with 3 work orders (e.g., 200/200/100 pcs, split via production-run-split). POST /api/dispatch/delivery-notes with items totalling 500 pcs → three production_tracking rows, each { productionStage: 'SHIPPED', quantityCompleted: 500 } — the 100-pc WO now shows 500 shipped in its tracking timeline, and any future aggregation over production_tracking counts 1500 shipped for a 500-pc dispatch. Second failure mode: dispatch 200 pcs today and 300 tomorrow → each WO gets two SHIPPED rows (200, then 300); the latest-row-only consumers (productionStatus/orderProductionStatus) report shipped = 300, not the cumulative 500. Third mode: if any create in the loop throws (FK, connection), the catch logs and the delivery note still returns 201 — SHIPPED tracking silently absent with no user-visible error.

confirmed.title: deliveryNumber/asnNumber generated by count() with no unique constraint — duplicates after any delete or concurrent create
confirmed.evidence: generateDeliveryNumber (lines 115-128) and generateASNNumber (130-142) use prisma.*.count({ startsWith: prefix }) + 1. schema.prisma: delivery_notes.deliveryNumber (line 641) has only @@index, no @unique; asn_applications.asnNumber (line 6462) likewise. Deletes of PENDING notes/ASNs are allowed, which shrinks the count.
confirmed.failureScenario: Same day: create DN-...-0001 and DN-...-0002, delete 0001, create again → count=1 → DN-...-0002 issued a second time and silently stored (no unique constraint to reject it). Two concurrent creates also both compute the same number. Duplicate dispatch document numbers = split ledger for a legal document.
confirmed.fixSketch: Add @unique on deliveryNumber/asnNumber and generate from a sequence table (or retry on P2002) instead of count().

verdict.reasoning: backend/src/controllers/dispatch.controller.ts lines 115-128 (generateDeliveryNumber) and 130-142 (generateASNNumber) derive the next document number from prisma.count({ startsWith: prefix }) + 1, with no transaction/lock around count-then-create (createDeliveryNote: count at line 309, create at 311; createASN: 740/742). backend/prisma/schema.prisma confirms delivery_notes.deliveryNumber (line 641) has only @@index([deliveryNumber]) (line 661) and NO @unique; asn_applications.asnNumber (line 6462) has neither @unique nor an index. (The @unique at schema line 5537 is on a different model, processing_delivery.) deleteDeliveryNote (controller lines 390-411) and deleteASN (880-901) hard-delete PENDING records, and new records are created with status PENDING (line 318), so the count can shrink after numbers are issued. There is no P2002 retry or app-level duplicate check — a duplicate number is silently persisted.
verdict.failureScenario: Delete path: same day, create note A (count=0 → DN-20260721-0001), create note B (count=1 → DN-20260721-0002), delete A (PENDING, allowed by deleteDeliveryNote), create note C → count=1 → DN-20260721-0002 issued a second time and stored without error since no unique constraint rejects it. Race path: two concurrent POSTs both await count() before either create commits, both compute the same number, both persist. Result: two live delivery notes (a legal dispatch document) sharing one deliveryNumber; search/lookup by deliveryNumber (e.g. line 196) conflates them. Identical mechanics for ASN numbers per order.

confirmed.title: recordPODSchema uses z.string().datetime() but DispatchPODForm sends YYYY-MM-DD — recording POD from the UI always 400s
confirmed.evidence: recordPODSchema.deliveryDate/customerGrnDate are z.string().datetime() (lines 261, 271). frontend/src/pages/DispatchPODForm.tsx:28 initializes deliveryDate = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0] ('2026-07-21') from an <input type='date'> and sends it verbatim (line 109). validateBody uses schema.parse (validation.middleware.ts:28) → ZodError → 400 'Invalid request data'. All 14 dispatch datetime fields are grandfathered in scripts/hooks/datetime-schema-baseline.json (lines 3-16), so the hook won't force the fix.
confirmed.failureScenario: Every POD submission from DispatchPODForm returns 400; deliveries can never be marked DELIVERED through the UI. Same class breaks lrDate/expectedDeliveryDate on assign-transport, requestedShipDate on ASN create, and fromDate/toDate date-range filters if sent as plain dates.
confirmed.fixSketch: Replace z.string().datetime() with z.coerce.date() (per the project guardrail's positive fix) across dispatch.schema.ts and remove the entries from the datetime baseline.

verdict.reasoning: Every link of the chain checks out in the actual code. (1) Route: backend/src/routes/dispatch.routes.ts:79-82 wires POST /delivery-notes/:id/record-pod through validateBody(recordPODSchema). (2) Schema: backend/src/schemas/dispatch.schema.ts:261 has `deliveryDate: z.string().datetime().optional()` and line 271 `customerGrnDate: z.string().datetime().optional()`; z.string().datetime() only accepts full ISO-8601 datetimes (e.g. 2026-07-21T00:00:00Z) and rejects date-only strings. (3) Middleware: backend/src/middleware/validation.middleware.ts:28 uses schema.parse (not safeParse-and-continue), so a ZodError returns 400 {message:'Invalid request data'}. (4) Frontend: frontend/src/pages/DispatchPODForm.tsx:28 initializes deliveryDate = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0] (YYYY-MM-DD), the field is an <input type='date'> (line 274) whose value stays YYYY-MM-DD, client-side validateForm (line 77) REQUIRES deliveryDate, and handleSubmit sends it verbatim in podData (line 109) via deliveryNoteService.recordPOD → api.post with no transformation (frontend/src/services/dispatch.service.ts:74-75). (5) The axios request interceptor in frontend/src/lib/api.ts does NOT transform request data — the decamelize/transform code is commented out (lines 64-74), only auth header + Content-Type are set. So deliveryDate is always present and always date-only → parse always throws → 400 before the controller runs. The controller (dispatch.controller.ts:574-644, `new Date(deliveryDate)` at 625) would happily accept a plain date, so the schema is strictly stricter than both producer and consumer. (6) Grandfathering confirmed: scripts/hooks/datetime-schema-baseline.json lines 3-16 list all 14 dispatch.schema.ts datetime fields (deliveryDate, customerGrnDate, lrDate, expectedDeliveryDate, requestedShipDate, fromDate, toDate, etc.), so the smart-check hook will not block or force a fix. The same z.string().datetime() pattern appears on assignTransportSchema (lrDate:247, expectedDeliveryDate:250), createASNSchema (requestedShipDate:161), and the query schemas (fromDate/toDate:103-104, 212-213), so the collateral claims are also code-accurate — those fail only if the sending UI uses date-only strings, which I did not individually verify per form.
verdict.failureScenario: User opens Record Proof of Delivery for an IN_TRANSIT delivery note (/manufacturing/dispatch → POD form). Delivery Date defaults to today as '2026-07-21' and cannot be omitted (client-side required + validateForm check). Clicking 'Record POD' POSTs {deliveryDate:'2026-07-21', receivedBy:'...', deliveryStatus:'DELIVERED', ...} to /api/dispatch/delivery-notes/:id/record-pod. validateBody runs recordPODSchema.parse; z.string().datetime() rejects '2026-07-21' (no time component) → ZodError → HTTP 400 'Invalid request data' with details [{field:'deliveryDate', message:'Invalid datetime'}]. The controller never executes, no dispatch_pods row is created, and the note stays IN_TRANSIT. This happens on 100% of UI submissions — deliveries can never be marked DELIVERED through this form. Filling the optional Customer GRN Date (also <input type='date'>) adds a second identical failure on customerGrnDate.

confirmed.title: Order-delete guard checks delivery status 'SHIPPED', which is not a DeliveryStatus value — in-transit deliveries don't block deletion
confirmed.evidence: order.service.ts:681: const shippedDeliveries = order.delivery_notes.filter((dn) => ['SHIPPED', 'DELIVERED'].includes(dn.status)); Prisma enum DeliveryStatus is PENDING | IN_TRANSIT | DELIVERED (schema.prisma:8517-8521) — 'SHIPPED' can never match, so only DELIVERED blocks. The delete then hard-deletes delivery_note_items and delivery_notes (lines 725-731).
confirmed.failureScenario: An order whose delivery note is IN_TRANSIT (goods physically on a truck, FG stock already deducted) passes canDelete → the order, its delivery notes, and their items are permanently deleted mid-shipment; the dispatch record for goods in transit disappears and FG stock is never reconciled.
confirmed.fixSketch: Change the guard to ['IN_TRANSIT', 'DELIVERED'] (or status !== 'PENDING').

verdict.reasoning: order.service.ts:681 filters delivery notes with ['SHIPPED','DELIVERED'].includes(dn.status), but delivery_notes.status is Prisma enum DeliveryStatus = PENDING | IN_TRANSIT | DELIVERED (schema.prisma:8517-8521; field at 649). 'SHIPPED' is a dead value — only DELIVERED blocks deletion, despite the comment "no shipped or delivered". The state is reachable: dispatch.controller.ts creates delivery notes without checking order status and never flips the order to DISPATCHED (order can remain PENDING with live delivery notes), deducts finished_goods_stock at creation (lines 337-358), and markInTransit (line 555) sets IN_TRANSIT. Separately, cancelOrder (order.service.ts:488-516) has no status guard at all, so any mid-shipment order can be set CANCELLED, satisfying the ['PENDING','CANCELLED'] check at line 670 and cancelling PENDING/IN_PRODUCTION work orders to satisfy line 675. hardDeleteOrder (705-778) then hard-deletes delivery_note_items and delivery_notes inside the tx, cascading delivery_notes_ext (transport/POD/cartons via onDelete: Cascade, schema.prisma:6515), with no reversal of the FG stock deduction anywhere in the path. TypeScript cannot catch it because .includes on a string-literal array accepts the enum value. Only mitigant: COMPLETED work orders block at line 675, but dispatch requires neither completed nor any work orders.
verdict.failureScenario: 1) Create an order (leave PENDING — dispatch doesn't require any other status — or cancel any order, since cancelOrder has no guard). 2) POST a delivery note with items via dispatch controller: FG stock is deducted immediately, note status PENDING. 3) Call mark-in-transit: status becomes IN_TRANSIT, goods physically dispatched. 4) Call the order hard-delete endpoint: canDeleteOrder passes (order PENDING/CANCELLED; work orders PENDING/CANCELLED or absent; IN_TRANSIT matches neither 'SHIPPED' nor 'DELIVERED'; no paid invoices; ASN pending). The transaction permanently deletes the delivery notes, their items, and cascaded transport/POD/carton records while goods are on the truck; the FG stock deduction is orphaned and never reconciled.

confirmed.title: sendOutSchema/receiveSchema validate a completely different API shape than the controller and frontend use — embroidery send-out and receive endpoints always 400
confirmed.evidence: embroideryStock.schema.ts:36 sendOutSchema requires {processorId, items[]}; embroideryStock.schema.ts:52 receiveSchema requires {sendOutId, items[{sendOutItemId, receivedQuantity}]}. But embroidery-stock.controller.ts:21-40 reads {sourceFabricStockId, embroideryId, supplierId, quantitySent, sentWidth, sendDate, agreedRate} and :75-91 reads {sendOutId, quantityReceived, receivedWidth, actualReturnDate}. Routes wire the schemas: embroidery-stock.routes.ts:36-37 `validateBody(sendOutSchema)` / `validateBody(receiveSchema)`. Frontend types confirm the controller shape (embroidery.types.ts:212 EmbroiderySendOutRequest, :229 EmbroideryReceiveRequest).
confirmed.failureScenario: User submits the Embroidery Send-Out form → POST /api/embroidery-stock/send-out with sourceFabricStockId etc. → 400 'processorId Required, items Required'. Receive form → 400 'items Required'. Even a schema-conforming payload would be stripped to fields the controller ignores, hitting its manual ValidationError. The entire embroidery send-out/receive workflow is dead.
confirmed.fixSketch: Rewrite sendOutSchema/receiveSchema to mirror SendOutDTO/ReceiveDTO in embroidery-stock.service.ts (sourceFabricStockId, embroideryId cuid-tolerant, supplierId, quantitySent positive, sentWidth, sendDate coerce.date, agreedRate; sendOutId, quantityReceived positive, receivedWidth, actualReturnDate, etc.).

verdict.reasoning: Traced all four layers and they agree with the finding. (1) Route wiring: backend/src/routes/embroidery-stock.routes.ts:36-37 attaches `validateBody(sendOutSchema)` to POST /send-out and `validateBody(receiveSchema)` to POST /receive. (2) Schemas: backend/src/schemas/embroideryStock.schema.ts:36-46 sendOutSchema requires `processorId` (uuid) and `items[]` (min 1, each with embroideryId/quantity); :52-69 receiveSchema requires `sendOutId` plus `items[]` (each with sendOutItemId/receivedQuantity). (3) Controller: backend/src/controllers/embroidery-stock.controller.ts:21-40 destructures {sourceFabricStockId, embroideryId, supplierId, quantitySent, sentWidth, sendDate, agreedRate, ...} and manually throws ValidationError if any is missing; :75-91 destructures {sendOutId, quantityReceived, receivedWidth, actualReturnDate, ...} with the same manual guard. (4) Frontend: frontend/src/types/embroidery.types.ts:212-241 EmbroiderySendOutRequest/EmbroideryReceiveRequest match the CONTROLLER shape (no processorId, no items[]), and frontend/src/services/embroidery.service.ts:94/:102 posts exactly those payloads to the two endpoints. The middleware (backend/src/middleware/validation.middleware.ts:25-45) does `req.body = schema.parse(req.body)` and returns 400 on ZodError — Zod objects are strip-mode by default, so there is no passthrough. Therefore: the real frontend payload fails schema.parse (missing processorId/items on send-out, missing items on receive) → 400 'Invalid request data'. Conversely, a payload crafted to satisfy the schema is stripped to {processorId, items, ...}, so the controller's destructured fields are all undefined and its own guard at :36/:90 throws ValidationError → also 400. There is no code path to a 2xx on either endpoint; the schema appears written for a different (processor/multi-item challan) design than the implemented single-fabric-roll service (embroideryStockService.sendOut takes sourceFabricStockId etc.). No second unvalidated route to these controllers exists that could bypass the schema.
verdict.failureScenario: Repro 1 (real UI flow): open /embroidery-stock/send-out, fill the form; frontend posts {sourceFabricStockId, embroideryId, supplierId, quantitySent, sentWidth, sendDate, agreedRate} to POST /api/embroidery-stock/send-out → sendOutSchema.parse fails → 400 {error:'Validation Error', details:[{field:'processorId',...},{field:'items',...}]}. Repro 2: /embroidery-stock/receive posts {sendOutId, quantityReceived, receivedWidth, actualReturnDate} → receiveSchema.parse fails on missing items[] → 400. Repro 3 (proves no workaround): POST a schema-conforming body {processorId:<uuid>, items:[{embroideryId:<cuid>, quantity:5}]} → passes Zod, req.body is replaced with only those keys → controller line 36 finds sourceFabricStockId et al. undefined → throws ValidationError → 400 again. Every request to these two endpoints returns 400; the fabric-level embroidery send-out/receive workflow cannot succeed.

confirmed.title: SampleStatusEnum drifts from Prisma SampleStatus — valid workflow statuses 400, Zod-accepted statuses 500 at the DB
confirmed.evidence: sample.schema.ts:16 allows PENDING, RECEIVED, REVISION_REQUIRED (not in Prisma) and omits REQUESTED, SUBMITTED, FEEDBACK_PENDING, REVISION_NEEDED, APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS (prisma/schema.prisma:8852 SampleStatus). Used by updateSampleSchema:106, updateSampleStatusSchema:126, sampleQuerySchema:221. recordFeedbackSchema:194 additionally allows 'REVISION_REQUIRED' which is not a Prisma value, while the controller (sample.controller.ts:929) checks 'REVISION_NEEDED'. Controller's own status logic (sample.controller.ts:637, 643) uses APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS/SUBMITTED which Zod rejects.
confirmed.failureScenario: PATCH /api/samples/:id/status with status='APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS' (a real buyer outcome) → 400. POST /:id/feedback with status='REVISION_REQUIRED' passes Zod, then prisma.samples.update throws invalid enum → 500 and revisionRequired flag logic is bypassed. GET /api/samples?status=FEEDBACK_PENDING → 400.
confirmed.fixSketch: Align SampleStatusEnum (and recordFeedbackSchema's status subset) with the Prisma SampleStatus enum values exactly.

verdict.reasoning: Zod SampleStatusEnum (backend/src/schemas/sample.schema.ts:16-24) = {PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SENT, RECEIVED, APPROVED, REJECTED, REVISION_REQUIRED} while Prisma SampleStatus (backend/prisma/schema.prisma:8852-8862) = {REQUESTED, IN_PROGRESS, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, SENT, FEEDBACK_PENDING, REVISION_NEEDED, APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS} — only 4 values overlap. samples.status is typed as the Prisma enum (schema.prisma:1468), so invalid values throw at the DB layer. Routes enforce the Zod schemas (sample.routes.ts:77 validateQuery(sampleQuerySchema), :101 validateBody(updateSampleStatusSchema), :163 validateBody(recordFeedbackSchema)); validation.middleware.ts:28 replaces req.body with the parse result and returns 400 on enum failure, and .passthrough() does not relax declared enum fields. There is NO mapping layer: sample.controller.ts passes status verbatim to prisma.samples.update at :542, :626, :925. The controller's own logic branches on APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS/SUBMITTED (:637, :643) — dead code, since the validator 400s those values before the controller runs. The mismatch is self-inflicted at runtime: the app itself sets REQUESTED on create (:173), FEEDBACK_PENDING on receive (:878), and dashboards filter on SUBMITTED/FEEDBACK_PENDING/APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS (:358, :1080, :1126), so real rows carry statuses that sampleQuerySchema:221 rejects as query filters. recordFeedbackSchema:194 additionally accepts 'REVISION_REQUIRED' (not in Prisma) while the controller's revisionRequired flag at :929 checks 'REVISION_NEEDED' — so the only revision value Zod accepts both 500s at Prisma and bypasses the flag. Every element of the claimed finding traces to concrete code; no refuting guard exists.
verdict.failureScenario: (1) PATCH /api/samples/:id/status with {status:'APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS'} (or SUBMITTED/FEEDBACK_PENDING/REVISION_NEEDED/REQUESTED) → validateBody 400 'Invalid request data' — these workflow statuses can never be set via the status endpoint, and the controller's date-setting logic for them (sample.controller.ts:637,643) is unreachable. (2) POST /api/samples/:id/feedback with {status:'REVISION_REQUIRED'} → passes recordFeedbackSchema, prisma.samples.update at :925 throws invalid-enum → 500; revisionRequired flag logic (:929, checks 'REVISION_NEEDED') is bypassed. (3) GET /api/samples?status=FEEDBACK_PENDING (a status the app itself writes at :878, and the default REQUESTED written at :173) → validateQuery 400, making real DB rows un-filterable. (4) PUT /api/samples/:id or PATCH /:id/status with Zod-accepted 'PENDING' or 'RECEIVED' → 500 at Prisma. Same drift pattern also affects SampleTypeEnum (schema.ts:14 DEVELOPMENT/FIT/... vs Prisma SampleType FIT_SAMPLE/PP_SAMPLE/... at schema.prisma:8864) — creates with any Zod-valid sampleType would fail at the DB.

confirmed.title: embroidery_master uses cuid IDs but routes validate params as UUID — GET/PUT/DELETE /api/embroidery/:id and /by-embroidery/:embroideryId reject every real record
confirmed.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:2138 `embroidery_master id @default(cuid())`. embroidery.routes.ts:49/56/63 use validateParams(idParamSchema) where common.schema.ts:15 is `z.string().uuid()`. embroidery-stock.routes.ts:52 uses embroideryIdParamSchema (common.schema.ts:52, also uuid-only). embroideryStock.schema.ts:22 even documents 'embroideryId accepts CUID (embroidery_master uses @default(cuid()))' — but the param schemas were never fixed. Frontend calls `/embroidery/${id}` with the cuid (embroidery.service.ts:46, 63, 71).
confirmed.failureScenario: User opens an embroidery design detail page or clicks Edit/Delete: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/embroidery/c<cuid> → validateParams 400 'Invalid ID' before the controller runs. Same for GET /api/embroidery-stock/by-embroidery/:embroideryId. Detail, update, delete and stock-by-design views all fail for every design created with the cuid default.
confirmed.fixSketch: Use a cuid-or-uuid param schema (reuse the isValidIdFormat refinement from embroideryStock.schema.ts) for embroidery :id and :embroideryId params.

verdict.reasoning: All links in the chain verified in code. (1) backend/prisma/schema.prisma:2138 — `embroidery_master.id String @id @default(cuid())`, and the create path (backend/src/controllers/embroidery.controller.ts:110) does not supply an explicit id, so every design created through POST /api/embroidery gets a CUID ("c" + ~24 base36 chars, no dashes). (2) backend/src/routes/embroidery.routes.ts:49/56/63 wrap GET/PUT/DELETE /:id with validateParams(idParamSchema), and common.schema.ts:14-16 defines idParamSchema as `z.string().uuid('Invalid ID')` — Zod's uuid() regex requires the 8-4-4-4-12 dashed hex form and rejects CUIDs. (3) validation.middleware.ts:79-101 shows validateParams returns 400 'Invalid URL parameters' on ZodError before the controller runs — no fallback. (4) embroidery-stock.routes.ts:52 validates /by-embroidery/:embroideryId with embroideryIdParamSchema (common.schema.ts:51-53, also uuid-only). (5) The frontend passes the raw record id: frontend/src/services/embroidery.service.ts lines 46, 63, 71 call `/embroidery/${id}` and line 158 calls `/embroidery-stock/by-embroidery/${embroideryId}`. (6) The team already knew the ID is a CUID elsewhere: embroideryStock.schema.ts:17-23 has an isValidIdFormat helper explicitly commented 'embroideryId accepts CUID (embroidery_master uses @default(cuid()))' — used only for body validation of send-out items, never applied to the param schemas. Refutation attempts failed: there is no id override at create, no CUID-tolerant param schema on these routes, and no controller-level bypass. Note the asymmetry proving the operational impact: list (GET /), search, and stock send-out creation work fine (they don't validate a :id param, or use the CUID-aware body schema), so designs can be created and listed but never opened, edited, deleted, or queried by design — a classic F3 contract drift between the ID generator and the param validator.
verdict.failureScenario: Create an embroidery design via the UI (POST /api/embroidery succeeds, id = e.g. "cmb3x9k2l0000abcdxyz12345"). Then click the design to view/edit: frontend calls GET /api/embroidery/cmb3x9k2l0000abcdxyz12345 → validateParams(idParamSchema) → z.string().uuid() fails → 400 {error:'Validation Error', message:'Invalid URL parameters', details:[{id:'Invalid ID'}]} before getEmbroideryById runs. Identical 400 for PUT (edit save) and DELETE, and for GET /api/embroidery-stock/by-embroidery/:embroideryId. Every record created with the cuid default is affected — detail, update, delete, and stock-by-design views are all unreachable.

confirmed.title: Partial embroidery receipts overwrite quantityReceived instead of accumulating, with no over-receipt guard — send-out ledger corrupts and stock inflates
