confirmed.evidence: receive() sets `quantityReceived: data.quantityReceived` (line 315) — plain overwrite of the stored aggregate — then computes status from only the latest batch: `totalReceived = data.quantityReceived + (data.quantityDamaged||0)` vs quantitySent (lines 308-310). The status guard (line 239) blocks only RECEIVED/CANCELLED, so PARTIALLY_RECEIVED can be received again indefinitely; each call creates a new fabric_stock lot (line 254) and increments stock_levels (line 305), and resultFabricStockId (line 324) is overwritten to the newest lot. No check that cumulative receipts ≤ quantitySent.
confirmed.failureScenario: Send 100m; receive 60m → PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, quantityReceived=60. Receive remaining 40m → quantityReceived overwritten to 40, totalReceived=40 < 100 → status stays PARTIALLY_RECEIVED forever, record claims only 40m ever returned while 100m of stock exists. A user 'correcting' a receipt by re-submitting doubles fabric_stock and stock_levels silently; receiving 500m against a 100m send-out is accepted.
confirmed.fixSketch: Accumulate: quantityReceived: { increment: qty } (same for quantityDamaged), compute status from the accumulated total, and reject receipts that would exceed quantitySent. Consider a child receipts table since multiple result lots are created.

verdict.reasoning: Every element of the claim is verbatim in backend/src/services/embroidery-stock.service.ts: the status guard at line 239 rejects only RECEIVED/CANCELLED, so a PARTIALLY_RECEIVED send-out passes and receive() can run repeatedly; line 315 writes `quantityReceived: data.quantityReceived` as a plain overwrite (no increment, no read-modify-write of the prior aggregate); lines 308-310 derive status solely from the latest batch (`totalReceived = data.quantityReceived + (data.quantityDamaged||0)` vs quantitySent), so cumulative partials can never reach RECEIVED; there is no check anywhere that cumulative receipts <= quantitySent (over-receipt of any size is accepted); each call unconditionally creates a new fabric_stock lot (line 254), a fabric_stock_transaction (line 285), and increments stock_levels via syncStockLevelQuantity (line 305); and line 324 overwrites resultFabricStockId to the newest lot, orphaning traceability to prior lots. cancelSendOut (line 480) only works on status SENT, so a corrupted PARTIALLY_RECEIVED record cannot even be unwound. One material caveat the finding missed: the HTTP path is currently dead because of a separate F3 drift — the route (embroidery-stock.routes.ts:37) validates with receiveSchema (embroideryStock.schema.ts:52-69), which requires an items[] array of {sendOutItemId, receivedQuantity}, while the controller (embroidery-stock.controller.ts:75-98) and the frontend (embroidery.types.ts:229-241) use a flat {sendOutId, quantityReceived, receivedWidth, actualReturnDate} shape; validateBody (validation.middleware.ts:28) strictly replaces req.body, so a flat body 400s at Zod ('items Required') and an items-shaped body 400s at the controller's own required-field check. So the service bug is real and unguarded, but is presently masked by an endpoint-breaking contract-drift bug; the moment the schema is aligned to the controller (the obvious fix for the 400), the F1 corruption becomes live with no protection.
verdict.failureScenario: Direct service call (script/seed/future aligned route): sendOut 100m -> fabric_stock decremented 100, status SENT. receive({quantityReceived: 60}) -> new 60m lot, stock_levels +60, quantityReceived=60, status PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. receive({quantityReceived: 40}) -> guard at line 239 passes (status is PARTIALLY_RECEIVED), quantityReceived OVERWRITTEN to 40 (line 315), totalReceived=40 < 100 (lines 308-310) so status stays PARTIALLY_RECEIVED forever; ledger claims 40m returned while 100m of embroidered stock exists, and resultFabricStockId now points only at the 40m lot. Re-submitting the same receipt doubles fabric_stock and stock_levels silently; receive({quantityReceived: 500}) against the 100m send-out is accepted (no cumulative-vs-sent check exists). Caveat on today's reachability: POST /api/embroidery-stock/receive cannot currently reach the service at all — receiveSchema requires an items[] shape the controller and frontend don't use, so every request 400s (flat body fails Zod; items body fails the controller's required-field check). The repro therefore requires a direct service invocation today, and becomes UI-reachable the moment the schema/controller drift is fixed.

confirmed.title: Measurement schemas validate fields the controller never reads and strip the fields it does read — both measurement endpoints are dead
confirmed.evidence: updateMeasurementsSchema:136 requires items {measurementPointId (uuid), targetValue, tolerance}, but the controller (sample.controller.ts:731-739) maps m.sizeId, m.measurementPoint, m.specValue, m.actualValue — all stripped by the non-passthrough z.object. recordActualMeasurementsSchema:150 requires {measurementPointId, actualValue} while the controller (sample.controller.ts:779-786) reads m.id for findUnique/update. validateBody replaces req.body with the parsed result (validation.middleware.ts:28).
confirmed.failureScenario: PUT /api/samples/:id/measurements with the controller/DB shape ({measurementPoint, specValue}) → 400 'measurementPointId Required'. With the schema shape → measurementPoint/specValue stripped → createMany receives undefined required columns → Prisma error → 500 (transaction rolls back, so at least no data loss). PATCH /:id/measurements/actual: m.id is stripped → prisma findUnique({where:{id: undefined}}) throws → 500 — and because the loop (lines 779-794) is not in a transaction, a mid-loop failure leaves some measurements PASS/FAIL-stamped and others untouched (F4).
confirmed.fixSketch: Rewrite both schemas to match the controller/DB shape (id/sizeId/measurementPoint/specValue/actualValue/tolerance), and wrap the recordActualMeasurements loop in one $transaction.

verdict.reasoning: Traced end-to-end. (1) Routes: backend/src/routes/sample.routes.ts:117-134 apply validateBody(updateMeasurementsSchema) to PUT /:id/measurements and validateBody(recordActualMeasurementsSchema) to PATCH /:id/measurements/actual, and validation.middleware.ts:28 does `req.body = schema.parse(req.body)` — so the controller only ever sees the parsed (stripped) result. (2) updateMeasurementsSchema (sample.schema.ts:136-144) is a non-passthrough z.object whose items require measurementPointId (uuid) and allow only targetValue/tolerance; the controller (sample.controller.ts:731-739) maps m.sizeId, m.measurementPoint, m.specValue, m.actualValue, m.tolerance into sample_measurements.createMany — and the Prisma model (schema.prisma:5731-5746) has measurementPoint (String) and specValue (Decimal) as REQUIRED columns, so the schema-shaped payload yields createMany with undefined required fields → PrismaClientValidationError → 500. It is an array-form $transaction([deleteMany, createMany]) so the deleteMany rolls back — no data loss, endpoint just always fails. (3) recordActualMeasurementsSchema (150-159) requires {measurementPointId, actualValue} per item and strips id; the controller loop (779-794) reads m.id → prisma.sample_measurements.findUnique({where:{id: undefined}}) throws on the FIRST iteration. One refinement to the claim: because id is stripped from EVERY item, the loop dies uniformly at iteration 1, so the feared partial PASS/FAIL stamping cannot actually occur from this bug — the un-transactioned loop (F4) is latent and would only bite after the schema is fixed. (4) The real client confirms both endpoints are dead: frontend/src/services/sample.service.ts:106 sends SampleMeasurementInput ({sizeId, measurementPoint, specValue, actualValue, tolerance} — types/sample.types.ts:83-89) and :117 sends {id, actualValue}. Neither shape contains measurementPointId, so every frontend call 400s at validation ("measurementPointId Required") and never reaches the controller. There is no code path by which either endpoint can succeed.
verdict.failureScenario: Concrete repro A (the real frontend path): sampleService.updateMeasurements() sends PUT /api/samples/:id/measurements with items {measurementPoint:"Chest", specValue:40, tolerance:0.5} → updateMeasurementsSchema rejects (measurements.0.measurementPointId Required) → 400 "Invalid request data"; same 400 for sampleService.recordActualMeasurements() sending {id, actualValue}. Repro B (schema-compliant payload): PUT with {measurementPointId:"<uuid>", targetValue:40} passes validation but the parse strips everything the controller maps → createMany receives measurementPoint:undefined, specValue:undefined (required columns) → PrismaClientValidationError → 500 (array $transaction rolls back deleteMany, so no data loss). PATCH with {measurementPointId, actualValue} → m.id is undefined for every item → findUnique({where:{id:undefined}}) throws on iteration 1 → 500 before any update (partial-write risk is latent only). Net: both measurement endpoints fail 100% of the time regardless of payload shape.

allFindings.title: updateOrderSchema and updateOrderStatusSchema require body `id` that the frontend never sends → PUT /orders/:id and PATCH /orders/:id/status 400 on every call
allFindings.evidence: order.schema.ts:56-58 `updateOrderSchema = createOrderSchema.partial().extend({ id: z.string().uuid() })` and :61-65 `updateOrderStatusSchema = z.object({ id: z.string().uuid(), status, reason })`. Routes wire these via validateBody (order.routes.ts:39-45). The controller reads id from req.params only (order.controller.ts:703, 499). Frontend OrderForm.tsx:918-942 builds orderData WITHOUT id and calls `updateOrder(id, orderData)`; frontend type UpdateOrderStatusRequest = { status } only (order.types.ts:228-230).
allFindings.failureScenario: User edits any order in the UI and clicks Save → validateBody parses body, `id` missing → 400 'Invalid request data' every time; order editing (and any status PATCH from the typed client) is completely broken.
allFindings.fixSketch: Remove `id` from both body schemas (it belongs to params, already validated by idParamSchema); alternatively make it optional. Also drop unused `reason`/`status` extras or wire them through.

allFindings.title: updateOrder replaces order items via sequential global-prisma deletes/creates with no transaction; totals written in a separate later update
allFindings.evidence: order.controller.ts:786-801: `prisma.order_item_breakup.deleteMany(...)`, then `prisma.order_items.deleteMany(...)`, then a for-loop of `prisma.order_items.create(...)`, then per-work-order breakup deletes/creates (803-841), and only at :847 the order header (totalQuantity/totalAmount) is updated — all on the global client, no $transaction.
allFindings.failureScenario: Item replacement where the 2nd create fails (e.g., duplicate (colorId,sizeId) breakup → P2002, or bad styleId → P2003): breakups and items are already deleted, order is left with 0/partial items, header totals still show the old values, and work_orders.orderItemId has been set NULL by the delete — silent corruption with no rollback.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap the whole item-replacement + work-order sync + header-total update in one prisma.$transaction(tx => ...) and use tx.* throughout.

allFindings.title: Order status route bypasses the state machine: service.updateStatus validates transitions, but the wired controller does a raw update allowing any transition
allFindings.evidence: order.service.ts:446-482 `updateStatus` calls `validateTransition('order', existing.status, status, userRole)` — but order.routes.ts:40-45 wires PATCH /:id/status to controller `updateOrderStatus` (order.controller.ts:498-523) which does `prisma.orders.update({ data: { status } })` with no transition check. Similarly `deleteOrder` (order.controller.ts:888-908) cancels without any status guard.
allFindings.failureScenario: PATCH /orders/:id/status with status=PENDING on a DISPATCHED order (or CANCELLED→COMPLETED) succeeds; DELETE /orders/:id cancels a DISPATCHED/COMPLETED order, releasing lace allocations and cancelling work orders for goods already shipped.
allFindings.fixSketch: Make the controller delegate to orderService.updateStatus (which runs validateTransition) and add a status guard to deleteOrder/cancelOrder; delete the dead duplicate path.

allFindings.title: RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD clone guard checks the wrong row → duplicate CAD clones when a style appears in multiple orders
allFindings.evidence: order.controller.ts:557-577: `findFirst({ where: { purpose: 'RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION', styleFabric: {...styleId} } })` returns ANY raw-mat CAD for the style, then skips only if `existingRawMat.clonedFromOrderId === id`. With no state machine (orders-3), status can be toggled off/on IN_PRODUCTION repeatedly.
allFindings.failureScenario: Order A (style S) confirmed → clones CADs. Order B (style S) confirmed → clones again. Order A toggled back to PENDING and re-confirmed → findFirst may return B's row, guard fails (clonedFromOrderId !== A), A clones a THIRD set → duplicate RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD rows inflate downstream material calculations. Loop also runs off-transaction with per-item catch-swallow (:669-681).
allFindings.fixSketch: Query `findFirst({ where: { purpose: 'RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION', clonedFromOrderId: id, styleFabric: {...} } })` — i.e. guard on THIS order's clones — and wrap the clone loop in a transaction.

allFindings.title: Two divergent order-creation implementations; the live route uses a racy non-atomic order-number generator while an atomic one exists unused
allFindings.evidence: Controller createOrder (order.controller.ts:34-336) and orderService.createWithItems (order.service.ts:107-289) both implement number-generation + totals + item creation but diverge: the service uses `generateAtomicOrderNumber()` (order.service.ts:826-828), filters 0-qty breakups and auto-creates work orders; the controller uses local `generateOrderNumber()` (order.controller.ts:1141-1165, findFirst+parseInt+1) and keeps 0-qty breakups. POST /orders is wired to the controller.
allFindings.failureScenario: Two users submit orders in the same instant → both read the same last orderNumber → same ORD-yyyymm-#### → orders.orderNumber @unique (schema.prisma:1123) → P2002 → 500 on a normal create. Meanwhile any caller of createWithItems gets different behavior (work orders yes/no, breakup filtering).
allFindings.fixSketch: Delete the controller's local generator and creation logic; route POST /orders through orderService.createWithItems (which already uses generateAtomicOrderNumber), moving the cost-sheet validation/snapshot logic into the service.

allFindings.title: orders.totalQuantity/totalAmount are stored aggregates that can be set directly from the request body, drifting from SUM(order_items)
allFindings.evidence: order.controller.ts:842-845: `else if (totalQuantity !== undefined) { updateData.totalQuantity = totalQuantity; }` — header quantity overwritten without touching items; totalAmount not recalculated. Reports aggregate the stored columns: getOrderStatisticsByCustomer (order.controller.ts:1094-1097 `_sum: { totalQuantity, totalAmount }`) and getStatistics (order.service.ts:804-807).
allFindings.failureScenario: OrderForm always sends totalQuantity; when an order has BOM/MRP deps, items are not sent, so PUT sets header totalQuantity=800 while order_items still sum to 500 and totalAmount stays priced at 500 → customer statistics and order lists report drifted piece counts vs amounts.
allFindings.fixSketch: Never accept header totals from the client: recompute totalQuantity/totalAmount from order_items (or forbid changing quantity without editing items) and derive statistics from order_items aggregates.

allFindings.title: Post-create side effects (work orders, cost-sheet snapshots) run off-transaction with catch-and-continue
allFindings.evidence: order.service.ts:219-234: work-order auto-creation loop after the tx, `catch { logError(...) }` — order committed, work orders silently missing. Same pattern in controller createOrder for order_item_costing snapshots (order.controller.ts:251-326, catch at :321-325 logs a warning only) and in approveAndCalculateMRP (order-bom.controller.ts:339-343, 386-389) where MRP/WO/service failures are swallowed (though at least surfaced in the response there).
allFindings.failureScenario: workOrderService.createFromOrderItem fails on item 2 of 3 (bad data, DB hiccup) → order exists with 1 of 3 work orders; nothing in the API response indicates it; production planning silently misses items. Snapshot failure loses the pricing baseline used for variance tracking.
allFindings.fixSketch: Either include the dependent writes in the same $transaction, or make the failure loud: return partial-failure info in the response and/or persist a retry flag instead of only logging.

allFindings.title: Editing order items cascade-deletes order_item_costing snapshots (variance baseline) and never recreates them
allFindings.evidence: updateOrder deletes all order_items and recreates them with new randomUUID ids (order.controller.ts:789-801). order_item_costing has `orderItemId @unique` with `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:4416, 4443), so the cost-sheet snapshot created at order time (order.controller.ts:294-312, including costingSnapshot JSON, estimatedCostPerPiece, originalCostSheetVersion) is destroyed; the update path contains no snapshot re-creation.
allFindings.failureScenario: User edits an order to fix a size quantity → all items replaced → every order_item_costing row (the frozen pricing/variance baseline) is silently deleted; later variance tracking and costing comparison return null; selectedCadId choices on items are also lost.
allFindings.fixSketch: Update items in place (upsert by styleId) instead of delete-and-recreate, or carry order_item_costing (and selectedCadId) over to the replacement items inside the same transaction.

allFindings.title: createQuotationSchema strips placeOfSupplyId/includeTaxEstimate/taxRate that the service reads and the frontend sends → quotation GST estimation silently never runs
allFindings.evidence: createQuotationSchema (quotation.schema.ts:43-58) has no placeOfSupplyId/includeTaxEstimate/taxRate fields; route POST / uses validateBody(createQuotationSchema) (quotation.routes.ts:67-72) which replaces req.body with the parsed (stripped) object; quotation.service.ts:220-247 branches on `data.includeTaxEstimate` to compute estimatedCGST/SGST/IGST/totalWithTax; frontend CreateQuotationRequest includes all three fields (frontend/src/types/quotation.types.ts:139-141). No route exposes service estimateGST() as a fallback.
allFindings.failureScenario: User creates a quotation with 'include tax estimate' checked → fields silently stripped → quotation saved with estimatedCGST/SGST/IGST = 0 and totalWithTax null; customer-facing quote omits tax with no error anywhere.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add `placeOfSupplyId: z.string().uuid().optional(), includeTaxEstimate: z.boolean().optional(), taxRate: z.number().optional()` to createQuotationSchema (and updateQuotationSchema), and/or register a route for estimateGST.

allFindings.title: updateQuotation deletes all quotation_items on the global client before the header update — a failed update leaves the quotation permanently itemless
allFindings.evidence: quotation.service.ts:471-473 `await this.prisma.quotation_items.deleteMany({ where: { quotationId: id } })` runs standalone; the recreate happens only via nested create inside `this.model.update(...)` at :492-496. No $transaction spans the two.
allFindings.failureScenario: Items deleteMany succeeds, then model.update throws (DB connection blip, constraint on a nested item like a since-deleted styleId FK) → quotation keeps its old totalAmount but has ZERO line items; document prints empty; no error recovery path.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap deleteMany + update in `this.prisma.$transaction`, or use nested `quotation_items: { deleteMany: {}, create: [...] }` inside the single update call (atomic).

allFindings.title: quotationQuerySchema uses z.string().datetime() for fromDate/toDate → date-picker values (YYYY-MM-DD) are rejected with 400
allFindings.evidence: quotation.schema.ts:107-109: `fromDate: z.string().datetime('Invalid date format').optional()` (same for toDate); route GET / uses validateQuery(quotationQuerySchema) (quotation.routes.ts:50). This is exactly the datetime-schema class the smart-check guardrail exists for — `.datetime()` requires full ISO 8601 with time.
allFindings.failureScenario: User filters the quotation list by date using an <input type=date> → request `?fromDate=2026-07-01` → 400 'Invalid query parameters' — date filtering unusable.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use `z.coerce.date().optional()` (per the project guardrail) for fromDate/toDate; service already does new Date(fromDate).

allFindings.title: orderQuerySchema validates startDate/endDate but the controller and frontend use fromDate/toDate — query validation guards fields nobody sends and the real filters bypass validation
allFindings.evidence: order.schema.ts:72-73 declares `startDate`/`endDate`; order.controller.ts:343 destructures `fromDate, toDate` from req.query; frontend sends fromDate/toDate (frontend/src/services/order.service.ts:33-34). It only 'works' because validateQuery (validation.middleware.ts:51-73) copies validated keys onto req.query without removing unvalidated ones — so fromDate/toDate reach the controller raw and unvalidated, while startDate/endDate validation is dead code. Any future strict/replace behavior in validateQuery silently kills date filtering.
allFindings.failureScenario: `?fromDate=garbage` passes validation and hits `new Date('garbage')` → Invalid Date in the Prisma where clause → 500; meanwhile a well-formed `?startDate=...` is validated then ignored — the filter simply doesn't apply.
allFindings.fixSketch: Rename the schema fields to fromDate/toDate (z.coerce.date) to match controller + frontend, and read from req.validatedQuery.

allFindings.title: OrderList reads pagination.pages but the backend returns pagination.totalPages → totalPages state is undefined and order-list pagination breaks
allFindings.evidence: OrderList.tsx:98 `setTotalPages(response.pagination.pages)`; frontend type OrderListResponse declares `pages` (order.types.ts:242); backend getAllOrders returns `{ pagination: { page, limit, total, totalPages } }` (order.controller.ts:427-435). CostSheetList.tsx:91 has the same `.pages` bug.
allFindings.failureScenario: Order list loads → totalPages becomes undefined → the pagination control receives totalPages=undefined (renders 'Page 1 of undefined' / next-button logic comparing page < undefined is always false) → user cannot page past page 1 even with hundreds of orders.
allFindings.fixSketch: Change to `response.pagination.totalPages` and fix the OrderListResponse type (`totalPages: number`); grep for other `.pagination.pages` users.

allFindings.title: Zod MaterialTypeEnum for Order BOM is missing 4 Prisma MaterialType values (OTHER_TAPE, OTHER_DECORATIVE, OTHER_FUNCTIONAL, OTHER_MATERIAL) → BOMs containing them cannot be edited
allFindings.evidence: orderBom.schema.ts:14-43 (and the duplicated copy in order-bom.controller.ts:17-46) end at OTHER_FASTENER; Prisma enum MaterialType (schema.prisma:9011-9014) additionally has OTHER_TAPE, OTHER_DECORATIVE, OTHER_FUNCTIONAL, OTHER_MATERIAL. The BOM-from-cost-sheet mapper explicitly handles otherTapeId/otherDecorativeId/otherFunctionalId trims (order-bom.service.ts:68-71), so such items legitimately exist.
allFindings.failureScenario: Cost sheet contains an OTHER_TAPE trim → BOM created server-side with that materialType → user opens the BOM editor and saves → PUT /orders/:orderId/bom validateBody rejects the item with 400 'Invalid enum value' → the BOM is uneditable through the UI.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add the 4 missing values to MaterialTypeEnum (this is the exact enum-drift class the smart-check ratchet targets), and delete the duplicated enum in the controller.

allFindings.title: Order BOM requests are validated twice by two independently-maintained schema copies (route validateBody + controller .parse)
allFindings.evidence: Routes apply validateBody(createFromCostSheetSchema/updateOrderBOMSchema/changeWidthSchema) from schemas/orderBom.schema.ts (order-bom.routes.ts:43, 65, 188), then the controller re-parses the already-replaced req.body with LOCAL duplicates: CreateFromCostSheetSchema.parse (order-bom.controller.ts:106), CopyFromOrderSchema.parse (:135), UpdateOrderBOMSchema.parse (:230), ChangeWidthSchema.parse (:638). The MaterialTypeEnum is already duplicated in both files.
allFindings.failureScenario: Someone extends the route schema (e.g., adds the missing enum values from orders-14) but not the controller copy → route accepts, controller's stricter parse throws → confusing 400/500 that 'shouldn't be possible'; this is the same dual-schema pattern that bit /stock.
allFindings.fixSketch: Delete the controller-local schemas and consume the validated req.body typed via the schema exports from schemas/orderBom.schema.ts (single source of truth).

allFindings.title: order_item_breakup unique (orderItemId, colorId, sizeId) does not protect size-only orders because colorId is nullable (Postgres NULLs are distinct)
allFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:1068-1081: `colorId String?` with `@@unique([orderItemId, colorId, sizeId])`. Size-only orders are an explicitly supported path — controller converts '' → null (order.controller.ts:178, 774) and order.service.ts:164 comments 'Handle size-only orders'. In Postgres a unique index treats NULL != NULL, so two rows (item, NULL, size-M) both insert.
allFindings.failureScenario: Client submits breakup with size M listed twice (double-click / merge bug) on a size-only order → both rows insert despite the 'unique' → order item shows M twice; work_order_breakup copies both (order.controller.ts:827-837 and workOrder createFromOrderItem) → cutting plans double-count the size.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add a partial unique index `(orderItemId, sizeId) WHERE colorId IS NULL` via raw SQL migration (or make colorId non-null with a sentinel), plus de-duplicate breakup input in the schema/service.

allFindings.title: All order/quotation/BOM money rollups computed on raw JS floats; currency.ts helpers unused in the module
allFindings.evidence: order.controller.ts:149-153 `parseFloat(...)`, `itemTotal = itemTotalQty * parsedUnitPrice`, `totalAmount += itemTotal` (same in order.service.ts:139-143 and updateOrder :756-760); quotation.service.ts:167-172 (calculateTotalAmount), :304-311 (header GST re-summed as float +=), :683-706 (estimateGST accumulators); order-bom.service.ts:1115, 1284-1286, 1541, 1713-1717 (totalWithWastage * unitPrice chains); orderCosting.service.ts:174-184 (subtotal/valueLoss/markup on floats before wrapping in Prisma.Decimal). No import of backend/src/utils/currency.ts anywhere in these files.
allFindings.failureScenario: 1000-piece order at ₹129.95: 1000*129.95 → 129949.99999999999 stored into Decimal(12,2) → header totalAmount off by paise vs the invoice module's own computation; float-summed GST (cgst+sgst over many items) diverges from roundToCent per-line totals → reconciliation mismatches that 'appear' randomly.
allFindings.fixSketch: Route line totals and rollups through utils/currency.ts (decimal.js mul/add + roundToCent); keep gst.service as the only GST computer and sum its rounded outputs.

allFindings.title: createOrderSchema marks expectedDeliveryDate optional but controller and DB require it (500 instead of 400); schema also accepts 6 fields the controller ignores
allFindings.evidence: order.schema.ts:41 `expectedDeliveryDate: z.coerce.date().optional()` vs order.controller.ts:192 unconditional `new Date(expectedDeliveryDate)` and schema.prisma:1126 `expectedDeliveryDate DateTime` (required). Additionally the schema accepts orderNumber, status, currencyId, exchangeRate, billingAddress, internalNotes (order.schema.ts:38-51) which createOrder never reads — accepted-then-dropped silently.
allFindings.failureScenario: API client omits expectedDeliveryDate (schema says optional) → Invalid Date reaches Prisma → PrismaClientValidationError 500 instead of a clean 400; a client setting currencyId/exchangeRate believes multi-currency was recorded but it is silently discarded.
allFindings.fixSketch: Make expectedDeliveryDate required in createOrderSchema; delete the never-read fields from the schema (or implement them) so schema = controller contract.

allFindings.title: generateQuotationNumber is non-atomic (findFirst by createdAt + increment) → concurrent creates collide on the quotationNumber unique
allFindings.evidence: quotation.service.ts:136-162: reads latest by `orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }`, regex-extracts, +1 — no lock/atomic counter; quotations.quotationNumber is @unique (schema.prisma:1429). Same non-atomic pattern as the order controller's generator (orders-5) even though utils/atomicCodeGenerator exists.
allFindings.failureScenario: Two sales users create quotations simultaneously → both compute QT-2607-0042 → second insert fails P2002 → 500 to the user (retry loses their tax/item state).
allFindings.fixSketch: Reuse the atomicCodeGenerator pattern (sequence table / INSERT ... ON CONFLICT retry) used by generateAtomicOrderNumber.

allFindings.title: Order costing recalculation picks an arbitrary style_costing row (first of unordered array, no isApproved/supersededById filter) while order creation picks the latest approved — the two 'base costings' diverge
allFindings.evidence: orderCosting.service.ts:145 `const baseCosting = Array.isArray(style.style_costing) ? style.style_costing[0] : ...` with the include at :93 having no where/orderBy — comment claims 'first/latest' but Prisma returns unspecified order and includes superseded/unapproved versions. The snapshot path in createOrder instead uses `findFirst({ where: { isApproved: true, supersededById: null }, orderBy: { version: 'desc' } })` (order.controller.ts:254-261).
allFindings.failureScenario: Style has cost sheet v1 (superseded) and v3 (approved). Recalculate-costing for an order item lands on v1 → trimsTotal/cmtTotal/markup pulled from the obsolete sheet → order_item_costing.totalCostPerPiece silently computed from stale figures, disagreeing with the snapshot taken at order creation.
allFindings.fixSketch: Filter/order the include (where: { isApproved: true, supersededById: null }, orderBy: { version: 'desc' }, take: 1) so both paths select the same authoritative cost sheet.

allFindings.title: selectCadAndRecalculate and delete() perform two dependent writes without a transaction
allFindings.evidence: orderCosting.service.ts:273-282: `order_items.update({ selectedCadId })` then `this.recalculate(...)` (which upserts order_item_costing) — if recalculate throws (it wraps errors in InternalError at :261-267), the CAD selection is already persisted. delete() (:287-305) likewise deletes costing then clears selectedCadId in separate calls.
allFindings.failureScenario: User selects a new CAD width; recalculate fails (e.g., transient DB error) → order item now points at the new CAD while order_item_costing still holds figures computed from the old CAD → displayed costing silently inconsistent with the selected width.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap the selectedCadId update and the costing upsert in one $transaction (pass tx into recalculate), same for delete().

allFindings.title: GRN item Zod schema strips receivedAsReadyFabric/actualRatePerUnit/updateFutureSourcing — source-mismatch override silently never fires
allFindings.evidence: grnItemSchema (grn.schema.ts:39-53) has no receivedAsReadyFabric, actualRatePerUnit, or updateFutureSourcing fields and is NOT .passthrough() (only the top-level createGRNSchema is). validateBody (validation.middleware.ts:28) replaces req.body with the stripped parse. grn.service.ts:177-179 persists item.receivedAsReadyFabric/actualRatePerUnit/updateFutureSourcing, and approveGRN branches on them at grn.service.ts:987 (overrideItems filter). Frontend sends the fields (frontend/src/pages/GRNForm.tsx).
allFindings.failureScenario: User receives a GREIGE PO 'as ready fabric' with an actual rate and ticks 'update future sourcing'. Zod strips all three flags from every item → GRN stores receivedAsReadyFabric=false → approval books the receipt into greige_stock at the greige PO rate instead of fabric_stock at the actual rate; downstream processing POs are not cancelled and cost-sheet sourcing is never updated. No error anywhere.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add the three override fields (and thanCount if intended) to grnItemSchema so they survive validateBody stripping.

allFindings.title: POST/PUT /api/procurement validated by TWO disagreeing schemas — endpoint cannot succeed with either documented shape
allFindings.evidence: Route: validateBody(createProcurementSchema) (fabric-procurement.routes.ts:36) requires {supplierId, items[]} (fabricProcurement.schema.ts:46-54). Controller then re-parses with a LOCAL CreateProcurementSchema (controller lines 39-65, .parse at 197) requiring a flat {procurementType, quantityPurchased, width, ratePerUnit, totalCost}. For PUT, route updateProcurementSchema status enum is ['PLANNED','PO_CREATED','ORDERED','PARTIAL_RECEIVED','RECEIVED','CANCELLED'] while controller UpdateProcurementSchema enum is ['ORDERED','CONFIRMED','IN_TRANSIT','RECEIVED','PROCESSING','COMPLETED','CANCELLED']; controller schema also strips route-documented fields (invoiceNumber, supplierId, items) via ...validatedData spread at line 258.
allFindings.failureScenario: A client sending the flat controller shape gets 400 from the route ('items required'); a client sending the route's header+items shape gets a ZodError from the controller ('procurementType required'). Updating status to 'IN_TRANSIT' → 400 at route; to 'PARTIAL_RECEIVED' → controller rejects. Setting invoiceNumber on update is silently dropped.
allFindings.fixSketch: Delete the controller-local schemas and consume the typed body validated by the single route schema; align the status enum with the Prisma enum.

allFindings.title: receiveChallan credits general-material stock via createStockIn on the GLOBAL client inside the receive transaction
allFindings.evidence: Inside prisma.$transaction (challan.service.ts:565), line 695 calls stockMovementService.createStockIn({...}) with NO tx argument. createStockIn (stockMovement.service.ts:204-205) does not accept a tx and opens its OWN prisma.$transaction on the global client. Contrast issueChallan line 410-424, which passes the outer tx to createStockOut precisely to avoid this (comment cites F4).
allFindings.failureScenario: During challan receive, material stock-in commits on a second connection; if the subsequent challans.update (line 815) or a later item's processing fails, the outer tx rolls back but the stock_movements + stock_levels credit survives → phantom stock with no RECEIVED challan behind it. Also risks pool exhaustion/deadlock (nested tx waiting on outer tx's locks).
allFindings.fixSketch: Give createStockIn an optional outerTx parameter (same pattern as createStockOut) and pass the receive transaction's tx.

allFindings.title: receiveChallan has no status guard and re-credits the FULL receivedQty on every call — double stock credit
allFindings.evidence: receiveChallan (challan.service.ts:564-833) never checks challan status (no guard that it is ISSUED/IN_TRANSIT and not already RECEIVED). Item receivedQty is set by assignment (line 577), but the INWARD credit loop increments stock by the full receivedQty per call: fabric_stock quantityAvailable:{increment:receivedQty} (line 638), lace_stock (line 662), plus syncStockLevelQuantity(+receivedQty) (649/682) and createStockIn for materials (695).
allFindings.failureScenario: Partial receive of 50/100 → stock +50, status PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. User completes the receipt entering total 100 → item receivedQty overwritten to 100 but stock incremented by another 100 → 150 credited for 100 received. Calling receive again on a RECEIVED challan doubles it again. stock_levels and lot tables both drift upward.
allFindings.fixSketch: Guard on status (reject if RECEIVED/CANCELLED) and credit only the DELTA (newReceivedQty − previous receivedQty) per item.

allFindings.title: createGRN PROCESSING branch runs AFTER the GRN commit on the global client, and throws user-facing errors after the receipt is already booked
allFindings.evidence: GRN + purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity increments commit in the tx at lines 113-224. Then the PROCESSING block (lines 227-340) runs on global prisma: it THROWS 'already been received' (line 239) or 'Cannot receive. Job status is …' (line 241) — re-thrown at 330-337 — after the GRN exists; fabric_master update (263), createChallan (275, failure swallowed at 298-300), and job_work_orders update (303) are three separate non-atomic writes.
allFindings.failureScenario: Second GRN against a PROCESSING PO whose job was already received: GRN row created and PO item receivedQuantity incremented, then the API returns the 'already been received' error → user retries → a third GRN and another increment; PO flips to RECEIVED with phantom receipts. Separately, a crash between the job update and challan creation leaves a RECEIVED job with no inward challan (only logged).
allFindings.fixSketch: Validate the job-work-order state BEFORE the GRN transaction, and move the job/challan/fabric writes into the same tx (or a compensating saga); do not swallow the inward-challan failure.

allFindings.title: updateReceivedQuantity credits the FULL accepted qty to EVERY requirement_po_link of a PO item instead of allocating it
allFindings.evidence: mrp.service.ts:2418-2447 — for each link of purchaseOrderItemId: newReceived = Number(link.receivedQuantity) + receivedQuantity (the whole GRN accepted qty), and marks the requirement RECEIVED when newReceived >= allocatedQuantity. Yet PO generation explicitly allocates one PO item across MULTIPLE requirements proportionally (requirement_po_links.allocatedQuantity, mrp.service.ts:2296-2311).
allFindings.failureScenario: One consolidated PO item of 100m covers requirement A (allocated 60) and B (allocated 40). GRN approves 40m → BOTH links get receivedQuantity=40; B (40>=40) flips to RECEIVED even though its physical share may be zero, and total link receivedQuantity (80) is double the real receipt (40). MRP stops chasing B's material → production shortage that MRP believes is fulfilled.
allFindings.fixSketch: Distribute the accepted qty across links proportionally to allocatedQuantity (or fill sequentially up to each link's remaining allocation), not the full amount to each link.

allFindings.title: purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity is a hand-maintained counter that permanently includes QC-REJECTED quantity — PO closes as RECEIVED with rejected goods never re-procured
allFindings.evidence: createGRN increments receivedQuantity by GROSS item.receivedQuantity at GRN creation, pre-QC (grn.service.ts:212-219). approveGRN never subtracts rejectedQuantity (rejections only get an ADJUSTMENT_OUT stock_movements audit row, lines 887-907). rejectGRN decrements only whole-GRN rejection (1793-1801). updateReceivingStatus derives PO status from this gross counter (purchaseOrder.service.ts:878-893). Meanwhile MRP link receivedQuantity is updated with ACCEPTED qty only (grn.service.ts:881) — the two rollups use different figures.
allFindings.failureScenario: PO orders 100; GRN receives 100 with 20 rejected at QC. receivedQuantity stays 100 → PO status RECEIVED, pendingQuantity shows 0 (purchaseOrder.service.ts:1242), so the 20 rejected units awaiting supplier return are never reordered; MRP shows the requirement 80/100 while the PO says fully received.
allFindings.fixSketch: Derive received qty from accepted grn_items of ACCEPTED GRNs (or decrement rejectedQuantity at approval), and use one definition of 'received' for both PO status and MRP links.

allFindings.title: Strict float equality accepted + rejected !== received blocks legitimate decimal receipts
allFindings.evidence: grn.service.ts:95: `if (item.acceptedQuantity + item.rejectedQuantity !== item.receivedQuantity)` — raw JS float comparison on quantities that are decimal meters.
allFindings.failureScenario: Receive 10.3m with accepted 10.1 and rejected 0.2: 10.1 + 0.2 === 10.300000000000001 !== 10.3 → GRN creation fails with 'Accepted (10.1) + Rejected (0.2) must equal Received (10.3)', which looks correct to the user and is impossible to fix from the form.
allFindings.fixSketch: Compare with an epsilon (Math.abs(a+r−rcv) > 0.001) or use decimal.js from utils/currency.ts.

allFindings.title: MRP and Service PO generation use non-atomic generateCode('PO') on a SEPARATE PrismaClient while manual POs use the atomic generator — duplicate numbers under concurrency and a silent timestamp fallback
allFindings.evidence: mrp.service.ts:2178 and work-order-service-requirement.service.ts:1010 call generateCode('PO','purchase_orders','poNumber'). code-generator.ts instantiates its OWN `new PrismaClient()` (line 4) and does SELECT-max-LIKE 'PO-%' + 1 (lines 41-63) — outside the caller's tx and race-prone; on ANY error it silently returns `PO-<timestamp>` (lines 70-76). purchaseOrder.service.ts:28 uses generateAtomicPONumber() instead (format PO2511-0001), so two independent numbering series exist.
allFindings.failureScenario: Two users generate MRP POs simultaneously → both read PO-0042 → both create PO-0043 → the second insert fails on the unique poNumber (whole PO generation 500s) or, if the read errors, a PO-1731... timestamp number silently enters the ledger breaking the sequence.
allFindings.fixSketch: Route all PO number generation through generateAtomicPONumber() (atomicCodeGenerator) inside the creating transaction.

allFindings.title: MRP PO generation re-implements GST inline instead of gstService.calculateLineItemGST — tax diverges from manually-created POs
allFindings.evidence: mrp.service.ts:2186-2229 computes GST as `mat?.gstRate ? Number(mat.gstRate) : gstService.getDefaultGSTRate(hsn)` with hand-rolled cgst/sgst/igst parseFloat/toFixed math, and stores subtotal/totalAmount as unrounded float sums (2228-2247). purchaseOrder.service.ts:130 uses gstService.calculateLineItemGST which applies the HSN resolution chain and the apparel price-slab (gst.service.ts:85, 182-191). getDefaultGSTRate itself warns it 'CANNOT apply price-based slab' (gst.service.ts:502-511).
allFindings.failureScenario: The same material at ₹2,600/unit ordered manually gets 18% (apparel slab) but via MRP generate-po gets the material's base 5% rate → PO totals and GST filings differ by 13% of line value depending on which screen created the PO; header totals carry float dust (e.g. 10160.000000000002).
allFindings.fixSketch: Call gstService.calculateLineItemGST per item (passing unitPrice/materialId) and round header totals with Decimal, as purchaseOrder.service does.

allFindings.title: allocateStock marks requirements FULFILLED_STOCK without verifying stock exists, and reserves against quantityAvailable ignoring existing reservations
allFindings.evidence: mrp.service.ts:1805-1813 computes newAllocated/newShortfall/FULFILLED_STOCK purely from the REQUESTED data.quantity. The FIFO loops (1844-1889) reserve best-effort — `remaining` can end > 0 and is never checked, no error thrown. toReserve = min(remaining, lot.quantityAvailable) with quantityReserved only incremented, never netted against quantityAvailable, so an already-fully-reserved lot is reserved again.
allFindings.failureScenario: Requirement needs 500m, physical free stock is 200m. allocateStock(500) → requirement flips to FULFILLED_STOCK, shortfall 0, MRP stops procuring; only 200m actually reserved. Second requirement allocates against the same lots (available still >0) → double-reserve. At cutting time 300m is missing with no PO in flight.
allFindings.fixSketch: Compute reservable = available − reserved per lot, throw (rolling back) if remaining > 0 after the FIFO pass, and set allocatedFromStock to the actually-reserved amount.

allFindings.title: Every service-requirement endpoint is double-validated by a route schema and a divergent controller-local schema
allFindings.evidence: Routes use schemas/serviceRequirement.schema.ts, controllers re-.parse() with local duplicates (controller lines 107-343). Divergences: generate-po route requires expectedDeliveryDate z.string().datetime() (schema line 129, rejects 'YYYY-MM-DD' from date inputs) vs controller Date.parse refine (line 67) which would accept it; updateExecution route allows actualQuantity 0 (nonnegative, schema 158) vs controller .positive() (line 92) → passes route, throws in controller; /list route schema (60-71) rejects comma-separated status/serviceType and omits orderId while the controller explicitly supports comma lists and reads req.query.orderId (387-420).
allFindings.failureScenario: Frontend sends expectedDeliveryDate '2026-07-21' from an <input type=date> → 400 'Invalid request data' at the route even though the controller accepts it. Filtering the list by status=PENDING,PO_GENERATED → 400. Setting execution actualQuantity to 0 → raw ZodError instead of the route's formatted 400.
allFindings.fixSketch: Delete the controller-local schemas (consume the route-validated body), replace z.string().datetime() with z.coerce.date(), and let the list schema model comma-separated values + orderId.

allFindings.title: cancelChallan cancels ANY challan unconditionally without restoring the stock deducted at issue
allFindings.evidence: challan.service.ts:835-840 — `prisma.challans.update({data:{status:'CANCELLED'}})`, no status guard, no compensation. issueChallan deducted greige/fabric/lace/thread stock and stock_levels (209-441). Controller (challan.controller.ts:108-110) adds no guard either.
allFindings.failureScenario: User issues an OUTWARD challan for 300m greige (stock consumed, transferred to processor warehouse), then cancels it because the truck never left. Status becomes CANCELLED but the 300m stays consumed at source and duplicated at the processor warehouse → permanent stock ledger corruption. RECEIVED challans can also be cancelled after stock was credited.
allFindings.fixSketch: Only allow cancelling DRAFT challans (or, for ISSUED, run a compensating reversal of every stock deduction in one transaction).

allFindings.title: createFabricReturnChallan credits fabric_stock without syncing stock_levels and can drive quantityConsumed negative
allFindings.evidence: challan.service.ts:1029-1038 — fabric_stock quantityAvailable:{increment}, quantityConsumed:{decrement} with no syncStockLevelQuantity call (mandated by the material-sync pattern; the receiveChallan fabric branch at 649 does sync) and no check that item.quantity <= quantityConsumed.
allFindings.failureScenario: Cutting returns 40m to the fabric store: lot table shows +40 but the centralized stock_levels page still shows the pre-return figure — exactly the stock_levels drift class (template drifted ~60k). Returning more than was consumed (typo 400 vs 40) silently makes quantityConsumed negative.
allFindings.fixSketch: Look up the fabric's materials record and call syncStockLevelQuantity(+qty) in the same tx; validate quantity <= quantityConsumed.

allFindings.title: Challan number generation is read-max+1 (non-atomic) against a @unique column
allFindings.evidence: generateChallanNumber (challan.service.ts:91-116) does findFirst(startsWith prefix, orderBy desc) + 1 inside whatever tx supplied — no advisory lock/sequence. schema.prisma line 8347: `challanNumber String @unique`. PO/GRN numbers use generateAtomicGRNNumber/generateAtomicPONumber precisely to avoid this.
allFindings.failureScenario: Two GRNs for PROCESSING POs are created concurrently → both createChallan calls read CH2607-0011 → both write CH2607-0012 → second commit fails P2002; in the GRN flow that failure is swallowed (grn.service.ts:298) so the receipt has NO inward challan, in quickIssueChallan the whole request 500s.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use the atomic sequence generator (atomicCodeGenerator) for challan numbers.

allFindings.title: po_source_links has 4 nullable polymorphic FKs and NO unique constraint; linkRequirementToPO adds links without checking the requirement is already covered
allFindings.evidence: po_source_links (schema.prisma:3625-3655) — costSheetGenerationId/materialRequirementId/serviceRequirementId/productionRunId all nullable, only @@index, no @@unique, so duplicate rows for the same (poItem, requirement) are legal. requirement_po_links' unique is only (requirementId, purchaseOrderItemId) — the same requirement CAN link to items on two different POs. mrp linkRequirementToPO (mrp.service.ts:2339-2372) creates the link and force-sets status PO_GENERATED with no check of current status/existing links; generateServicePO reads requirements OUTSIDE its tx (work-order-service-requirement.service.ts:958-963) before linking inside it.
allFindings.failureScenario: A requirement already PO_GENERATED is linked to a second PO via /mrp/requirements/:id/link-po (no guard) → material procured twice; updateReceivedQuantity then updates BOTH links. Two concurrent generate-service-po calls for the same PENDING requirements both pass the status read and create two POs to different processors.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add partial unique indexes on po_source_links per source column, reject linkRequirementToPO when status is already PO_GENERATED/RECEIVED (or remaining allocation is zero), and re-read requirement status inside the PO-generation transaction with a conditional updateMany guard.

allFindings.title: updateReceivingStatus runs outside the GRN transaction and has no branch to revert PARTIALLY_RECEIVED when receipts drop to zero
allFindings.evidence: Called post-commit from grn.service.ts:343 and 1808 on the global client. Its logic (purchaseOrder.service.ts:878-893) only ever upgrades to RECEIVED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED and `return`s otherwise — never back to SENT/ACKNOWLEDGED.
allFindings.failureScenario: GRN created (PO → PARTIALLY_RECEIVED) then rejected: receivedQuantity decremented to 0 but the status recompute finds neither branch true and returns → PO stays PARTIALLY_RECEIVED forever with zero receipts. Separately, a crash between the GRN commit and this call leaves the status stale until the next GRN.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add an else branch restoring SENT/ACKNOWLEDGED when nothing is received, and run the recompute on the same tx as the receipt/rejection.

allFindings.title: createPurchaseOrder silently drops per-item foldLengthCm that the schema accepts and sibling paths persist
allFindings.evidence: purchaseOrderItemSchema includes foldLengthCm (purchaseOrder.schema.ts:85). updatePurchaseOrder persists it (service line 475) and addPurchaseOrderItem persists it (line 599), but the create path's itemsWithTotals object (lines 142-162) omits foldLengthCm entirely → NULL in DB.
allFindings.failureScenario: User creates a greige PO entering fold length 98cm per item (used for than-based actual-meter calculation at GRN). The PO saves fine but foldLengthCm is null; at receiving, the fold-length-adjusted quantity logic gets no default from the PO item — quantities computed from nominal instead of actual fold length, with no error shown.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add `foldLengthCm: item.foldLengthCm ?? null` to the create-path item mapping (and to updatePurchaseOrderItemSchema/service if item-level edit should carry it).

allFindings.title: PO item add/update/remove write the item and recalculate header totals in two separate non-transactional steps
allFindings.evidence: addPurchaseOrderItem: purchase_order_items.create (line 577) then this.recalculatePOTotal(poId) (line 615) — both on the global client, no shared tx; same pattern in updatePurchaseOrderItem (665/696) and removePurchaseOrderItem (725/730).
allFindings.failureScenario: Item is created but the process crashes (or recalculatePOTotal throws) before the header update → purchase_orders.totalAmount/subtotal no longer equal the sum of items until some later item operation happens to recompute them; PO printed/approved in between shows the wrong total.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap the item write and recalculatePOTotal in one prisma.$transaction (make recalculatePOTotal tx-aware).

allFindings.title: PROCESSING GRN approval force-sets PO to RECEIVED and overwrites receivedQuantity on only the FIRST PO item
allFindings.evidence: grn.service.ts:767-781 — unconditional `status: 'RECEIVED'` regardless of quantities, then `poItems[0]` gets receivedQuantity = qtyReceived by ASSIGNMENT (clobbering the increment applied at createGRN, lines 212-219); any additional items on the PO are untouched.
allFindings.failureScenario: A PROCESSING PO with two items (e.g. dyeing + transport line) is approved: item[0]'s receivedQuantity is overwritten with total meters received (possibly double-counting vs the create-time increment when units differ), item[1] stays 0, yet the PO is marked RECEIVED — the received-qty rollup and PO status permanently disagree with grn_items.
allFindings.fixSketch: Derive status via updateReceivingStatus and set received quantities per matching PO item (by poItemId) instead of poItems[0] assignment.

allFindings.title: calculateBulkRequirements sums per-style shortfalls, double-counting the same available stock once per style
allFindings.evidence: Per style, shortfall = totalRequired − availableStock (line 148, availableStock from shared stock_levels). Aggregation then does `existing.shortfall += req.shortfall` (line 229) — each style's shortfall already subtracted the FULL shared stock, so N styles subtract it N times; correct is sum(required) − availableStock.
allFindings.failureScenario: Fabric with 100m free stock; style A needs 150m, style B needs 120m in the same bulk plan. Reported aggregate shortfall = (150−100)+(120−100) = 70m instead of 270−100 = 170m → bulk procurement suggestion under-buys by 100m (and with surpluses it can even report negative shortfall while a real shortage exists).
allFindings.fixSketch: Aggregate requiredQuantity first, then compute shortfall once per material as sum(required) − availableStock.

allFindings.title: Stock valuation and processing cost math on raw floats instead of currency helpers
allFindings.evidence: grn.service.ts:821 `totalValue = acceptedQty * unitPrice` (raw float, stored as stock_movements.value); line 633 `totalCostPerMeter = processingRate + sourceCost`; defect stock at `totalCostPerMeter * 0.5` (699-700); fabric_procurement `totalCost: acceptedQty * actualRate` (1097). purchaseOrder.service.ts:485-490 stores updatePurchaseOrder header totals (subtotal, subtotal+totalTax) without rounding, unlike the create path which uses toFixed(2). None route through utils/currency.ts (roundToCent/weighted average).
allFindings.failureScenario: Receiving 33.33m at ₹142.7 stores value 4756.191000000001; repeated stock valuations and weightedAvgCost seeds accumulate float dust that surfaces as off-by-a-paisa mismatches between PO totals, GRN valuations, and reports (e.g. ₹563.796 renders).
allFindings.fixSketch: Route these multiplications/sums through Decimal helpers in backend/src/utils/currency.ts and round to 2dp before persisting.

allFindings.title: work_orders.completedQuantity is stored-not-derived and effectively never updates
allFindings.evidence: addProductionTracking only sets completedQuantity when a SINGLE tracking entry satisfies `data.productionStage === ProductionStage.PACKING && data.quantityCompleted >= workOrder.totalQuantity` (lines 604-616). production_tracking rows are the line items but are never summed. work_order_breakup.completedQuantity is written once as 0 (line 131) and never updated by any code path (grep confirms no other writer). Meanwhile updateWorkOrderSchema (workOrder.schema.ts:52) lets any PUT /work-orders/:id set completedQuantity to an arbitrary number with no derivation check. calculateCMTCost (line 1035) then computes totalCost = perPieceCost * workOrder.completedQuantity from this stale/hand-set value.
allFindings.failureScenario: Pack a 1000-pc WO in two PACKING tracking entries of 500 each: neither entry is >= 1000, so the WO never flips to COMPLETED and completedQuantity stays 0; CMT actual-cost update (updateActualCMTCosts) computes totals from completedQuantity=0. Conversely a client PUT with completedQuantity=99999 is accepted verbatim.
allFindings.fixSketch: Derive completedQuantity from SUM of finishing/packing line items (finishing_output_skus / production_tracking for PACKING) at read time or recompute inside the same transaction as each output write; remove completedQuantity from the update schema.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: completeCuttingBatch fabricReturns: three-way field-name drift (schema returnQuantity vs controller returnedQuantity vs frontend returnedQuantity) breaks fabric returns
allFindings.evidence: completeCuttingBatchSchema (production.schema.ts:186-192) REQUIRES `returnQuantity: z.number().positive()` per item; the controller reads `ret.returnedQuantity` (cutting.controller.ts:612: `if (ret.fabricStockId && ret.returnedQuantity > 0)`); the frontend sends `returnedQuantity` (frontend/src/pages/CuttingDetail.tsx:196, frontend/src/types/cutting.types.ts:237). validateBody strictly parses (validation.middleware.ts:28), so the required-but-missing returnQuantity fails.
allFindings.failureScenario: User completes a cutting batch and enters any fabric return (the dialog pre-fills returns with the full balance, CuttingDetail.tsx:178) → POST /cutting/batches/:id/complete returns 400 'Invalid request data'; batch cannot be completed with returns, and the return challan / stock restore never happens. Even if the schema were fixed to match the frontend, the controller/schema mismatch would silently drop returns.
allFindings.fixSketch: Align on one field name (returnedQuantity) in schema, controller, and frontend type; add a test that completes a batch with a return.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: record-output and issue-to-stitching schemas require skuId that neither controller nor frontend uses → 400s / silent skips
allFindings.evidence: recordCuttingOutputSchema requires `skuId: z.string().uuid()` per SKU (line 99) but the controller iterates `if (sku.id)` (cutting.controller.ts:511) and silently SKIPS items without `id`; the frontend type sends `id?` and no skuId (cutting.types.ts:215). issueToStitchingSchema likewise requires skuId (line 162) but cutting-issue.controller.ts:68-113 reads only colorId/sizeId/quantity, and the frontend builds `{colorId, sizeId, quantity}` (CuttingDetail.tsx:386-391).
allFindings.failureScenario: POST /cutting/batches/:id/record-output and /issue-to-stitching with the frontend's actual payload → Zod 400 (missing skuId), endpoints unusable. A client that appeases Zod by sending only skuId gets a 200 from record-output while ZERO cutting_batch_skus rows are updated (sku.id undefined → loop skips silently).
allFindings.fixSketch: Make the schemas match the controllers (id optional / colorId+sizeId keys), or refactor controllers to use skuId; remove the silent `if (sku.id)` skip and throw on unmatched SKUs.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: createCuttingBatch auto-issues the ENTIRE fabric lot because it reads sku.cutQuantity which is never set at creation
allFindings.evidence: `const totalPieces = skuOutputs.reduce((sum, s) => sum + (Number(s.cutQuantity) || 0), 0)` (line 277) — but at batch creation the SKUs carry toCut/plannedQty (created with cutQty: 0, line 207) and the frontend CreateCuttingBatchRequest has no cutQuantity. So totalPieces=0 and line 294 falls through to `fabricNeeded = Number(stock.quantityAvailable)` → `issueQty = min(fullLot, fullLot)` — the whole lot is issued via challan for every batch.
allFindings.failureScenario: Create a batch needing ~200m from a 1,000m lot → the auto-challan issues all 1,000m (fabric_stock.quantityAvailable → 0). Recovery depends on completion-time returns, which are broken by production-2 → the 800m surplus is stranded/lost from available stock and other work orders see zero stock.
allFindings.fixSketch: Compute fabricNeeded from toCut/plannedQty * cadAvg (the fields actually present at creation), and never default to issuing the full lot.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: createCuttingBatch multi-write flow is off-transaction and swallows the fabric-issue challan failure
allFindings.evidence: Sequence: cutting_batches.create (180) → cutting_batch_fabrics.createMany (218) → work_orders.update (232) → production_tracking.create in try/catch (242-261, logs and continues) → createChallan+issueChallan in try/catch that logs 'Don't fail batch creation if challan fails' (263-330). No prisma.$transaction wraps any of it.
allFindings.failureScenario: issueChallan throws (e.g. stock row conflict) → batch exists and is cuttable but fabric_stock was never deducted; completeCuttingBatch later finds no challans and falls back to lay-based consumption (line 666) → stock ledger silently overstates available fabric. A crash between batch create and WO status update likewise leaves a batch on a PENDING work order.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap batch + junction rows + WO status + challan create/issue in one prisma.$transaction (challan.service already accepts a tx per external-process usage); if auto-issue is best-effort, at least persist a flag on the batch that fabric was NOT issued instead of swallowing.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: deleteCuttingBatch restores stock from fabricIssued/fabricConsumed which are 0 for deletable batches, while the creation-time challan deduction stands
allFindings.evidence: Deletion is allowed for PENDING/ON_HOLD/IN_PROGRESS with no lays (399-406). Restore amount = `Number(existing.fabricIssued || existing.fabricConsumed || 0)` (414) — but batch.fabricIssued is only written at COMPLETION (completeCuttingBatch line 695) and fabricConsumed only by lays (which block deletion). The whole-lot auto-issue challan from creation (production-4/5) is neither cancelled nor reversed.
allFindings.failureScenario: Create batch (auto-challan deducts the lot from fabric_stock) → realize it was a mistake → delete the PENDING batch → code restores 0m, challan stays ISSUED with no owning batch → fabric permanently vanishes from available stock; the orphan challan also still pollutes the per-WO issuedMap used by every other batch's completion math.
allFindings.fixSketch: On delete, void/reverse the batch's INTERNAL issue challans (restore challan_items quantities to fabric_stock) inside the same transaction, rather than trusting fabricIssued/fabricConsumed columns.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: completeCuttingBatch attributes work-order-wide challan issuance to the single batch being completed (double-count across batches)
allFindings.evidence: issuedItems groups challan_items by fabricStockId where challan.productionRunId = existing.workOrderId (586-598) — the filter is per WORK ORDER, not per batch (challans carry no batch id). Each batch completion then writes `fabricIssued: issued` per batchFabric (652-659) and totalFabricIssued/actualConsumption/wastage/actualAverage from those WO-level sums (663-703).
allFindings.failureScenario: WO has 2 batches drawing from the same fabric lot, 500m issued for each (1000m total in challans). Completing batch A records fabricIssued=1000, wastage and actualAverage computed on 1000m; batch B records the same 1000m again → consumption/wastage reports double the real figure and CAD variance is nonsense.
allFindings.fixSketch: Attribute challans to batches (add cuttingBatchId to the challan or its items, set by the auto-issue path) or divide WO-level issuance across batches by recorded lay consumption.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: transfer_slips has no uniqueness (per batch/issue or on slipNumber) and generate endpoints have no existing-slip guard → duplicate transfers and FG stock double-count
allFindings.evidence: Model transfer_slips: slipNumber is a plain String (5949), cuttingBatchId/stitchingIssueId/finishingIssueId nullable FKs with no @@unique (5958-5960). cutting.controller.ts:860 generateTransferSlip, stitching.controller.ts:611, finishing.controller.ts:589 all create a slip carrying the FULL goodPcs with no check for an existing slip. finishing's version additionally increments finished_goods_stock (`quantity: existing.quantity + sku.finishedQty`, finishing.controller.ts:708) on every invocation. Slip numbers are count-based `existingSlips + 1` in 4 places → races/deletions produce duplicate slipNumbers silently (no unique index to stop them).
allFindings.failureScenario: User double-clicks 'Generate Transfer Slip' on a completed finishing issue of 500 pcs → two slips of 500 each AND finished_goods_stock += 500 twice → FG inventory shows 1000; stitching likewise 'receives' cut pieces twice via two CUTTING→STITCHING slips, inflating every WIP summary that sums transfer_slips.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add partial unique indexes (one active slip per cuttingBatchId/stitchingIssueId/finishingIssueId where the column is not null), make slipNumber @unique with retry-on-conflict generation, and guard generate endpoints with an existing-slip check.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: finished_goods_stock update is non-atomic read-modify-write outside any transaction, after the slip create
allFindings.evidence: generateTransferSlip: transfer_slips.create (649) then a per-SKU loop doing findUnique + update with plain assignment `quantity: existing.quantity + sku.finishedQty` (693-711) — no $transaction, no { increment }, no idempotency.
allFindings.failureScenario: Two concurrent slip generations (or any concurrent FG writer) read the same existing.quantity → one addition is lost. A crash mid-loop leaves the slip created but only some SKUs added to FG stock, with no way to tell which.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap slip + FG updates in one prisma.$transaction and use upsert with `quantity: { increment: ... }`.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: receiveSendOut overwrites cumulative received/damaged/cost on partial receipts instead of accumulating
allFindings.evidence: Status check permits receiving while PARTIALLY_RECEIVED (370-372), but the update ASSIGNS `quantityReceived: data.quantityReceived, quantityDamaged, quantityGood, actualCost` (404-408) rather than incrementing; SKU rows likewise assigned (383-386). Yet the fabric_stock restore `{ increment: quantityGood }` (436) IS per-call cumulative.
allFindings.failureScenario: Send 100m to smocking; receive 50 (record shows 50, stock +50); receive the remaining 50 → record now shows quantityReceived=50 again (first receipt erased), status stays PARTIALLY_RECEIVED forever (50+0 < 100), actualCost reflects only the last delivery — while fabric_stock correctly gained 100 → ledger vs record diverge and vendor liability/cost is understated.
allFindings.fixSketch: Accumulate: quantityReceived: { increment: ... } (same for damaged/good/SKU rows), recompute status from the accumulated totals, and sum actualCost.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: receiveSendOut status math double-counts damaged pieces (received treated as both inclusive and exclusive of damaged)
allFindings.evidence: `quantityGood = data.quantityReceived - quantityDamaged` (375) treats received as INCLUSIVE of damaged, but `totalAccountedFor = data.quantityReceived + quantityDamaged` (392) treats them as disjoint — one of the two must be wrong.
allFindings.failureScenario: Sent 100; vendor returns 95 of which 10 damaged (received=95, damaged=10): accountedFor=105 ≥ 100 → status RECEIVED and serviceRequirement marked COMPLETED although 5 pieces are still with the vendor and will never be chased.
allFindings.fixSketch: Pick one semantic (received includes damaged) and use `totalAccountedFor = quantityReceived` (accumulated); validate damaged ≤ received.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: cancelSendOut 'reverses' WIP counters using the RECEIVE mapping, which advances pieces to the next stage instead of returning them
allFindings.evidence: cancelSendOut calls `this.updateProductionTracking(tx, styleId, processType, 'RECEIVE', qty)` with comment 'Reverse = same as receive'. But for SMOCKING, RECEIVE does `piecesInSmocking: decrement` AND `piecesInStitching: INCREMENT` (545-546) — a cancel should restore piecesInCutting, not push pieces into stitching.
allFindings.failureScenario: Cancel a 200-pc smocking send-out → style_production_tracking shows 200 pcs in stitching that never left cutting; piecesInCutting is permanently understated. Every cancel corrupts the stage dashboard counters (which are themselves hand-maintained F1 counters with swallowed errors, lines 572-574).
allFindings.fixSketch: Add an explicit 'CANCEL' action that decrements the process stage and increments the ORIGIN stage (cutting/stitching per processType).
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: disposeDefects: Zod enum and controller enum are disjoint except REWORK
allFindings.evidence: disposeDefectsSchema: `z.enum(['RECTIFIED', 'REJECTED', 'REWORK'])` (production.schema.ts:286); controller: `if (!disposition || !['REWORK', 'SCRAP'].includes(disposition))` (stitching.controller.ts:1111); route applies validateBody(disposeDefectsSchema) (stitching.routes.ts:93).
allFindings.failureScenario: Client sends SCRAP (a value the controller supports) → Zod 400 before the controller runs; client sends RECTIFIED or REJECTED (values the schema advertises) → passes Zod, controller 400s. Only REWORK works; scrapping defects is impossible through the API.
allFindings.fixSketch: Align both to one enum (and ideally record disposition in a structured field rather than concatenated remarks).
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: receiveFromStitching: schema REQUIRES receivedQty which the controller silently discards; received quantity is never stored
allFindings.evidence: receiveFromStitchingSchema requires `receivedQty: z.number().int().positive()` (production.schema.ts:334) and the route validates it (finishing.routes.ts:75-79); the controller destructures only `{ transferSlipId }` (finishing.controller.ts:382) and just flips issue status to RECEIVED and slip to RECEIVED — the mandatory receivedQty is dropped, and short receipts are indistinguishable from full ones.
allFindings.failureScenario: Finishing receives 480 of 500 transferred pcs and enters 480 → API returns 200, but nothing records 480 anywhere; all downstream WIP math uses the issue's skuBreakdown.issuedQty, so 20 lost pieces are invisible forever.
allFindings.fixSketch: Either persist receivedQty (per-SKU, like stitching's receiveFromCuttingSchema.skuReceived — which the stitching controller also ignores, same bug at stitching.controller.ts:406) or remove the field from the schema so the contract is honest.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: pushToCutting flips the work order to IN_PRODUCTION BEFORE the blocking validation runs; a block leaves half-applied state
allFindings.evidence: Controller comment says 'Material availability check is now informational' but the flow is: updateWorkOrder({status: IN_PRODUCTION, actualStartDate: now}) (326-329) THEN addProductionTracking(IN_CUTTING) (332) which calls productionBlockingValidationService.validateStageTransition and THROWS if blocked (workOrder.service.ts:538-546) — including on MATERIAL_SHORTAGE, contradicting the comment. No transaction wraps the two calls.
allFindings.failureScenario: WO has a fabric shortfall → push-to-cutting responds 500 'Stage transition blocked' yet the WO is now IN_PRODUCTION with actualStartDate set and NO tracking entry; retrying keeps failing while the WO looks started on every dashboard; issueFabric/issueTrims now accept it (they only check status === IN_PRODUCTION).
allFindings.fixSketch: Validate first, then perform status update + tracking insert in one transaction (or pass a flag so addProductionTracking skips re-validation after an explicit pre-check).
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: All work-order mutation sub-routes lack validateBody; tracking endpoint parseInt/enum-casts raw body → NaN/Prisma 500s
allFindings.evidence: POST /:id/tracking, /:id/split, /:id/push-to-cutting, /:id/issue-fabric, /:id/issue-trims, /:id/issue-packaging, /:id/issue-thread (routes 55-61) have validateParams only. Controller does `quantityCompleted: parseInt(req.body.quantityCompleted)` and `req.body.productionStage as ProductionStage` unvalidated (workOrder.controller.ts:204-205); issueFabric/issueThread accept arbitrary lot quantities with no schema (516-521, 927-931).
allFindings.failureScenario: POST /work-orders/:id/tracking with missing quantityCompleted → NaN handed to Prisma → 500; an invalid productionStage string → Prisma enum error 500. Negative or absurd challan quantities in issue-fabric pass straight through to stock deduction.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add Zod schemas + validateBody for each mutation route (the smart-check route-validation ratchet will then also cover them).
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: workOrderNumber / batchNumber / issueNumber have no @unique; all generators are read-max+1 or count+1 races (one even reads via global client inside a tx)
allFindings.evidence: work_orders.workOrderNumber is @@index only (3096); cutting_batches.batchNumber (5783), stitching_issues.issueNumber (6041), transfer_slips.slipNumber (5949) all non-unique. generateWorkOrderNumber does findFirst-desc +1 (workOrder.service.ts:81-98) and splitWorkOrder calls it INSIDE the $transaction callback via the GLOBAL prisma client (line 868) — escaping tx isolation. generateBatchNumber (cutting.utils.ts:109) and generateIssueNumber (stitching.controller.ts:85) are COUNT-based, so any deletion reuses a number.
allFindings.failureScenario: Two users create WOs in the same second → identical workOrderNumber inserted silently (no unique constraint) → documents, challans and searches by number become ambiguous. Delete a cutting batch then create one → duplicate batchNumber for the same WO.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add @unique on the number columns, generate inside the transaction with retry-on-P2002, and switch count-based generators to max-based.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: SKU uniqueness constraints include nullable colorId — NULLs are distinct in Postgres, so size-only SKUs can duplicate and double-count
allFindings.evidence: @@unique([cuttingBatchId, colorId, sizeId]) with `colorId String?` (5861/5874); same pattern on stitching_issue_skus (6087/6095) and transfer_slip_skus (5988/5995). For colorless (size-only) work orders, two rows (batch, NULL, sizeM) are both legal. recalculateBatchTotals keys lay totals by `${colorId}|${sizeId}` and writes the SAME cutQty into every matching batch-SKU row (cutting.utils.ts:191-200), and all summaries sum rows.
allFindings.failureScenario: createCuttingBatch is sent the same sizeId twice (no server-side dedup, cutting.controller.ts:198-210) on a size-only order → two NULL-color rows; after lays, each row gets cutQty=laySum → totalCut, goodPcs, WIP and transfer availability all double.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use a sentinel non-null color value or Postgres NULLS NOT DISTINCT partial unique indexes; dedupe skuOutputs server-side before create.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: totalQuantity is never validated against the colorSizeBreakup sum (and split keeps them consistent only by luck)
allFindings.evidence: createWorkOrder writes totalQuantity and work_order_breakup rows independently (107-134); neither createWorkOrderSchema nor the service checks sum(breakup.quantity) === totalQuantity. Everything downstream treats totalQuantity as authoritative (cutting chart totalOrderQty, WIP orderQty, split validation `totalSplitQty >= originalWorkOrder.totalQuantity` line 861).
allFindings.failureScenario: Client sends totalQuantity=1000 with breakup summing 800 → cutting ratios, maxCuttable, shortfall meters and completion checks all computed against 1000 while only 800 pcs exist in the size grid; the 'cannot split entire quantity' guard also compares against the wrong total.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add a Zod refine (or service check) that breakup sums to totalQuantity — or derive totalQuantity from the breakup and drop it from the input.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: Lace receive computes cost with unguarded division by receivedQty/sentQty on raw floats → Infinity written into stock cost
allFindings.evidence: `processingCostPerMeter = totalCost / sentQty` (588) and `finishedCostPerMeter = (greigeCostPerMeter + processingCostPerMeter) * (sentQty / receivedQty)` (590) with no zero-guards and no currency.ts helpers; the result is persisted to lace_stock.weightedAvgCost and purchaseCost (608-609). actualShrinkagePercent also divides by sentQty (582). There is also no guard against receiving an already-COMPLETED batch, so a second receive creates a second full-quantity lace_stock lot.
