allFindings.failureScenario: Vendor loses the entire lot → receive with actualQuantityReceived=0 → finishedCostPerMeter = Infinity stored as the lot's cost (Prisma Decimal write error at best, corrupt costing at worst); any downstream weighted-average cost that includes this lot is poisoned.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use divideByShrinkage/guarded divide + roundToCent from backend/src/utils/currency.ts, reject receivedQty<=0 (or branch to a loss workflow), and guard re-receive on overallStatus.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: CMT actual-cost math on raw floats, and the whole cost update is a swallowed fire-and-forget
allFindings.evidence: updateActualCMTCosts: `newActualPerPiece = currentActual - estimatedCmt + cmtResult.perPieceCost` and variance% on Number()-cast Decimals (1089-1099) with no roundToCent/decimal.js; calculateCMTCost sums costs with plain reduce (1033) and multiplies by completedQuantity (1035 — itself stale per production-1). The controller trigger wraps it in try/catch logWarn-and-continue (workOrder.controller.ts:163-165), so failure leaves order_item_costing silently stale.
allFindings.failureScenario: Repeated completions/edits accumulate float residue in actualCostPerPiece (e.g. ₹563.7960000000001) and variancePercent; if updateActualCMTCosts throws, the order costing silently keeps the estimate with no operator signal.
allFindings.fixSketch: Route the arithmetic through backend/src/utils/currency.ts (roundToCent, guarded ops) and surface the failure (retry queue or response warning) instead of logWarn.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: recordDailyOutput required-field guards use && instead of || — they can never fire; missing quantities silently become 0
allFindings.evidence: `if (goodQty === undefined && goodQty === null)` (502) and `if (defectQty === undefined && defectQty === null)` (507) are contradictions (always false). Fallback `Number(goodQty) || 0` (515) then records 0. The finishing controller has the correct `||` version (finishing.controller.ts:477-485), proving the intent.
allFindings.failureScenario: A client omits goodQty (e.g. sends passedQty under a different key) → validation intended to reject it never runs, a daily output of 0 good pcs is recorded, and stitching WIP/completed totals silently under-count. (Route-level Zod requires goodQty, so this bites callers of the passedQty legacy alias path the code explicitly supports at line 500.)
allFindings.fixSketch: Change && to || (or delete the dead guards and rely on the Zod schema, extending it with the passedQty/rejectedQty aliases the controller accepts).
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: createStitchingIssue and daily outputs have no guard against issuing/producing more than upstream supplied
allFindings.evidence: createStitchingIssue accepts skuBreakdown.issuedQty verbatim (286-299) with no check against cutting goodPcs or the consumed transfer slips' quantities (slips are just bulk-marked RECEIVED, 306-311, outside any tx); recordDailyOutput accepts any goodQty with no cumulative check against issuedQty (491-519); completeStitchingIssue only checks output > 0 (553-558). Per-batch issueToStitching DOES enforce availability (cutting-issue.controller.ts:68-81), but this parallel path bypasses it.
allFindings.failureScenario: Operator creates a stitching issue for 600 pcs when cutting produced 500 (typo) → accepted; daily outputs then record 600 good pcs → stitching 'produced' exceeds cutting 'completed'; WIP summary masks it via Math.max(0, ...) (workOrder.controller.ts:1120-1140) so the inconsistency is invisible.
allFindings.fixSketch: Validate issuedQty per SKU against selected transfer-slip quantities minus already-issued, mark slips consumed in the same transaction, and cap cumulative output at issuedQty.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: Run split distributes breakup with independent Math.round per child — children no longer sum to parent (phantom/lost pieces)
allFindings.evidence: `const childQty = Math.round(breakup.plannedQuantity * ratio)` inside the per-child loop (116) with no remainder reconciliation; child breakups are also never checked to sum to split.quantity.
allFindings.failureScenario: Parent 100 pcs (50 M / 50 L) split 33/33/34: size M gets round(16.5)+round(16.5)+round(17)=17+17+17=51 → one phantom M piece; the child whose breakup sums to 34 may actually carry 35, so its own totalQuantity disagrees with its size grid — feeding production-19's drift downstream.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use largest-remainder allocation so per-size child quantities sum exactly to the parent, and assert sum(child breakup) === child.totalQuantity.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: rejectDelivery and updateDelivery mutate QC quantities without adjusting the hand-maintained stage/batch counters
allFindings.evidence: createDelivery increments stage.quantityReceived and decrements quantityInProcess (162-172); acceptDelivery rolls quantities into batch counters atomically (582-595). But rejectDelivery only flips qualityStatus (605-611) — stage.quantityReceived keeps the rejected qty and batch.quantityRejected is never incremented on this path; generic updateDelivery (446-448) can rewrite quantityAccepted/quantityRejected AFTER acceptance with no compensating batch update.
allFindings.failureScenario: Accept a delivery (batch.totalQuantityReceived += 100), then PUT the delivery with quantityAccepted=80 → batch still shows 100; reject a delivery → stage counters still count it as received/in-process resolved, so stage-level available-for-delivery math (line 99) is permanently off by the rejected quantity.
allFindings.fixSketch: Make reject/update flow through the same transactional rollup as accept (or derive stage/batch totals from processing_delivery aggregates, which createDelivery already does for its own guard at line 89).
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: workOrder.controller instantiates its own PrismaClient instead of the shared client
allFindings.evidence: `const prisma = new PrismaClient()` (line 19) while every service and other production controller imports the singleton from '../config/database'. This opens a second connection pool and means any future tx-passing pattern can't span the two.
allFindings.failureScenario: Under load, duplicate pools exhaust Postgres connections sooner; more importantly the issueFabric/issueTrims flows in this controller (createChallan → issueChallan as two separate non-tx calls, lines 533-555) can leave an orphan DRAFT challan if issueChallan fails, and the split client makes wrapping them in one transaction with challan.service impossible.
allFindings.fixSketch: Import the shared prisma from config/database and wrap createChallan+issueChallan pairs in a single transaction.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: cancelCuttingBatch sets status ON_HOLD (not CANCELLED) and releases nothing
allFindings.evidence: The cancel endpoint writes `status: 'ON_HOLD', remarks: 'CANCELLED: ...'` (847-853) even though CuttingBatchStatusEnum includes CANCELLED (production.schema.ts:18); no fabric restore or challan reversal occurs.
allFindings.failureScenario: A 'cancelled' batch still appears in every ON_HOLD filter and in alreadyCutQty exclusions ambiguity ('exclude ON_HOLD as they may resume', line 1843 comment vs sums that include it); its auto-issued fabric (production-4) stays deducted with no path back except the broken returns flow.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use the CANCELLED status and reverse outstanding fabric issuance in the same transaction.
allFindings.module: production (workOrder, cutting, stitching, finishing, external-process, processing delivery/batch, blocking validation, run-split)

allFindings.title: PATCH /style-costing/:id/actuals is a silent no-op: route schema and controller share ZERO field names
allFindings.evidence: Route validates with updateActualsSchema = {actualFabricCost, actualTrimCost, actualLaborCost, actualOverheadCost, remarks} (schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts:111-117). validateBody REPLACES req.body with the Zod-stripped parse result (validation.middleware.ts:28 `req.body = schema.parse(req.body)`). The controller then destructures `{ fabricActual, trimsActual, cmtActual, embroideryActual, accessoriesActual, totalActual } = req.body` (style-costing-approval.controller.ts:657) — none of these survive stripping, and none of the schema's fields are read.
allFindings.failureScenario: User posts {fabricActual: 50000} to record actual procurement cost → all schema-optional so validation passes → body stripped to {} → controller reads all-undefined → nothing is written, variance recalculated on stale data → returns 200 success. Actual-vs-budget variance tracking silently never updates from this endpoint.
allFindings.fixSketch: Make schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts updateActualsSchema use the controller's field names (fabricActual, trimsActual, cmtActual, embroideryActual, accessoriesActual, totalActual) and delete the duplicate vocabulary.

allFindings.title: PUT /style-costing/:id silently discards every edit: route schema fields don't overlap controller schema
allFindings.evidence: Route validateBody(updateCostSheetSchema) allows only {widthCombination, fabricCost, trimCost, laborCost, overheadCost, profitMargin, remarks, items} (schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts:59-68) and strips everything else. Controller re-parses with UpdateCostSheetSchema = CreateCostSheetSchema.partial() (styleCosting.controller.ts:722, style-costing.utils.ts:312) whose fields are fabricDetails/trimsDetails/cmtCosts/valueLossPercent/markupPercent/notes/closedCost/budget fields — zero overlap, all optional, so the parse of the stripped body succeeds with nothing in it.
allFindings.failureScenario: User edits fabric rates in the cost-sheet form and saves; frontend sends {fabricDetails:[...], trimsDetails:[...], cmtCosts:{...}} → route strips all of them → controller's partial schema parses {} without error → update writes no meaningful fields → 200 success, edits silently lost.
allFindings.fixSketch: Delete the divergent updateCostSheetSchema in schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts and validate the route with the real UpdateCostSheetSchema from style-costing.utils.ts (single source of truth), removing the in-controller re-parse.

allFindings.title: Cost-sheet actuals OVERWRITTEN with per-GRN amount instead of accumulated — last GRN wins
allFindings.evidence: updateCostSheetActuals does `data: { [actualField]: actualCost }` (plain assignment, costSheet.service.ts:265-270). Its only caller, grn.controller.ts approveGRN (lines 216-287), computes styleActuals from THIS GRN's items only (`for (const grnItem of grnWithItems.grn_items)` at 218, unitPrice*receivedQty summed at 222-242) and passes that per-GRN figure as actualCost. The whole block is wrapped in `catch { logError(...) }` (grn.controller.ts:289-292) — fire-and-forget, off-transaction (F4).
allFindings.failureScenario: Style receives fabric via GRN-1 (₹80,000) then GRN-2 (₹30,000). After GRN-2 approval, fabricActual = 30,000 (not 110,000) → fabricVariance computed against budget shows a large favorable variance → varianceStatus WITHIN_BUDGET when the real spend exceeds budget → wrong money decisions, silently.
allFindings.fixSketch: Derive the actual as SUM over all approved GRN items traced to the style (recompute from line items on each approval), or at minimum use { increment: actualCost } plus an idempotency guard; run it inside the GRN-approval transaction and stop swallowing the error.

allFindings.title: POST /style-costing (create cost sheet) always 400s: route schema strips the fields the controller schema requires
allFindings.evidence: Route validateBody(createCostSheetSchema) = {styleId, purpose, widthCombination, fabricCost, trimCost, laborCost, overheadCost, profitMargin, remarks, items} (schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts:42-53) strips fabricDetails/trimsDetails/cmtCosts from req.body. Controller then runs CreateCostSheetSchema.parse(req.body) (styleCosting.controller.ts:47) which REQUIRES fabricDetails.min(1), trimsDetails.min(1) and cmtCosts (style-costing.utils.ts:271-274). Frontend confirmed to send fabricDetails/trimsDetails/cmtCosts (frontend/src/types/costSheet.types.ts:290-304). Purpose enums also disagree: route allows PROCUREMENT_PRODUCTION, controller allows PRODUCTION.
allFindings.failureScenario: Any create request: frontend sends full payload → route strips detail arrays → controller parse throws ZodError ('At least one fabric is required') → endpoint can never succeed. If frontend sends purpose:'PRODUCTION' it 400s even earlier at the route.
allFindings.fixSketch: Validate the route with the controller's CreateCostSheetSchema (move it into schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts) and remove the in-controller re-parse; align the purpose enum with the Prisma enum.

allFindings.title: POST /:id/create-version always rejects: schema strips versionReason that the controller requires (frontend sends it)
allFindings.evidence: createCostSheetVersionSchema = {remarks: optional} only (schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts:93-95). Controller: `const { versionReason } = req.body; if (!versionReason ...) throw new ValidationError('Version reason is required...')` (style-costing-approval.controller.ts:146-155). Frontend sends { versionReason } (frontend/src/services/costSheet.service.ts:87-92).
allFindings.failureScenario: User clicks 'Create new version' on an approved cost sheet → versionReason stripped by validateBody → controller throws 'Version reason is required' 100% of the time → cost-sheet versioning (needed after rate changes ≥5% block PO generation with RATES_OUTDATED) is impossible via the API, deadlocking the rates-outdated workflow.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add versionReason: z.string().min(1) to createCostSheetVersionSchema.

allFindings.title: POST /variance/:id/approve unusable: controller requires 'action' which the schema always strips
allFindings.evidence: approveVarianceSchema = {approved: z.boolean() (required), remarks, rejectionReason} (schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts:123-127). Controller: `const { action, notes } = req.body; if (!action || !['APPROVE','REJECT'].includes(action)) throw new ValidationError(...)` (style-costing-approval.controller.ts:716-720). 'action' and 'notes' are not in the schema so they can never reach the controller; conversely 'approved' is required by the schema but never read.
allFindings.failureScenario: Variance exceeds buffer → varianceStatus REQUIRES_APPROVAL blocks order creation → admin posts either {action:'APPROVE'} (400 at route: 'approved' missing) or {approved:true} (route passes, controller throws 'Action must be either APPROVE or REJECT'). Every possible payload fails → variances can never be approved → orders permanently blocked.
allFindings.fixSketch: Align approveVarianceSchema to {action: z.enum(['APPROVE','REJECT']), notes} (or rewrite the controller to consume 'approved'), one vocabulary only.

allFindings.title: Lace-items sub-routes: calculate-options mutually contradictory schemas; PUT and bulk-add use a different field vocabulary than the service
allFindings.evidence: (a) calculateLaceOptionsSchema = {laceId, quantity(required)} (schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts:218-221) but controller reads {laceId, quantityPerGarment, orderQuantity, wastagePercent, styleId} and 400s if quantityPerGarment undefined (styleCostingLaceItems.controller.ts:213-222). (b) updateLaceItemSchema = {quantity, unit, rate, costOption, processingCost, remarks} (185-192) but service updates quantityPerGarment/wastagePercent/costPerMeter/sourcingStrategy (styleCostingLaceItems.service.ts:158-181) — only processingCost overlaps. (c) bulkAddLaceItemsSchema items = {laceId, quantity, rate, ...} (198-212) but controller does parseFloat(item.quantityPerGarment) → NaN and service throws 'wastagePercent is required' (service:57-58).
allFindings.failureScenario: calculate-options: schema-shaped body passes route then 400s in controller; controller-shaped body 400s at route ('quantity' missing) — endpoint unusable. PUT lace-item with {quantity: 5, rate: 12} → 200 success but quantityPerGarment/costPerMeter unchanged (silent no-op; totals recomputed from OLD values). Bulk add always 500s.
allFindings.fixSketch: Rewrite the three schemas to the controller/service vocabulary (laceId, quantityPerGarment, wastagePercent, costPerMeter, sourcingStrategy, ...) matching addLaceItemSchema, which is already correct.

allFindings.title: Decimal >= Decimal compares as STRINGS — 'fully received' check is lexicographic
allFindings.evidence: `item.receivedQuantity >= item.orderedQuantity` (lines 1805-1807 in updateLaceProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeLaceGRN and 1862 in updateProcessingPOStatusOnGreigeGRN). Both columns are Prisma Decimal (schema.prisma purchase_order_items:1235-1236). decimal.js Decimal.prototype.valueOf returns a STRING, so JS relational comparison of two Decimal objects is string comparison: '95' >= '100' is true, '100' >= '20' is false.
allFindings.failureScenario: Greige PO orders 100m, GRN receives 95m → '95' >= '100' → lexicographically TRUE → PO treated as fully received → linked Processing PO auto-flipped PENDING_GREIGE → READY_FOR_PROCESSING before the greige exists. Conversely ordered 20m, received 100m → '100' >= '20' false → processing PO never released.
allFindings.fixSketch: Compare numerically: Number(item.receivedQuantity) >= Number(item.orderedQuantity), or item.receivedQuantity.gte(item.orderedQuantity).

allFindings.title: Greige-lace PO shortfall computed against FINISHED lace stock, not greige-lace stock
allFindings.evidence: In calculateRequirements, stockInfo comes from `this.getStockInfoForLace(laceItem.laceId)` (line 371, finished lace_stock). For GREIGE_PROCESSED, the greige item uses `shortfall: Math.max(0, greigeRequiredQty - stockInfo.available)` (lines 438 and 450) — i.e., greige requirement offset by FINISHED-lace availability of a different master (laceId, not greigeLaceId). The fabric flow does this correctly via getStockInfoForGreige(fabricItem.greigeId) (line 185).
allFindings.failureScenario: 20m of finished lace in stock, 0m greige lace, requirement 100m greige → shortfall computed 80m → greige-lace PO under-ordered by 20m; production starves. Or greige lace in stock is ignored entirely → over-ordering.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add a getStockInfoForGreigeLace(greigeLaceId) (lace_stock rows for the greige master or its own stock table) and compute greige-lace shortfall/availableStock from it.

allFindings.title: Preferred-supplier lace price never used: query selects 'pricePerMeter' but code reads '.price'
allFindings.evidence: The lace_suppliers select fetches `pricePerMeter` (lines 154-163), but getReadyLaceCost checks `if (preferredSupplier?.price) { cost = Number(preferredSupplier.price); ... rateSource='SUPPLIER_PRICE' }` (lines 368-372). `.price` is always undefined, so the branch is dead and it silently falls through to lace_master.pricePerMeter.
allFindings.failureScenario: Preferred supplier quotes ₹18/m, stale lace-master rate is ₹12/m → READY_LACE option costed at ₹12/m with rateSource LACE_MASTER → comparison recommends READY_LACE on a price nobody will honor → cost sheet and downstream PO budget wrong by 50%.
allFindings.fixSketch: Read preferredSupplier.pricePerMeter (the selected field name).

allFindings.title: 'Weighted' average cost is an UNWEIGHTED _avg of per-lot WACs
allFindings.evidence: calculateWeightedAverage aggregates `_avg: { weightedAvgCost: true }` and uses it as existing average (lines 80-94); getCurrentWeightedAverage does the same (lines 276-286). A simple mean of per-lot WACs ignores lot quantities. The repo's decimal.js weightedAverage helper in backend/src/utils/currency.ts (called out by the guardrails doc) is not used.
allFindings.failureScenario: Lot A: 1000m @ ₹10, Lot B: 10m @ ₹100 → true WAC ₹10.89, _avg returns ₹55. Next receipt blends new cost against ₹55 → fabric_stock.weightedAvgCost corrupted; STOCK_REUSE costing option (checkStockAvailability reads weightedAvgCost) and stock valuation report all inherit the wrong figure.
allFindings.fixSketch: Compute existing value as SUM(quantityAvailable * weightedAvgCost) / SUM(quantityAvailable) (per-lot quantities), routing the math through utils/currency.ts weightedAverage.

allFindings.title: Order-item costing omits laceTotal from the subtotal that style costing includes
allFindings.evidence: recalculate: `subtotal = fabricTotal + trimsTotal + embroideryTotal + accessoriesTotal + cmtTotal + processingTotal + overheadsTotal` (lines 174-175) — no lace term. The style cost sheet's own subtotal includes laceTotal (styleCostingLaceItems.service.ts:419 `subtotal = ... + laceTotalNum`). Duplicated value-loss/markup pipeline diverges between the two.
allFindings.failureScenario: Style with ₹40/pc of lace: cost sheet totalProductCost includes lace, but order-item recalculation (triggered on CAD width selection) produces totalCostPerPiece ₹40+markup lower → margin/selling-price decisions on the order made from an understated cost.
allFindings.fixSketch: Include laceTotal (from baseCosting.laceTotal or style_costing_lace_items sum) in the order costing subtotal; ideally extract the subtotal→valueLoss→markup pipeline into one shared function (also used by styleCosting.controller:104-134, costing.service.ts:508-534, styleCostingLaceItems.service.ts:409-423).

allFindings.title: cost_sheet_po_generation: no uniqueness on costSheetId + racy get-or-create + off-transaction link update → duplicate POs per category
allFindings.evidence: Model has no @@unique on costSheetId (schema.prisma:1811-1847). Every generate* method does findFirst({costSheetId, <categoryPOId>: null}) → create-if-missing → PO+items in $transaction → then `prisma.cost_sheet_po_generation.update({data:{fabricPOId}})` OUTSIDE that transaction (costSheetPOGeneration.service.ts:693-750, repeated at 833-890, 998-1060, 1151-1207, 1386-1442, 1527-1584, 1706-1768).
allFindings.failureScenario: Double-click on 'Generate Fabric PO': both requests findFirst the same generation row with fabricPOId null, both create full POs, second update overwrites fabricPOId — two live DRAFT fabric POs for one cost sheet, one invisible in generation status → double procurement. Also, if the trailing update fails after the PO tx committed, the generation row stays null and the next attempt silently creates another duplicate.
allFindings.fixSketch: Move the generation upsert + PO create + link update into one $transaction with a conditional updateMany({where:{id, fabricPOId:null}}) guard (retry if count 0), and add a partial unique index enforcing one open generation per cost sheet.

allFindings.title: Three divergent 'current rate' resolutions; rate-change guard hardcodes DYEING so printed fabrics are validated against the wrong process (or not at all)
allFindings.evidence: validateCostSheetRates calls getCurrentProcessorRate(processorId, greigeId, null, 'DYEING', slabId) for ALL fabric items (line 249-255) even though cost-sheet rates are built from lookupRate with processingType mapped from finishType (DYEING or PRINTING, fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:461,495). getCurrentProcessorRate filters effectiveTo:null (line 108) while lookupRate filters only isActive (processor-rate-v2.service.ts:939-951), and validateLacePOGeneration uses a third variant: findFirst orderBy createdAt desc with no slab/effective filter (costSheetPOGeneration.service.ts:1272-1282).
allFindings.failureScenario: PRINTED fabric cost sheet: current PRINTING rate rose 20% → validation looks up DYEING, finds nothing, `if (!currentRate) continue` → no block → Processing PO generated at a stale rate. Or a DYEING card exists for the same greige → compared against the wrong process → false RATES_OUTDATED block.
allFindings.fixSketch: Pass the item's actual processingType (derive from finishType/rateCard) into getCurrentProcessorRate, and consolidate all three resolutions onto the V2 lookupRate path with consistent effectiveTo semantics.

allFindings.title: consumeStock/receiveStock: stock write and ledger transaction row not atomic; read-check-update race
allFindings.evidence: consumeStock: findUnique (215), availability check on the read value (225), fabric_stock.update with computed availableQty - qty (230-237), then fabric_stock_transaction.create (243-259) — no $transaction, no atomic decrement. receiveStock likewise: fabric_stock.create (150) then fabric_stock_transaction.create (176) unbundled.
allFindings.failureScenario: Two concurrent consumptions of a 100m lot for 80m each: both read 100, both pass the check, final quantityAvailable = 20 with 160m consumed (oversell). Separately, a crash between update and transaction-create leaves stock changed with no ledger entry — balanceAfter/valueAfter audit trail silently wrong.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap each pair in prisma.$transaction and use an atomic guarded update (updateMany where quantityAvailable >= qty with decrement, checking affected count).

allFindings.title: Version creation: clone + supersede/lock of old sheet are two separate writes; dead versioning service has INVERTED supersededById semantics
allFindings.evidence: createCostSheetVersion creates the new sheet (187) then separately updates the old one's supersededById/lockedForOrders (286-292) with no transaction. Meanwhile the unused cost-sheet-versioning.service.ts sets supersededById on the NEW sheet pointing at the OLD one (line 133) — the opposite of the convention every consumer relies on (`supersededById: null` = current: costSheet.service.ts:240, order.controller.ts:98,258).
allFindings.failureScenario: Second write fails after the first commits → two sheets with supersededById null for the same style+purpose → findFirst 'current version' in updateCostSheetActuals/order flows nondeterministically picks the stale one; actuals and orders attach to the wrong version. If anyone wires the dead service, 'current version' resolution inverts entirely.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap clone + supersede in one $transaction; delete or fix cost-sheet-versioning.service.ts to set supersededById on the old row.

allFindings.title: 0% wastage treated as missing (falsy guard) → 500 for a legal value
allFindings.evidence: `wastagePercent: wastagePercent ? parseFloat(wastagePercent) : undefined` (laceCosting.controller.ts:31 and batch at 65; same pattern in styleCostingLaceItems.controller.ts:72 and 258). calculateLaceCost then throws 'wastagePercent is required - no hardcoded defaults allowed' (laceCostingCalculation.service.ts:125-127). The route schema explicitly allows 0 (laceCosting.schema.ts:29 min(0)), and the sibling controller documents '0 is valid, meaning no wastage' (styleCostingLaceItems.controller.ts:219).
allFindings.failureScenario: User calculates lace cost with wastagePercent 0 → 0 is falsy → converted to undefined → service throws → 500 Internal error for valid input; in bulk add, item creation aborts mid-list.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use explicit nullish checks: `wastagePercent != null ? parseFloat(wastagePercent) : undefined` in all four spots.

allFindings.title: fabric_costing_run.totalFabricCost/isComplete/fabricCount are stored aggregates refreshed only by an optional client-triggered recalculate
allFindings.evidence: Totals are computed and stored at createRun (203-214) and only refreshed via the separate PATCH /:runId/recalculate endpoint (307-320). saveFabricCosting (fabric-costing.controller.ts:690+) updates the underlying fabric_width_cad cost fields (totalCostPerMeter etc.) and can even clone rows into a run, but never touches the run's stored totals.
allFindings.failureScenario: User edits a CAD's totalCostPerMeter from ₹120 to ₹150 via fabric-costing save; run list/pages keep showing the old totalFabricCost and isComplete flag until someone happens to hit the recalculate endpoint — costing-run totals drift from their own line items.
allFindings.fixSketch: Derive run totals at read time from fabricCads (they are always loaded anyway), or recompute inside saveFabricCosting whenever an affected CAD belongs to a run; drop the stored columns from the source-of-truth path.

allFindings.title: style_costing_trim_items: 24 nullable master FKs with 'only ONE should be populated' enforced by nothing
allFindings.evidence: Model comment says 'Master FK fields - only ONE should be populated based on materialType' (schema.prisma:1977) over materialId/threadId/buttonId/.../masterId (1978-2004) with no CHECK, no partial unique, no @@unique; same shape on style_costing_accessory_items (2047-2065). Consumer resolves by first-non-null cascade (costSheetPOGeneration.service.ts:284-311).
allFindings.failureScenario: A row created with both threadId and buttonId set (nothing prevents it — the Zod detail schemas accept all FKs simultaneously): PO generation's `trim.bomId || trim.materialId || trim.threadId || trim.buttonId ...` silently orders the thread and drops the button; duplicate rows for the same master also pass, double-counting the trim in trimsTotal and in generated PO quantities.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add a DB CHECK constraint (num_nonnulls(...) <= 1) via raw migration plus a Zod refine that exactly one FK matches materialType; consider a partial unique on (costingId, coalesce(all FKs)) to block duplicates.

allFindings.title: Lace item writes and cost-sheet total recompute are separate non-transactional writes
allFindings.evidence: addLaceItemToCostSheet: create (65) then updateCostSheetLaceTotal (121); updateLaceItem: update (188) then total recompute (219); removeLaceItem: delete (239) then recompute (244). updateCostSheetLaceTotal itself is aggregate-read (384) then style_costing.update (426) — no shared transaction anywhere.
allFindings.failureScenario: Item insert commits, then updateCostSheetLaceTotal throws (e.g., connection drop) → laceTotal/subtotal/totalProductCost on the cost sheet no longer match the line items → an approved sheet with wrong totalProductCost flows into PO budgets. Two concurrent item edits can also interleave recomputes and persist a stale total.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap item write + total recompute in one prisma.$transaction (pass tx through), mirroring the aggregate-from-lines pattern that already exists.

allFindings.title: getStockInfoForLace computes total as available + reserved; greige twin uses available - reserved
allFindings.evidence: getStockInfoForLace returns `total: available + reserved` (line 586) while getStockInfoForGreige returns `total: available - reserved` (line 558) and getStockInfoForMaterial `available + fabricAvailable - totalReserved` (line 529) — same semantic field, opposite sign for lace.
allFindings.failureScenario: Lace with 100m available, 40m reserved reports total 140m instead of 60m in the requirements payload → UI/user judges net availability high → under-orders on manual adjustment of orderQty.
allFindings.fixSketch: Change to `available - reserved` to match the other two implementations (or centralize StockInfo computation in one helper).

allFindings.title: approveCostSheet 'action'/'rejectionNotes' unreachable — only the legacy 'approved' boolean survives validation; rejection notes silently lost
allFindings.evidence: Controller reads `{ action, rejectionNotes } = req.body` with legacy fallback `req.body.approved` (lines 25-27). Route schema approveCostSheetSchema = {approved (required), remarks, rejectionReason} (schemas/styleCosting.schema.ts:83-87) strips both action and rejectionNotes. Frontend currently sends {approved} (frontend/src/services/costSheet.service.ts:107) so approval works only via the legacy path.
allFindings.failureScenario: Any client using the documented action-based API gets 400 ('approved' required); a rejection sent as {approved:false, rejectionReason:'rates outdated'} loses the reason because the controller reads rejectionNotes, not rejectionReason → rejected sheets carry no rejection reason.
allFindings.fixSketch: Unify on one contract: schema {action: enum, rejectionNotes} or controller reading {approved, rejectionReason}; delete the other vocabulary.

allFindings.title: PO subtotals/taxes accumulated on raw floats with parseFloat(toFixed(2)) rounding instead of currency helpers
allFindings.evidence: Every generate* method does `subtotal += totalPrice` and `poTotalCgst += gst.cgstAmount` on JS floats then `parseFloat((subtotal + totalTax).toFixed(2))` (e.g., lines 654-664, 689-690, 794-830, 1112-1148). Same float pattern in costSheet.service.ts variance math (77-176) and styleCosting.controller totals (104-134). backend/src/utils/currency.ts (decimal.js, roundToCent) exists and is unused here; per-line GST correctly routes through gstService.
allFindings.failureScenario: Many-line POs accumulate binary-float error before the single final rounding; PO totalAmount can differ by ₹0.01+ from the sum of already-rounded line taxAmounts stored on purchase_order_items → invoice-vs-PO reconciliation mismatches.
allFindings.fixSketch: Sum the already-rounded line amounts with decimal.js (utils/currency.ts) and derive header totals from stored line values.

allFindings.title: Decimal(0) truthiness: ₹0 master rate becomes an 'available' option and wins the cheapest-recommendation
allFindings.evidence: `else if (fabric.costPerMeter)` (line 327) — Prisma Decimal is an object, so Decimal(0) is truthy → cost = 0 → option returned available with totalCost 0; the recommendation sorts ascending by totalCost (192-203), so a zero-rate master always wins. Contrast greige path which treats 0 as missing (line 435 `if (!greigeCostPerMeter)`).
allFindings.failureScenario: fabric_master.costPerMeter = 0 (unpriced) → READY_FABRIC recommended at ₹0 total → cost sheet seeded with a free fabric; downstream zero-price PO guard later blocks with a confusing error, or the sheet is approved understated.
allFindings.fixSketch: Treat 0 as 'no rate' (Number(fabric.costPerMeter) > 0), consistent with the greige branch.

allFindings.title: GSTR-1 silently excludes all OVERDUE invoices — under-reported GST liability and GSTR-1/GSTR-3B mismatch
allFindings.evidence: generateGSTR1 fetches invoices with `status: { not: InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE }` (comment claims 'Include PENDING, PARTIALLY_PAID, PAID'). GST liability arises on invoice issuance, not payment. Meanwhile generateGSTR3B (line 270) fetches invoices with NO status filter, and invoice.service.updateOverdueInvoices() (invoice.service.ts:747, exposed as POST /invoices/update-overdue for cron) bulk-flips every past-due PENDING/PARTIALLY_PAID invoice to OVERDUE.
allFindings.failureScenario: Invoice issued June 1, due June 15, unpaid. Cron marks it OVERDUE. GSTR-1 generated for June omits it entirely (b2b, b2cs, hsnSummary, totals) while GSTR-3B for the same period includes it → filed GSTR-1 under-reports outward tax and disagrees with GSTR-3B — the exact divergence that triggers GST department notices. Every invoice unpaid at filing time is silently dropped.
allFindings.fixSketch: Remove the status filter from the GSTR-1 invoice query (report on invoiceDate period regardless of payment status); add a shared 'reportable invoices' query used by both GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B so the two returns can never diverge.

allFindings.title: TDS create: Zod schema, service input, and Prisma model are three different contracts — POST /api/tds can never succeed
allFindings.evidence: createTDSSchema fields (vendorId, section, panNumber, tanNumber, challanNumber, challanDate) do NOT exist on tds_entries (schema.prisma:9498), while the model's REQUIRED columns deductorName, deducteeName, tdsSection, financialYear, quarter are absent from the schema, so validateBody (tds.routes.ts:17) strips them even if sent. tds.service.ts:33 then spreads the validated body straight into prisma.tds_entries.create({ ...data }). Also deductionDate is optional in Zod but `new Date(data.deductionDate)` runs unconditionally (service line 36) → Invalid Date.
allFindings.failureScenario: Any POST /api/tds: body passes Zod, then Prisma throws Unknown argument `section`/`vendorId` (or missing required deductorName/financialYear/quarter) → 500 on every request. The TDS-entry feature is dead via the API; the interface TDSCreateInput in the service documents the fields the schema refuses to deliver.
allFindings.fixSketch: Rewrite createTDSSchema/updateTDSSchema to mirror tds_entries columns (deductorName, deducteeName, tdsSection, tdsRate, grossAmount, tdsAmount, netAmount, certificateNo, deductionDate required, financialYear, quarter, remarks); add a refine that tdsAmount ≈ grossAmount*tdsRate/100 and netAmount = grossAmount − tdsAmount.

allFindings.title: TDSStatusEnum (Zod) vs TDSStatus (Prisma) enum drift + updateStatus schema strips certificateNo the controller reads
allFindings.evidence: Zod: TDSStatusEnum = ['PENDING','DEDUCTED','DEPOSITED','FILED','CANCELLED']. Prisma (schema.prisma:9492): enum TDSStatus { PENDING, CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED, VERIFIED }. Only PENDING overlaps. Additionally tds.controller.ts:39 destructures `{ status, certificateNo }` from req.body but updateTDSStatusSchema (line 66) only allows status/challanNumber/challanDate/remarks — certificateNo is silently stripped. tds.service.getSummary (tds.service.ts:117-119) counts statuses 'CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED'/'VERIFIED' that the API can never set.
allFindings.failureScenario: PUT /api/tds/:id/status with status='DEDUCTED' (a Zod-approved value) → Prisma enum rejection → 500. The two statuses that actually exist (CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED, VERIFIED) are rejected by Zod with a 400. certificateNo sent with a status update is silently dropped (never persisted). TDS summary certificate counts are permanently 0.
allFindings.fixSketch: Make TDSStatusEnum mirror the Prisma TDSStatus enum exactly (the enum-drift ratchet's positive fix) and add certificateNo to updateTDSStatusSchema.

allFindings.title: createInvoiceSchema/updateInvoiceSchema require z.string().datetime() but InvoiceForm sends YYYY-MM-DD — invoice create/update from the UI 400s
allFindings.evidence: dueDate: z.string().datetime(...).transform(...) (lines 23-26; invoiceDate line 17, and updateInvoiceSchema lines 81-91). Frontend InvoiceForm.tsx builds dueDate/invoiceDate from <Input type="date"> state initialized `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` (lines 42-43) and submits them raw (lines 198-218). z.string().datetime() rejects date-only strings. Only fromDate/toDate of invoice.schema.ts are grandfathered in scripts/hooks/datetime-schema-baseline.json — dueDate/invoiceDate are not.
allFindings.failureScenario: User fills the Create Invoice form and submits → validateBody returns 400 'Invalid request data' (details: dueDate 'Invalid date format') on every attempt; edit-invoice PUT fails identically. This is precisely the datetime-schema bug class the smart-check hook exists to block.
allFindings.fixSketch: Replace z.string().datetime().transform(...) with z.coerce.date() for invoiceDate/dueDate in both schemas (and fromDate/toDate in invoiceQuerySchema while there).

allFindings.title: Chart of Accounts update always returns 409 — controller reads accountCode that updateChartOfAccountSchema deliberately strips
allFindings.evidence: updateChartOfAccountSchema (chartOfAccounts.schema.ts:51, 'Note: accountCode is not updatable') omits accountCode; the route applies validateBody(updateChartOfAccountSchema) (chartOfAccounts.routes.ts:42). Controller updateAccount destructures accountCode from req.body (line 231) — always undefined post-validation — then `if (accountCode !== existingAccount.accountCode)` is always true, and `findFirst({ where: { accountCode: undefined, isActive: true } })` (lines 249-251): Prisma ignores undefined filters, so it matches the FIRST active account → ConflictError('Account code already exists') on every call.
allFindings.failureScenario: PUT /api/chart-of-accounts/:id with any valid body (e.g. rename an account) → 409 'Account code already exists' 100% of the time (any active account exists, including the one being edited). Editing the chart of accounts is impossible via the API.
allFindings.fixSketch: Drop accountCode from the controller's destructure and from the update data, and delete the code-uniqueness check (or gate it behind `accountCode !== undefined`).

allFindings.title: Approved credit notes never touch invoice balanceAmount — over-collection possible and receivables overstated
allFindings.evidence: approve() only flips status DRAFT→APPROVED (lines 331-334); nothing in creditNote.service writes invoices.paidAmount/balanceAmount (grep confirms the only balance writers are invoice.service create/update/recordPayment). recordPayment validates strictly against invoice.balanceAmount (invoice.service.ts:633-635), and dashboard receivables sum balanceAmount (dashboard.controller.ts:420,506) — both blind to credit notes. The stored balance aggregate is maintained for payments but not for the other document that reduces the receivable.
allFindings.failureScenario: Invoice ₹10,000; approved credit note ₹2,000 for returned goods. balanceAmount still reads ₹10,000, so a ₹10,000 customer payment passes validation and is recorded → ₹2,000 over-collected with no flag; dashboard receivables and invoice status ('PENDING' on a fully-settled invoice) are wrong for every credited invoice.
allFindings.fixSketch: On credit-note approval (and reversal on cancel of an approved note), atomically decrement invoices.balanceAmount and recompute status in the same transaction — or better, derive effective balance as totalAmount − sum(payments) − sum(approved credit notes) everywhere it is checked.

allFindings.title: Debit note interstate flag only computed when poId is present — standalone debit notes always charge CGST/SGST even for interstate suppliers
allFindings.evidence: `let isInterstate = false; if (data.poId) { const result = await gstService.isInterstatePO(data.supplierId); ... }` — the interstate lookup needs only supplierId (which is always required), yet it is guarded on the optional poId. poId is nullable in DebitNoteCreateInput and debit_notes.poId is String?.
allFindings.failureScenario: Create a debit note against an out-of-state supplier without linking a PO (e.g. quality claim on an old delivery): isInterstate stays false → GST split as CGST+SGST instead of IGST on the debit note document and in its stored cgst/sgst/igst columns → wrong tax head on a statutory document.
allFindings.fixSketch: Call gstService.isInterstatePO(data.supplierId) unconditionally (it already has billing-state fallbacks); poId should have no bearing on the interstate determination.

allFindings.title: updateInvoice mutates header money fields without recomputing GST columns, line items, or totals — header/items/GST-report divergence
allFindings.evidence: updateInvoice spreads the validated body (subtotal, taxAmount, totalAmount independently optional) straight into prisma update (lines 567-581). cgstAmount/sgstAmount/igstAmount and invoice_items are never recomputed; balance/status only recomputed when totalAmount is passed. The UI edit path (InvoiceForm.tsx:213-218) sends subtotal WITHOUT taxAmount/totalAmount. Also balanceAmount is computed from a pre-read paidAmount (line 570-571) outside any transaction/atomic op — the very read-compute-write pattern recordPayment (lines 642-695) was just fixed to avoid.
allFindings.failureScenario: (a) User edits an invoice and changes line amounts → PUT sends only subtotal → totalAmount, taxAmount, cgst/sgst/igst and invoice_items all keep old values → totalAmount ≠ subtotal + taxAmount and GSTR-1 (which reads header subtotal + cgst/sgst/igst) reports a taxable value with mismatched tax. (b) A payment recorded concurrently with an update that passes totalAmount → balanceAmount computed from the stale paidAmount clobbers the payment's decrement.
allFindings.fixSketch: Recompute taxAmount/totalAmount/cgst/sgst/igst server-side from subtotal (or from items) on any amount change instead of accepting them independently; wrap the update in a transaction and derive balanceAmount from the row read inside it.

allFindings.title: Header-level invoice creation trusts client taxAmount/totalAmount while storing independently computed CGST/SGST/IGST — internally inconsistent invoices
allFindings.evidence: `const taxAmount = data.taxAmount !== undefined ? data.taxAmount : gstCalc.totalTax; const totalAmount = data.totalAmount !== undefined ? data.totalAmount : data.subtotal + taxAmount;` (lines 409-410) — no check that client figures reconcile — while lines 428-434 always store gstCalc.cgst/sgst/igst computed from subtotal×taxRate.
allFindings.failureScenario: Client posts subtotal=1000, taxAmount=0 (or totalAmount=900): invoice persists taxAmount=0/totalAmount=900 but cgstAmount=25, sgstAmount=25 → taxAmount ≠ cgst+sgst+igst and totalAmount ≠ subtotal+taxAmount. GSTR-1 B2B entries (built from these header columns) report tax that was never charged; balanceAmount seeds from the inconsistent totalAmount.
allFindings.fixSketch: Ignore client-supplied taxAmount/totalAmount (schema comment already says they're auto-calculated) or reject with 400 when they deviate from the server-computed figures beyond a rounding epsilon.

allFindings.title: GSTR-3B input tax credit computed from PO header totals (including merely-SENT POs) instead of received goods/supplier invoices
allFindings.evidence: ITC sums purchase_orders.totalCgst/totalSgst/totalIgst where status in ['SENT','ACKNOWLEDGED','PARTIALLY_RECEIVED','RECEIVED'] by poDate (lines 282-301). ITC legally requires goods receipt + a supplier tax invoice; a SENT PO has neither, and a PARTIALLY_RECEIVED PO is credited at 100% of PO tax. netTaxPayable then clamps with Math.max(0, ...) (lines 312-318), silently discarding excess ITC instead of carrying it forward.
allFindings.failureScenario: Raise a ₹10L PO on June 28 (status SENT, nothing delivered): June GSTR-3B claims its full CGST/SGST as ITC → overstated credit / understated cash tax payable; when goods arrive in July the credit is double-counted by month. Conversely a month with ITC > output tax shows payable 0 and the excess vanishes from the report.
allFindings.fixSketch: Base ITC on GRN-received quantities/supplier invoices dated in the period (pro-rate PO tax by received value), and report negative net as carry-forward credit rather than clamping to 0.

allFindings.title: Document number generation: lexicographic max + 3-digit padding permanently wedges CN/DN creation after #999; invoice numbers race outside the transaction
allFindings.evidence: generateCreditNoteNumber orders by `creditNoteNumber: 'desc'` (string sort) with padStart(3). After CN-999 → CN-1000 is created, the next call still finds 'CN-999' as the lexicographic max ('CN-999' > 'CN-1000') → regenerates 'CN-1000' → @unique violation (schema.prisma:9379) → every subsequent create fails with P2002 forever. debitNote.service.ts:45-67 is identical; there the number is even generated on the GLOBAL prisma client before the $transaction (line 119) — and creditNote's generator also uses global prisma from inside the tx callback (line 38, called at line 79). invoice.service.generateInvoiceNumber (lines 167-193) does read-then-create outside the tx → concurrent creates mint the same INV-YYMM-#### and one 500s on the unique index.
allFindings.failureScenario: 999th credit note is created; from the 1000th onward every POST /api/credit-notes returns a P2002 500 with no self-healing. Separately, two users invoicing simultaneously at month start both get INV-2607-0001; one gets an unexplained 500.
allFindings.fixSketch: Derive next number numerically (e.g. parse max via raw query on CAST(substring)) or keep a counter row updated atomically inside the same transaction as the create; retry once on P2002.

allFindings.title: Duplicate-payment guard keys on (amount, 24h window) — blocks legitimate equal installments while the real natural key (referenceNumber) has no uniqueness
allFindings.evidence: recordPayment rejects any payment with the same invoiceId+amount within 24h (lines 650-657) regardless of referenceNumber/method, with the error suggesting 'use a different amount'. Meanwhile payments (schema.prisma:1177-1192) has no unique constraint on referenceNumber (or invoiceId+referenceNumber), so the same UTR/cheque number can be recorded twice on day 1 and day 3.
allFindings.failureScenario: Customer pays two genuine ₹5,000 UPI installments the same day (different UTRs) → second one is hard-rejected as a duplicate. Conversely the same cheque number keyed in again two days later is accepted → paidAmount double-incremented (invoice flips to PAID early).
allFindings.fixSketch: Add a partial unique index on payments(invoiceId, referenceNumber) WHERE referenceNumber IS NOT NULL; scope the time-window heuristic to payments lacking a reference (or same reference) instead of amount-only.

allFindings.title: All GST/invoice money math on raw JS floats with parseFloat(toFixed(2)) — decimal.js helpers in utils/currency.ts entirely unused by the financial services
allFindings.evidence: calculateLineItemGST: `parseFloat(((lineTotal * gstRate) / 100).toFixed(2))` (lines 246-266); calculateTotals' comment claims 'round only at the end (not per-item) to minimize rounding drift' but its inputs are the already-per-item-rounded cgstAmount/sgstAmount/igstAmount (lines 272-299) — the stated invariant is not what the code does. invoice.service accumulates subtotal/headerCgst/... as floats (lines 281-353); creditNote.service.ts:110-123 and debitNote.service.ts:104-118 repeat the same summation a third and fourth time. No financial service imports toCurrency/addCurrency/roundToCent from backend/src/utils/currency.ts (grep: currency.ts is imported nowhere in invoice/gst/creditNote/debitNote/tds services).
allFindings.failureScenario: 50-line invoice at 2.5% CGST: per-line toFixed(2) rounding then float summation yields header cgstAmount off by several paise vs tax computed on the aggregate; invoice taxAmount, credit-note reversal, and GSTR-1 totals each accumulate independently → paise-level mismatches between documents and returns that fail reconciliation (0.01 differences also interact with recordPayment's balance epsilon).
allFindings.fixSketch: Route line/tax/total arithmetic through utils/currency.ts (Decimal add, roundToCent) and centralize the item→header aggregation in gstService.calculateTotals for all four services, fixing it to genuinely round once at the header.

allFindings.title: Interstate determination computed three different ways from two different config sources, with error paths silently defaulting to intrastate
allFindings.evidence: createInvoice compares state UUIDs: `COMPANY_STATE_ID !== placeOfSupplyId` (env var, line 270); gstService.isInterstateSale/isInterstatePO compare stateCode strings against COMPANY_CONFIG.stateCode (gst.service.ts:315,373); legacy calculateGST compares caller-supplied IDs (line 463). isInterstatePO/isInterstateSale swallow all errors and return `{ isInterstate: false }` (lines 351-355, 378-384) — a DB hiccup silently converts an interstate supply to CGST/SGST.
allFindings.failureScenario: COMPANY_STATE_ID env var points at a different (or stale) indian_states row than COMPANY_CONFIG.stateCode: invoices classify interstate one way while debit notes/quotations using isInterstatePO classify the other → same counterparty gets IGST on one document and CGST/SGST on another. Any transient DB error during supplier-state lookup silently mislabels the supply intrastate rather than failing the request.
allFindings.fixSketch: Single authority: one gstService.isInterstate(placeOfSupplyStateId) backed by one config source (COMPANY_CONFIG), used by all paths; let lookup errors propagate instead of defaulting the tax classification.

allFindings.title: Credit-note GST recomputed from current rate tables instead of reversing the original invoice line's rate
allFindings.evidence: create() calls gstService.calculateLineItemGST({ hsnSacCode: item.hsnCode, unitPrice, ... }) for each CN item (lines 86-91) even when invoiceItemId is provided — the linked invoice_items row's stored gstRate/hsnCode (schema.prisma:852) is never consulted. getGSTRate falls back through material→HSN→tax_masters→5% (gst.service.ts:89-175).
allFindings.failureScenario: Invoice line: garment ₹3,000/pc, HSN 6204 → 18% charged. Credit note raised for a return but the operator omits hsnCode on the CN item → getGSTRate falls back to 5% → CN reverses ₹150/1000 instead of ₹180/1000 of tax; GSTR-1 CDNR nets out the wrong tax. Same drift whenever hsn_sac_masters rates change between invoice and return.
allFindings.fixSketch: When invoiceItemId is set, copy gstRate/hsnCode (and cgst/sgst/igst split) from the invoice item and compute the reversal at that rate; only fall back to fresh rate lookup for unlinked lines.

allFindings.title: Base-currency switch is non-atomic — unset of the old base and set of the new one are separate statements outside a transaction
allFindings.evidence: createCurrency: `updateMany({ where: { isBaseCurrency: true }, data: { isBaseCurrency: false } })` (lines 24-29) then a separate `create` (line 31); updateCurrency repeats the pattern (lines 127-142). No $transaction; no unique constraint guarantees exactly one base currency.
allFindings.failureScenario: POST /api/currencies with isBaseCurrency=true where the create then fails (e.g. race on currencyCode unique, or DB error): the old base currency is already unset → system left with zero base currency; any conversion logic reading 'the' base currency breaks. A concurrent pair of requests can also commit two base currencies.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap unset+create/update in one prisma.$transaction; optionally enforce with a partial unique index on currencies(isBaseCurrency) WHERE isBaseCurrency = true.

allFindings.title: Invoice PDF prints amounts with toLocaleString('en-IN', {minimumFractionDigits: 2}) and no maximumFractionDigits (known/baselined)
allFindings.evidence: Lines 348 and 357 format invoice.paidAmount/balanceAmount with `toLocaleString('en-IN', { minimumFractionDigits: 2 })`. This exact key is grandfathered in scripts/hooks/currency-format-baseline.json — a known, catalogued instance of the money-format bug class.
allFindings.failureScenario: A balanceAmount that is a non-terminating float (e.g. 563.79600000001 after float math upstream) renders as ₹563.796 on the customer-facing invoice PDF.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add maximumFractionDigits: 2 (the ratchet's prescribed fix) and remove the entry from the baseline when touched.

allFindings.title: Chart-of-accounts list ignores validated query contract: isActive/sortBy/sortOrder accepted by the schema but hardcoded in the controller; parentAccountId filter works only because validateQuery doesn't strip req.query
allFindings.evidence: chartOfAccountQuerySchema validates isActive/sortBy/sortOrder (schema lines 85-97) but getAllAccounts hardcodes `where = { isActive: true }` and `orderBy: { accountCode: 'asc' }` (lines 82, 108) and reads parentAccountId, which the schema doesn't declare — it survives only because validateQuery copies validated keys onto req.query without deleting unknown ones (validation.middleware.ts:55-60). Controller default limit '50' also disagrees with the schema default 10.
allFindings.failureScenario: GET /api/chart-of-accounts?isActive=false or ?sortBy=createdAt&sortOrder=desc validates 200 OK but returns active-only, accountCode-ascending data — inactive (soft-deleted) accounts are unreachable through the list endpoint, silently.
allFindings.fixSketch: Honor the validated isActive/sortBy/sortOrder in the where/orderBy, add parentAccountId to the query schema, and align the limit default.

allFindings.title: FG stock deduction on delivery-note creation is off-transaction, race-prone read-modify-write, and silently skipped
allFindings.evidence: Lines 311-361: prisma.delivery_notes.create is followed by a per-item loop that does findFirst({ where: { styleId, colorId: item.colorId || undefined, sizeId, quantity: { gte: item.quantity } } }) then update({ data: { quantity: fgStock.quantity - item.quantity } }). No $transaction, no { decrement }. If NO single finished_goods_stock row has >= item.quantity, the deduction is skipped entirely (comment at line 359: 'If no FG stock found, still allow dispatch'). If item.colorId is undefined, the colorId filter drops out and ANY color's stock row is deducted.
allFindings.failureScenario: (a) Two concurrent delivery notes for the same SKU both read quantity=100, both write 100-60=40 → one 60-pc deduction lost, FG stock overstated forever. (b) SKU spread across two rows of 50 each, dispatch 60 → gte:60 matches nothing → note created, zero deduction → stock overstated by 60 silently. (c) colorId omitted → wrong color's stock decremented. (d) Crash mid-loop → note exists with partial deductions.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap note creation + deductions in one prisma.$transaction; use quantity: { decrement } with an updateMany guard (quantity >= qty) per exact SKU, allocate across multiple rows, and fail (or explicitly flag) instead of silently skipping.

allFindings.title: Deleting a delivery note never restores the FG stock deducted at creation
allFindings.evidence: deleteDeliveryNote (lines 390-411) only checks status === 'PENDING' and calls prisma.delivery_notes.delete (items cascade via onDelete: Cascade, schema.prisma:627). FG stock was decremented in createDeliveryNote, but there is no compensating increment anywhere on delete.
allFindings.failureScenario: User creates a delivery note for 200 pcs (FG stock -200), realizes it is wrong, deletes it while still PENDING (allowed). The 200 pcs vanish from finished_goods_stock permanently even though nothing shipped — hand-maintained balance drifts exactly like stock_levels did in the template bug.
allFindings.fixSketch: In deleteDeliveryNote, inside one transaction, re-increment finished_goods_stock per item before deleting; or derive FG on-hand from receipts minus dispatched delivery-note items instead of storing it.

allFindings.title: Over-dispatch guard checks only order-level totals (per-SKU map built but never used per-SKU) and races check-then-insert
allFindings.evidence: Lines 288-305: dispatchedMap is built keyed by styleId-colorId-sizeId, but the guard only compares totalAlreadyDispatched + totalNewDispatch > totalOrdered (sums across ALL SKUs). No per-SKU comparison against order_items. The whole check is a plain read before the create with no transaction/lock.
allFindings.failureScenario: Order: 100 pcs size M + 100 pcs size L. Dispatch 200 pcs of size M → total (200) <= 200 → passes; customer receives double M and zero L. Separately, two users creating notes concurrently both read the same 'already dispatched' figure and both pass, exceeding the order cap.
allFindings.fixSketch: Compare the dispatchedMap per SKU key against per-order_item quantities, and run validation + create inside one serializable transaction (or enforce with a DB constraint / SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the order).

allFindings.title: SHIPPED production_tracking rows record the FULL delivery-note quantity once PER work order, inside an error-swallowing catch
allFindings.evidence: Lines 364-384: for every work_order of the order, production_tracking.create is called with quantityCompleted = items.reduce(... total of the whole delivery note ...). An order with N work orders gets N rows each carrying the full dispatched qty (N× inflation). The whole block is try/catch { logger.error(...) } — fire-and-forget, so failures silently lose tracking while the note still succeeds.
allFindings.failureScenario: Order with 3 work orders, delivery note of 500 pcs → three SHIPPED tracking rows of 500 each → any report summing production_tracking shows 1500 shipped for a 500-pc dispatch. Conversely, if the create throws, shipped tracking is silently absent.
allFindings.fixSketch: Attribute dispatched quantity to the correct work order (via order_items/WO linkage) or record one order-level event; include the write in the same transaction as the note instead of a swallowed catch.

allFindings.title: deliveryNumber/asnNumber generated by count() with no unique constraint — duplicates after any delete or concurrent create
allFindings.evidence: generateDeliveryNumber (lines 115-128) and generateASNNumber (130-142) use prisma.*.count({ startsWith: prefix }) + 1. schema.prisma: delivery_notes.deliveryNumber (line 641) has only @@index, no @unique; asn_applications.asnNumber (line 6462) likewise. Deletes of PENDING notes/ASNs are allowed, which shrinks the count.
allFindings.failureScenario: Same day: create DN-...-0001 and DN-...-0002, delete 0001, create again → count=1 → DN-...-0002 issued a second time and silently stored (no unique constraint to reject it). Two concurrent creates also both compute the same number. Duplicate dispatch document numbers = split ledger for a legal document.
allFindings.fixSketch: Add @unique on deliveryNumber/asnNumber and generate from a sequence table (or retry on P2002) instead of count().

allFindings.title: recordPODSchema uses z.string().datetime() but DispatchPODForm sends YYYY-MM-DD — recording POD from the UI always 400s
allFindings.evidence: recordPODSchema.deliveryDate/customerGrnDate are z.string().datetime() (lines 261, 271). frontend/src/pages/DispatchPODForm.tsx:28 initializes deliveryDate = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0] ('2026-07-21') from an <input type='date'> and sends it verbatim (line 109). validateBody uses schema.parse (validation.middleware.ts:28) → ZodError → 400 'Invalid request data'. All 14 dispatch datetime fields are grandfathered in scripts/hooks/datetime-schema-baseline.json (lines 3-16), so the hook won't force the fix.
allFindings.failureScenario: Every POD submission from DispatchPODForm returns 400; deliveries can never be marked DELIVERED through the UI. Same class breaks lrDate/expectedDeliveryDate on assign-transport, requestedShipDate on ASN create, and fromDate/toDate date-range filters if sent as plain dates.
allFindings.fixSketch: Replace z.string().datetime() with z.coerce.date() (per the project guardrail's positive fix) across dispatch.schema.ts and remove the entries from the datetime baseline.

allFindings.title: Zod marks fields optional that the controller/Prisma require — omitted fields produce Invalid Date / Prisma 500s instead of 400s
allFindings.evidence: recordPOD: new Date(deliveryDate) at line 625 with schema-optional deliveryDate → new Date(undefined) = Invalid Date; dispatch_pods.receivedBy and deliveryStatus are required in Prisma (schema.prisma:6595, 6599) but optional in recordPODSchema. createASN: plannedDispatchQty, cartonsPlanned, requestedShipDate all optional in createASNSchema (lines 159-161) but required in asn_applications (schema.prisma:6464-6466) and passed through new Date(requestedShipDate) at line 748. approveASN: new Date(appointmentDate) at line 815 with optional appointmentDate. deliveryNoteItemSchema marks styleId/colorId/sizeId optional (schema lines 34-40) while delivery_note_items requires all three (schema.prisma:619-621).
allFindings.failureScenario: POST /api/dispatch/asn with { orderId } only passes validation, then Prisma throws (missing required plannedDispatchQty / Invalid Date) → opaque 500. POST record-pod without deliveryDate or receivedBy → 500. API clients get server errors for what should be field-level 400s.
allFindings.fixSketch: Make controller-required fields required in the Zod schemas (deliveryDate, receivedBy, deliveryStatus; requestedShipDate, plannedDispatchQty, cartonsPlanned; appointmentDate; item styleId/colorId/sizeId) so validation, controller, and DB agree.

allFindings.title: Frontend dispatch service calls endpoints that don't exist and its create-request type contradicts the backend schema
allFindings.evidence: generateDocument POSTs /dispatch/delivery-notes/:id/generate-document (line 84) and getSummaryByOrder GETs /dispatch/summary/order/:orderId (line 171) — neither route exists in dispatch.routes.ts. CreateDeliveryNoteRequest (dispatch.types.ts:292-299) has cartonIds: string[] and no items, but createDeliveryNoteSchema requires items min(1) and the controller only reads items — cartonIds would be ignored (passthrough) and the request 400s for missing items.
allFindings.failureScenario: Any UI wired to 'Generate Challan/E-way Bill' or per-order summary gets a 404; any future delivery-note-creation form built against CreateDeliveryNoteRequest compiles cleanly but always receives 400 'At least one item is required', and cartons selected by the user are silently ignored.
allFindings.fixSketch: Delete or implement the two missing endpoints, and align CreateDeliveryNoteRequest with createDeliveryNoteSchema (items array with styleId/colorId/sizeId/quantity).

allFindings.title: Nothing ever sets carton_packings.status='DISPATCHED' — dispatchedPieces is always 0 and dispatched cartons remain 'available' forever
allFindings.evidence: getOrdersReadyForDispatch filters cartons by status === 'DISPATCHED' (line 1015) and getAvailableCartons lists status: 'PACKED' (line 946). Repo-wide grep shows no write of carton status to 'DISPATCHED' anywhere in backend/src; dispatchDeliveryNote (lines 511-572) only flips the note status and transport dispatchDate. dispatch_cartons link rows are likewise never created by any controller.
allFindings.failureScenario: After dispatching an order's goods, /dispatch/available-cartons still lists the same cartons (double-dispatch invitation) and /dispatch/orders-ready reports dispatchedPieces: 0 for every order indefinitely — the rollup is guarding/reporting a state no code produces.
allFindings.fixSketch: When a delivery note is dispatched, mark the linked cartons DISPATCHED (and create dispatch_cartons rows) in the same transaction; or derive availability from cartons minus dispatch_cartons joins.

allFindings.title: Order-delete guard checks delivery status 'SHIPPED', which is not a DeliveryStatus value — in-transit deliveries don't block deletion
allFindings.evidence: order.service.ts:681: const shippedDeliveries = order.delivery_notes.filter((dn) => ['SHIPPED', 'DELIVERED'].includes(dn.status)); Prisma enum DeliveryStatus is PENDING | IN_TRANSIT | DELIVERED (schema.prisma:8517-8521) — 'SHIPPED' can never match, so only DELIVERED blocks. The delete then hard-deletes delivery_note_items and delivery_notes (lines 725-731).
allFindings.failureScenario: An order whose delivery note is IN_TRANSIT (goods physically on a truck, FG stock already deducted) passes canDelete → the order, its delivery notes, and their items are permanently deleted mid-shipment; the dispatch record for goods in transit disappears and FG stock is never reconciled.
allFindings.fixSketch: Change the guard to ['IN_TRANSIT', 'DELIVERED'] (or status !== 'PENDING').

allFindings.title: recordPOD's two writes (create POD, set note DELIVERED) are non-atomic; a failure between them wedges the note
allFindings.evidence: Lines 622-645: prisma.dispatch_pods.create followed by a separate prisma.delivery_notes.update({ status: 'DELIVERED' }), no $transaction. dispatch_pods.deliveryNoteExtId is @unique (schema.prisma:6592). Same pattern in assignTransport (ext create + transport upsert + note update, lines 449-506) and dispatchDeliveryNote (status update + transport dispatchDate, lines 553-569).
allFindings.failureScenario: POD row is created, then the status update fails (connection drop). Note stays IN_TRANSIT with a POD attached; the user retries record-pod, which now throws P2002 on the unique deliveryNoteExtId → 500 every time; the delivery can never be marked DELIVERED without manual DB surgery.
allFindings.fixSketch: Wrap each workflow action's writes in one prisma.$transaction (and make recordPOD idempotent via upsert on deliveryNoteExtId).

allFindings.title: PARTIAL/REJECTED PODs still mark the note DELIVERED, and shortage/rejected quantities stay counted against the order's dispatch cap with no FG restore
allFindings.evidence: recordPOD sets status: 'DELIVERED' unconditionally (lines 642-645) regardless of deliveryStatus DELIVERED|PARTIAL|REJECTED and shortageQty. The over-dispatch guard in createDeliveryNote (lines 278-297) sums delivery_note_items.quantity for ALL notes of the order, with no adjustment for POD shortage/rejection; FG stock deducted at creation is never re-credited for rejected goods.
allFindings.failureScenario: 500 pcs dispatched, customer rejects the lot (deliveryStatus=REJECTED). Note shows DELIVERED; the 500 pcs still count as dispatched, so re-dispatching the replacement 500 is blocked by the 'would exceed order limit' guard; the returned goods also never re-enter finished_goods_stock.
allFindings.fixSketch: Derive the dispatched-against-order figure net of POD shortage/rejection (or add a REJECTED/PARTIAL note status), and post a compensating FG stock movement for returned/short goods.

allFindings.title: deliveryNoteExtendedIncludeOptions (transport/POD data) is defined but never used — API never returns the ext object the frontend types expect
allFindings.evidence: deliveryNoteExtendedIncludeOptions is declared at line 159 and referenced nowhere else (repo grep: single occurrence). getDeliveryNoteById (line 251) and all other reads use plain deliveryNoteIncludeOptions, so transformDeliveryNote's note.delivery_notes_ext branch (lines 58-72) always yields ext: null. frontend DeliveryNote.ext / DispatchPOD types (dispatch.types.ts:171, 248-266) model data that never arrives.
allFindings.failureScenario: After a POD is recorded (customer GRN number, sign-off, shortage), viewing the delivery note returns ext: null — the POD/customer-GRN details are stored but permanently invisible to every consumer of the API; any UI reading dn.ext?.pod renders empty.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use deliveryNoteExtendedIncludeOptions (including transport) in getDeliveryNoteById and the list endpoint where needed.

allFindings.title: POST /asn/:id/apply validates the body with approveASNSchema (wrong schema for the action)
allFindings.evidence: Line 96: router.post('/asn/:id/apply', validateParams(idParamSchema), validateBody(approveASNSchema), asyncHandler(applyASN)); applyASN reads no body fields. approveASNSchema is the approve-action schema (appointmentDate/approvedQty).
allFindings.failureScenario: Currently harmless (all approveASNSchema fields optional, controller ignores body), but any tightening of approveASNSchema for the approve flow silently changes apply's validation too — classic same-request-two-schemas drift.
allFindings.fixSketch: Validate apply with asnActionSchema (or an empty // no-body marker) instead of approveASNSchema.

allFindings.title: SampleTypeEnum in Zod has ZERO overlap with Prisma SampleType — sample creation and type-filtered listing are dead endpoints
allFindings.evidence: sample.schema.ts:14 `SampleTypeEnum = z.enum(['DEVELOPMENT','FIT','PRE_PRODUCTION','PRODUCTION','PHOTO_SHOOT'])` vs prisma/schema.prisma:8864 `enum SampleType { FIT_SAMPLE PHOTO_SAMPLE PRODUCTION_SAMPLE PP_SAMPLE SIZE_SET_SAMPLE SHIPMENT_SAMPLE }`. No value is in both sets. createSampleSchema (line 44) and sampleQuerySchema (line 220) both use it; sample.routes.ts:69/77 wire them via validateBody/validateQuery. The controller (sample.controller.ts:104-113) and frontend (sample.service.ts:245 sends `sampleType=FIT_SAMPLE`) use the Prisma values.
allFindings.failureScenario: Frontend POSTs /api/samples with sampleType='FIT_SAMPLE' → Zod 400 'Invalid request data'. If a client sent 'FIT' instead it passes Zod but prisma.samples.create throws invalid-enum → 500. GET /api/samples?sampleType=FIT_SAMPLE (used by SampleList and getApprovedFitSamples) → 400. Every create and every type-filtered list fails; the sample module is unusable through validation.
allFindings.fixSketch: Replace SampleTypeEnum values with the Prisma SampleType values (FIT_SAMPLE, PP_SAMPLE, SIZE_SET_SAMPLE, SHIPMENT_SAMPLE, PHOTO_SAMPLE, PRODUCTION_SAMPLE) and allow array form in sampleQuerySchema (controller supports arrays at sample.controller.ts:324-327).

allFindings.title: sendOutSchema/receiveSchema validate a completely different API shape than the controller and frontend use — embroidery send-out and receive endpoints always 400
allFindings.evidence: embroideryStock.schema.ts:36 sendOutSchema requires {processorId, items[]}; embroideryStock.schema.ts:52 receiveSchema requires {sendOutId, items[{sendOutItemId, receivedQuantity}]}. But embroidery-stock.controller.ts:21-40 reads {sourceFabricStockId, embroideryId, supplierId, quantitySent, sentWidth, sendDate, agreedRate} and :75-91 reads {sendOutId, quantityReceived, receivedWidth, actualReturnDate}. Routes wire the schemas: embroidery-stock.routes.ts:36-37 `validateBody(sendOutSchema)` / `validateBody(receiveSchema)`. Frontend types confirm the controller shape (embroidery.types.ts:212 EmbroiderySendOutRequest, :229 EmbroideryReceiveRequest).
allFindings.failureScenario: User submits the Embroidery Send-Out form → POST /api/embroidery-stock/send-out with sourceFabricStockId etc. → 400 'processorId Required, items Required'. Receive form → 400 'items Required'. Even a schema-conforming payload would be stripped to fields the controller ignores, hitting its manual ValidationError. The entire embroidery send-out/receive workflow is dead.
allFindings.fixSketch: Rewrite sendOutSchema/receiveSchema to mirror SendOutDTO/ReceiveDTO in embroidery-stock.service.ts (sourceFabricStockId, embroideryId cuid-tolerant, supplierId, quantitySent positive, sentWidth, sendDate coerce.date, agreedRate; sendOutId, quantityReceived positive, receivedWidth, actualReturnDate, etc.).

allFindings.title: SampleStatusEnum drifts from Prisma SampleStatus — valid workflow statuses 400, Zod-accepted statuses 500 at the DB
allFindings.evidence: sample.schema.ts:16 allows PENDING, RECEIVED, REVISION_REQUIRED (not in Prisma) and omits REQUESTED, SUBMITTED, FEEDBACK_PENDING, REVISION_NEEDED, APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS (prisma/schema.prisma:8852 SampleStatus). Used by updateSampleSchema:106, updateSampleStatusSchema:126, sampleQuerySchema:221. recordFeedbackSchema:194 additionally allows 'REVISION_REQUIRED' which is not a Prisma value, while the controller (sample.controller.ts:929) checks 'REVISION_NEEDED'. Controller's own status logic (sample.controller.ts:637, 643) uses APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS/SUBMITTED which Zod rejects.
allFindings.failureScenario: PATCH /api/samples/:id/status with status='APPROVED_WITH_COMMENTS' (a real buyer outcome) → 400. POST /:id/feedback with status='REVISION_REQUIRED' passes Zod, then prisma.samples.update throws invalid enum → 500 and revisionRequired flag logic is bypassed. GET /api/samples?status=FEEDBACK_PENDING → 400.
allFindings.fixSketch: Align SampleStatusEnum (and recordFeedbackSchema's status subset) with the Prisma SampleStatus enum values exactly.

allFindings.title: embroidery_master uses cuid IDs but routes validate params as UUID — GET/PUT/DELETE /api/embroidery/:id and /by-embroidery/:embroideryId reject every real record
allFindings.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:2138 `embroidery_master id @default(cuid())`. embroidery.routes.ts:49/56/63 use validateParams(idParamSchema) where common.schema.ts:15 is `z.string().uuid()`. embroidery-stock.routes.ts:52 uses embroideryIdParamSchema (common.schema.ts:52, also uuid-only). embroideryStock.schema.ts:22 even documents 'embroideryId accepts CUID (embroidery_master uses @default(cuid()))' — but the param schemas were never fixed. Frontend calls `/embroidery/${id}` with the cuid (embroidery.service.ts:46, 63, 71).
allFindings.failureScenario: User opens an embroidery design detail page or clicks Edit/Delete: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/embroidery/c<cuid> → validateParams 400 'Invalid ID' before the controller runs. Same for GET /api/embroidery-stock/by-embroidery/:embroideryId. Detail, update, delete and stock-by-design views all fail for every design created with the cuid default.
allFindings.fixSketch: Use a cuid-or-uuid param schema (reuse the isValidIdFormat refinement from embroideryStock.schema.ts) for embroidery :id and :embroideryId params.

allFindings.title: Partial embroidery receipts overwrite quantityReceived instead of accumulating, with no over-receipt guard — send-out ledger corrupts and stock inflates
allFindings.evidence: receive() sets `quantityReceived: data.quantityReceived` (line 315) — plain overwrite of the stored aggregate — then computes status from only the latest batch: `totalReceived = data.quantityReceived + (data.quantityDamaged||0)` vs quantitySent (lines 308-310). The status guard (line 239) blocks only RECEIVED/CANCELLED, so PARTIALLY_RECEIVED can be received again indefinitely; each call creates a new fabric_stock lot (line 254) and increments stock_levels (line 305), and resultFabricStockId (line 324) is overwritten to the newest lot. No check that cumulative receipts ≤ quantitySent.
allFindings.failureScenario: Send 100m; receive 60m → PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, quantityReceived=60. Receive remaining 40m → quantityReceived overwritten to 40, totalReceived=40 < 100 → status stays PARTIALLY_RECEIVED forever, record claims only 40m ever returned while 100m of stock exists. A user 'correcting' a receipt by re-submitting doubles fabric_stock and stock_levels silently; receiving 500m against a 100m send-out is accepted.
allFindings.fixSketch: Accumulate: quantityReceived: { increment: qty } (same for quantityDamaged), compute status from the accumulated total, and reject receipts that would exceed quantitySent. Consider a child receipts table since multiple result lots are created.

allFindings.title: Measurement schemas validate fields the controller never reads and strip the fields it does read — both measurement endpoints are dead
allFindings.evidence: updateMeasurementsSchema:136 requires items {measurementPointId (uuid), targetValue, tolerance}, but the controller (sample.controller.ts:731-739) maps m.sizeId, m.measurementPoint, m.specValue, m.actualValue — all stripped by the non-passthrough z.object. recordActualMeasurementsSchema:150 requires {measurementPointId, actualValue} while the controller (sample.controller.ts:779-786) reads m.id for findUnique/update. validateBody replaces req.body with the parsed result (validation.middleware.ts:28).
allFindings.failureScenario: PUT /api/samples/:id/measurements with the controller/DB shape ({measurementPoint, specValue}) → 400 'measurementPointId Required'. With the schema shape → measurementPoint/specValue stripped → createMany receives undefined required columns → Prisma error → 500 (transaction rolls back, so at least no data loss). PATCH /:id/measurements/actual: m.id is stripped → prisma findUnique({where:{id: undefined}}) throws → 500 — and because the loop (lines 779-794) is not in a transaction, a mid-loop failure leaves some measurements PASS/FAIL-stamped and others untouched (F4).
